Here are some more examples of conditional sentences with [إِذَا]{.ar}:

(@ex001211) [إِذَا صَلَحَتْ صَلَحَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ وَإِذَا فَسَدَتْ فَسَدَ الْجَسَدُ كُلُّهُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :52](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:52)]{.citex}  
    [When it is upright, the whole body is upright. And when it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt.]{.trans}  

(@ex001212) [كَانَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا سَجَدَ جَافَى حَتَّى يُرَى بَيَاضُ إِبْطَيْهِ]{.ar}
    [[[مسند أحمد]{.ar} :14138](https://hadithunlocked.com/ahmad:14138)]{.citex}  
    [When the Messenger of Allāh would prostrate, he would put his upper arms apart from his sides until the whiteness of his underarms could be seen.]{.trans}  

(@ex001213) [كَانَ إِذَا خَرَجَ أَقْرَعَ بَيْنَ نِسَائِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :5211](https://hadithunlocked.com/bukhari:5211)]{.citex}  
    [When he would go out (on a journey), he would draw lots among his wives.]{.trans}  

(@ex001214) [إِذَا دَخَلَ أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ الْجَنَّةَ، نُودُوا\ ...]{.ar}
    [[[مسند أحمد]{.ar} :18935](https://hadithunlocked.com/ahmad:18935)]{.citex}  
    [When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, it will be called out to them\ ...]{.trans}  

### [#muDArie]{.trn2} verbs in the [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentence

We learned
in @sec-jsh_arch_in above,
that the conditional-device [إِنْ]{.ar}
governs the condition-verb and the condition-response-verb in the ø-case.

The conditional-device [إِذَا]{.ar}, however,
does not govern either the condition-verb or condition-response-verb,
as we saw in @fig-idha_hmarra_lbusru_ataytuka above.
So [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} is not usually used in [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentences.
The most common form for
[إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentences,
as we saw in example (@ex001210) above,
is
[إِذَا قَتَلَ قَتَلَ]{.ar}.

Having said that,
we do often find
the _u-case_ [muDArie]{.trn2} verb
[يَقْتُلُ]{.ar}
as either or as both
the condition-verb
and the condition-response-verb.^[[[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/79](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1184#p1)]
Here are some examples:

<!--
(@ex001215) [إذا زالت الشمس **آتيك**]{.ar}
    [[[الإيضاح في علوم البلاغة للقزويني]{.ar} 2/117](https://shamela.ws/book/7380/324)]{.citex}  
    [When the sun declines, I will come to you.]{.trans}
-->

(@ex001216) [إِذَا **تُتۡلَىٰ** عَلَیۡهِمۡ ءَایَـٰتُ ٱلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ خَرُّوا۟ سُجَّدࣰا وَبُكِیࣰّا]{.quran}
    [[[سورة مريم]{.ar} 19:58](https://quran.com/19/58) cited by Reckendorf, _Die syntaktischen Verhältnisse des Arabischen_ 648]{.citex}  
    [When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration and weeping.]{.trans}

(@ex001217) [إِذَا **تَكُونُ** كَرِيهَةٌ **أُدْعَى** لَهَا]{.ar}
    [cited by Reckendorf, _Die syntaktischen Verhältnisse des Arabischen_ 647]{.citex}  
    [When there is an inconvenience, I am called to it.]{.trans}  

(@ex001218) [إِنّ الكريم إذا **يُحَرَّبُ يَغضَبُ**]{.ar}
    [cited by Reckendorf, _Die syntaktischen Verhältnisse des Arabischen_ 647]{.citex}  
    [The noble person -- when he is provoked, he becomes angry.]{.trans}  

(@ex001219) [وإذا **تَضْحَكُ تُبْدي** حَبباً]{.ar}
    [cited by Reckendorf, _Die syntaktischen Verhältnisse des Arabischen_ 647--648]{.citex}  
    [When she laughs, she shows musky bubbles.]{.trans}  

Very rarely, we also find [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} used in [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentences.
For example:

(@ex001220) [إِذَا أَخَذْتُمَا مَضَاجِعَكُمَا **تُكَبِّرَا** أَرْبَعًا وَثَلاَثِينَ **وَتُسَبِّحَا** ثَلاَثًا وَثَلاَثِينَ **وَتَحْمَدَا** ثَلاَثَةً وَثَلاَثِينَ فَهْوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمَا مِنْ خَادِمٍ]{.ar}  
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3705](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3705) cited by [[شواهد التوضيح لابن مالك]{.ar} 71](https://shamela.ws/book/98123/68#p1)]{.citex}  
    [When you go to bed, you magnify thirty-four times, and glorify thirty-three times, and praise thirty-three times.]{.trans}  

(@ex001221) [إِذَا **تُصِبْكَ** خَصَاصَةٌ  فَتَجَمَّلِ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/18](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1710); Wright 2/12B]{.citex}  
    [When poverty befalls you then bear it patiently.]{.trans}  
    ([تَجَمَّلِ]{.ar} in rhyme for [تَجَمَّلْ]{.ar}.)  

### Negation in the [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentence

When the negating the condition-verb
or the condition-response-verb
in [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentences,
the form
[لَمْ يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}
is used.

The form
[لَا يَقْتُلُ]{.ar}
can also be used to negate
the condition-response-verb.

Here are some examples:

(@ex001222) [إِنَّ مِمَّا أَدْرَكَ النَّاسُ مِنْ كَلاَمِ النُّبُوَّةِ الأُولَى إِذَا **لَمْ تَسْتَحِي** فَاصْنَعْ مَا شِئْتَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6120](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6120)]{.citex}  
    [One of the sayings of the early prophets which the people have got is: If you don't feel ashamed, then do whatever you like.]{.trans}  

(@ex001223) [إِذَا **لَمْ يَجِدِ** الْمَاءَ **لاَ يُصَلِّي**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :345](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:345) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 28]{.citex}  
    [If he doesn't find water, he doesn't pray?]{.trans}  

(@ex001224) [أَلَيْسَ إِذَا حَاضَتْ **لَمْ تُصَلِّ وَلَمْ تَصُمْ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :304](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:304)]{.citex}  
    [Is it not the case [that] when she mensurates, she does not pray, and she does not fast?]{.trans}  

### The inverted conditional sentence with [إِذَا]{.ar}

Let's go back to example (@ex001208) above:

(@ex001225) [آتِيكَ إِذَا احْمَرَّ الْبُسْرُ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/60](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/913#p1)]{.citex}  
    [I will come to you when the unripe dates redden.]{.trans}

Technically, this is not a conditional sentence.
Nor does it technically contain a conditional sentence.
This is
because a conditional sentence,
according to our definition,
requires that the condition-response follow the condition in sentence word order.
But there is no condition-response,
whether surface or [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed,
after
[إِذَا احْمَرَّ الْبُسْرُ]{.ar}.
(See the government of this sentence in @fig-aatika_idha_hmarra_lbusr.)

Having said that,
there is no problem if we refer to such a sentence,
loosely speaking and for convenience,
as an inverted conditional sentence.
if contains the _meaning_ of a condition.
Here are some more examples:

(@ex001226) [وَتَوَفَّنِي إِذَا كَانَتِ الْوَفَاةُ خَيْرًا لِي]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :5671](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5671)]{.citex}  
    [And take my soul if death is better for me.]{.trans}

(@ex001227) [فَأَقْبَلَ رَجُلٌ غَائِرُ الْعَيْنَيْنِ مُشْرِفُ الْوَجْنَتَيْنِ نَاتِئُ الْجَبِينِ كَثُّ اللِّحْيَةِ مَحْلُوقٌ فَقَالَ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ فَقَالَ  **مَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ إِذَا عَصَيْتُ** أَيَأْمَنُنِي اللَّهُ عَلَى أَهْلِ الأَرْضِ فَلاَ تَأْمَنُونِي]{.ar}^[It is not clear to us why [يُطِع]{.ar} is in the ø-case from this source. Peled's source [الجامع الصحيح]{.ar}, ed.\ L.\ Krehl, Leiden: Brill, 1864, II, 337 l:9 has [يُطِيعُ]{.ar} in the u-case.]  
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3344](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3344) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 142]{.citex}  
    [Then a man with sunken eyes, prominent checks, a raised forehead, a thick beard and a shaven head, came in front [of the Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng}] and said, "Be afraid of Allāh, O [#muHammad]{.trn2}!" The Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} said, "**Who would obey Allah if I disobeyed [Him]?** (Is it fair that) Allāh has trusted all the people of the earth to me while you do not trust me?"]{.trans}  

(@ex001228) [لِلْمُسْلِمِ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِ سِتٌّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ يُسَلِّمُ عَلَيْهِ إِذَا لَقِيَهُ وَيُجِيبُهُ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيُشَمِّتُهُ إِذَا عَطَسَ وَيَعُودُهُ إِذَا مَرِضَ وَيَتْبَعُ جَنَازَتَهُ إِذَا مَاتَ وَيُحِبُّ لَهُ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[جامع الترمذي]{.ar} :2736](https://hadithunlocked.com/tirmidhi:2736)]{.citex}  
    [There are six courtesies due to a Muslim from another Muslim: he gives the greeting of peace when he sees him, he responds to him when he invites him, he [says [يرحمك الله]{.ar}] when he sneezes, he visits him when he is ill, he follows his funeral when he dies, and he loves for him what he loves for himself.]{.trans}  

### Certainty of the event indicated by [إِذَا]{.ar}

[إِذَا]{.ar} is typically used when the condition is certain to occur.
The English expression,
[It's not a matter of "if" but "when"]{.trans},
also indicates the fundamental difference between [if]{.trans} and [when]{.trans} conditional sentences.
So, for example,
if you say:

(@ex001229) [إن تكرمني أكرمك]{.ar}
    [[[الإيضاح في علوم البلاغة للقزويني]{.ar} 2/117](https://shamela.ws/book/7380/324)]{.citex}  
    [If you will honor me, I will honor you.]{.trans}  

then you are not certain if the other person would honor you or not.
But if you say:

(@ex001230) [إذا زالت الشمس **آتيك**]{.ar}
    [[[الإيضاح في علوم البلاغة للقزويني]{.ar} 2/117](https://shamela.ws/book/7380/324)]{.citex}  
    [When the sun declines, I will come to you.]{.trans}

then you are certain that the condition
[إذا زالت الشمس]{.ar}
will, at some point, be valid.^[[[الإيضاح في علوم البلاغة للقزويني]{.ar} 2/117](https://shamela.ws/book/7380/324)]

Having said that,
[إِذَا]{.ar} may not always indicate the certainness of the event in the condition.
For example:

(@ex001231) [فَأَقْبَلَ رَجُلٌ غَائِرُ الْعَيْنَيْنِ مُشْرِفُ الْوَجْنَتَيْنِ نَاتِئُ الْجَبِينِ كَثُّ اللِّحْيَةِ مَحْلُوقٌ فَقَالَ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ فَقَالَ  **مَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ إِذَا عَصَيْتُ** أَيَأْمَنُنِي اللَّهُ عَلَى أَهْلِ الأَرْضِ فَلاَ تَأْمَنُونِي]{.ar}  
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3344](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3344)]{.citex}  
    [Then a man with sunken eyes, prominent checks, a raised forehead, a thick beard and a shaven head, came in front [of the Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng}] and said, "Be afraid of Allāh, O [#muHammad]{.trn2}!" The Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} said, "Who would obey Allah **if** I disobeyed [Him]? (Is it fair that) Allāh has trusted all the people of the earth to me while you do not trust me?"]{.trans}  

Even though [إِذَا]{.ar} is used in the above [HadIv]{.trn2}, it does not indicate a certain event.
Far from it.
In fact, there is no question that the Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} would never disobey Allāh.

In such cases, [إِذَا]{.ar} can retain its temporal signification,
but the event in the condition would not be considered certain.

<!--
### [إِذَا]{.ar} indicating a past time

(@ex001232) [وَإِذَا رَأَوۡا۟ تِجَـٰرَةً أَوۡ لَهۡوًا ٱنفَضُّوۤا۟ إِلَیۡهَا وَتَرَكُوكَ قَاۤىِٕمࣰاۚ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الجمعة]{.ar} 62:11](https://quran.com/62/11)]{.citex}  
    [But [on one occasion] when they saw a transaction or a diversion, [O Muḥammad], they rushed to it and left you standing.]{.trans}  
-->

<!--
### [إِذَا]{.ar} as a ø-case-izing conditional-device

By poetic license, [إِذَا]{.ar} may behave like [إِنْ]{.ar},
in that it will govern the condition-verb and/or the condition-response-verb in the ø-case.
For example:

(@ex001233) [وَإِذَا **تُصِبْكَ** خَصَاصَةٌ **فَتَجَمَّلِ**]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/18](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1710)]{.citex}  
    [And when poverty strikes you, then constrain yourself to be patient.]{.trans}
-->

### [إِذَا مَا]{.ar}

[مَا]{.ar} may optionaly be suffixed to [إِذَا]{.ar}.
This [مَا]{.ar} is redundant and it can
(but does not necessarily have to)
imply a vagueness in meaning.^[[[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/95](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1200) citing [الكليات للكفوي]{.ar}]
For example:

(@ex001234) [آتيك إذا ما طلعت الشمس]{.ar}  
    [composed from [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/95](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1200) citing [الكليات للكفوي]{.ar}]{.citex}  
    [I will come to you, [one of the days] when the sun will rise.]{.trans}

Or it can imply an extra emphasis.
For example:

(@ex001235) [حَتَّىٰۤ إِذَا مَا جَاۤءُوهَا شَهِدَ عَلَیۡهِمۡ سَمۡعُهُمۡ وَأَبۡصَـٰرُهُمۡ وَجُلُودُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ یَعۡمَلُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة فصلت]{.ar} 41:20](https://quran.com/41/20) cited by [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/96ff](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1201)]{.citex}  
    [Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will testify against them of what they used to do.]{.trans}  

<!--
(@ex001236) [وَإِذَا مَا غَضِبُوا۟ هُمۡ یَغۡفِرُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الشورى]{.ar} 42:37](https://quran.com/42/37)]{.citex}  
-->

[إِذَا مَا]{.ar} is more common than [إِذَا]{.ar}
when the condition-verb and/or the condition-response-verb
are [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} instead of [قَتَلَ]{.ar}
(see examples (@ex001220) and (@ex001221) above).^[[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 4/272](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/1636)]
Examples:

(@ex001237) [إذا ما **تأتني أُحسِنْ** إليك]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 4/272](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/1636)]{.citex}  
    [Whenever you come to me, I will do good to you.]{.trans}  

(@ex001238) [وَكَانَ إِذَا مَا يَسْلُلِ السَّيْفَ يَضْرِبِ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/19](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1711)]{.citex}  
    [And he would, when he drew his sword, strike.]{.trans}


<!--
## The nuances of the [mADI]{.trn2} and ø-case [muDArie]{.trn2} verbs in the conditional sentence
-->

### [كَانَ]{.ar} before the [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentence

TODO:

Fischer 236

(@ex001239) [كان إذا اشتكيت رحمني]{.ar}

(@ex001240) [كنت إذل قوم غزوني غزوتهم]{.ar}

(@ex001241) [كانت العجوز إذا كلمها تسكت عنه]{.ar}

## Other conditional-devices {#sec-jsh_other_adats}

In addition to [إِنْ]{.ar} and [إِذَا]{.ar},
there are other conditional-devices as well.
The main other conditional-device is [لَوْ]{.ar} but we will treate it separately in @sec-jsh_law below.
Besides [لَوْ]{.ar}, the additional conditional-devices can be split into two categories:

 i. ø-case-izing conditional-devices like [إِنْ]{.ar}: these govern a condition-verb and a condition-response-verb in the ø-case.
ii. Non-ø-case-izing conditional-devices: these _don't_ govern the condition-verb and the condition-response-verb in the ø-case.

We will discuss both categories below:

### ø-case-izing conditional-devices

Most of the nouns that constitute
the question-devices (like 
[مَنْ]{.ar} [who]{.trans},
[مَا]{.ar} [what]{.trans},
[أَيْنَ]{.ar} [where]{.trans},
etc.)
double as
ø-case-izing conditional-devices.^[[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 148](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n149/mode/2up)]

In addition to 
the question-devices,
some other adverbs of time/place also
double as
ø-case-izing conditional-devices,
like 
[حَيْثُ]{.ar} [where]{.trans},
and [إِذْ]{.ar} [when]{.trans}.

#### Suffixing [مَا]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

When the
above nouns
are re-used as
conditional-devices,
an extra [مَا]{.ar} is often suffixed to many of them,
signifying and emphasizing an [-ever]{.trans} meaning.
For example:
[أَيْنَمَا]{.ar} [wherever]{.trans}.
The suffixing of [مَا]{.ar} to these conditional-devices
falls under three categories^[[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 174ff](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n175/mode/2up)]:

  i. Those for whom suffixing a [مَا]{.ar} is obligatory:
     + [إِذْمَا]{.ar}   [if]{.trans}. (By the way, according to some grammarians, once [مَا]{.ar} is suffixed to [إِذْ]{.ar} to make it an conditional-device, it ceases to be a noun and becomes a particle.^[[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 162](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n163/mode/2up)])
     + [حَيْثُمَا]{.ar}   [wherever]{.trans}

 ii. Those for whom suffixing a [مَا]{.ar} is optional.
     These are the majority of the question-devices that are reused as conditional-devices.
     For example:

     + [مَا]{.ar}/[مَهْمَا]{.ar}        [what(ever)]{.trans}. (One theory is that the origin of [مَهْمَا]{.ar} is [مَامَا]{.ar}.^[[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 175](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n176)])
     + [أَيْنَ]{.ar}/[أَيْنَمَا]{.ar}       [where(ever)]{.trans}
     + [مَتَى]{.ar}/[مَتَى مَا]{.ar}      [when(ever)]{.trans}
     + [أَيَّانَ]{.ar}/[أَيَّانَ مَا]{.ar}    [when(ever)]{.trans}
     + [أَيّ]{.ar}/[أَيُّمَا]{.ar}        [which(ever)]{.trans}
     + [كَيْفَ]{.ar}/[كَيْفَمَا]{.ar}   [however]{.trans}. ([كَيْفَ]{.ar}/[كَيْفَمَا]{.ar} as  conditional-devices are disputed; some grammarians did not allow them.^[[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 177](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n177/mode/2up); [[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/18](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1710))]

     Note that when [مَا]{.ar} is suffixed, it is joined, in writing, to some of the question-devices and not to others.

iii. Those that are not suffixed with a [مَا]{.ar}, according to the standard view. But some grammarians did allow them to be suffixed with [مَا]{.ar}.^[[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/18](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1710); [[شرح الأشموني على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 582](https://archive.org/details/ar113lang19/page/n581/mode/2up)]:

     + [مَنْ]{.ar} [who(ever)]{.trans}
     + [أَنَّى]{.ar} [whence]{.trans} (can mean [from where]{.trans}, [how]{.trans}, [when]{.trans}^[[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)])

<!--
     So, for example, [مَنْ]{.ar}, as an conditional-device can mean [whoever]{.trans} without being suffixed with [مَا]{.ar}.
-->

<!--

Besides [إِنْ]{.ar} and [إِذَا]{.ar},
there are other conditional-devices.
Some of them function like [إِنْ]{.ar},
in that they
ø-case-ize the condition-verb and the condition-response-verb.
And others do not
ø-case-ize the condition-verb and the condition-response-verb,
like [إِذَا]{.ar}.
We will discuss each of these separately below.

### ø-case-izing conditional-devices

[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/459ff

Many of the question nouns double as conditional-devices.
They will be
ø-case-izing conditional-devices.
Often they may include an attached [مَا]{.ar} after them,
emphasizing the [-ever]{.trans} meaning.
These include^[[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/13](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1705); [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 459--462]:

+ [مَنْ]{.ar}        [who(ever)]{.trans}
+ [مَا]{.ar}/[مَهْمَا]{.ar}        [what(ever)]{.trans}
+ [أَيْنَ]{.ar}/[أَيْنَمَا]{.ar}       [where(ever)]{.trans}
+ [حَيْثُمَا]{.ar}  [wherever]{.trans}
+ [مَتَى]{.ar}      [when(ever)]{.trans}
+ [أَيَّانَ]{.ar}    [when(ever)]{.trans}
+ [أَنَّى]{.ar}      [whence]{.trans} (can mean [from where]{.trans}, [how]{.trans}, [when]{.trans})^[[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]
+ [كَيْفَمَا]{.ar}   [however]{.trans}
+ [أَيّ]{.ar}/[أَيُّمَا]{.ar}        [which(ever)]{.trans}
-->

#### Conditional sentences with the ø-case-izing the conditional-devices {.unnumbered}

Like [إِنْ]{.ar}, these conditional-devices will govern
a condition-verb and a condition-response-verb in the ø-case.
Also, like [إِنْ]{.ar},
[mADI]{.trn2} verbs can be used instead of the ø-case [muDArie]{.trn2} verbs.

The analysis of these
conditional-devices
governing
the condition-verb and condition-response-verb in the ø-case,
while themselves oftentimes being governees,
becomes complex, and
has been the subject of much discussion by the grammarians.^[See for example: [[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 165ff](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n166); [[همع الهوامع للسيوطي]{.ar} 2/566](https://shamela.ws/book/6975/1138); [[مغني اللبيب لابن هشام]{.ar} 5/434](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/55330/read?part=5&page=2486&index=413839%2F413842)]
Here, we treat the subject summarily:

The conditional-devices
[مَنْ]{.ar},
[مَا]{.ar},
and
[مَهْمَا]{.ar},
are,
by default,
in the u-case as the subject of the sentence.
Examples:

(@ex001282) [مَنْ يُكْرِمْنِي أُكْرِمْهُ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/15](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1707)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever honors me, I will honor him.]{.trans}  

<!--
(@ex001283) [من يضْرب زيدا أضربه]{.ar}
    [[[همع الهوامع للسيوطي]{.ar} 2/566](https://shamela.ws/book/6975/1138)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever beats Zayd, I will beat him.]{.trans}  
-->

(@ex001284) [مَن یَعۡمَلۡ سُوۤءࣰا یُجۡزَ بِهِۦ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة النساء]{.ar} 4:123](https://quran.com/4/123) cited by [[شرح ابن عقيل على الألفية]{.ar} 4/27](https://shamela.ws/book/9904/1034)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever does a wrong will be recompensed for it]{.trans}  

(@ex001285) [مَنِ اتَّبَعَ عَوْرَاتِهِمْ يَتَّبِعِ اللَّهُ عَوْرَتَهُ]{.ar}
    [[[سنن أبي داود]{.ar} :4880](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4880)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever trails [them for] their faults, Allāh will trail [him for] his fault.]{.trans}  

(@ex001162) [مَنْ يَقُمْ لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :35](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:35)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever stands [in prayer] on the Night of Decree, in faith, and hoping for reward, then his previous sins will be forgiven.]{.trans}  
    (This is a rare example of [مَنْ يَقْتُلْ قَتَلَ]{.ar}.)  

(@ex001286) [مَا يُعْجِبْكَ يُعْجِبْنِي]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/15](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1707)]{.citex}  
    [Whatever pleases you, it will please me.]{.trans}  

(@ex001287) [وَمَا تَفۡعَلُوا۟ مِنۡ خَیۡرࣲ یَعۡلَمۡهُ ٱللَّهُۗ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة البقرة]{.ar} 2:197](https://quran.com/2/197) cited by [[شرح ابن عقيل على الألفية]{.ar} 4/27](https://shamela.ws/book/9904/1034)]{.citex}  
    [And whatever good you do - Allāh knows it.]{.trans}

(@ex001288) [مَهْمَا حَصَلَ كَفَى]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/15](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1707)]{.citex}  
    [Whatever is achieved, it is sufficient.]{.trans}  

(@ex001289) [أَغَرَّكِ مِنِّي أَنَّ حُبَّكِ قَاتِلِى وَأَنَّكِ **مَهْمَا تَأْمُرِي الْقَلْبَ يَفْعَلْ**]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 4/267](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/1631)]{.citex}  
    [That your love is killing me has emboldened you against me. And that you: **whatever you order the heart, it will do [it]**.]{.trans}

If they refer to the direct doee of the condition-verb,
then they are analyzed in the a-case as a direct doee.

(@ex001290) [مَنْ تَضْرِبْ أَضْرِبْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/15](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1707)]{.citex}  
    [Whomever you beat, I will beat.]{.trans}  

(@ex001291) [مَا تَفْعَلْ أَفْعَلْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/15](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1707)]{.citex}  
    [Whatever you do, I will do.]{.trans}  

(@ex001292) [مَهْمَا تَفْعَلْ أَفْعَلْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/15](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1707)]{.citex}  
    [Whatever you do, I will do.]{.trans}  

(@ex001293) [آتِي مَنْ أَتَانِي]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/70](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/923)]{.citex}  
    [I will come to who will come to me.]{.trans}  
    (This is an inverted conditional sentence with a deleted condition-response. See @sec-jsh_inverted_in above and also example (@ex001324) below.)

In such cases, the condition-core and/or the condition-response-core
may include a pronoun that refers back to the conditional-device.
Examples:

(@ex001294) [من تضرب أضربه]{.ar}
    [[[همع الهوامع للسيوطي]{.ar} 2/566](https://shamela.ws/book/6975/1138)]{.citex}  
    [Whomever you beat, I will beat him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001295) [من يضْربهُ زيد أضربه]{.ar}
    [[[همع الهوامع للسيوطي]{.ar} 2/566](https://shamela.ws/book/6975/1138)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever Zayd beats [him], I will beat him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001296) [من تضربه أضربه]{.ar}
    [[[همع الهوامع للسيوطي]{.ar} 2/566](https://shamela.ws/book/6975/1138)]{.citex}  
    [Whomever you beat [him], I will beat him.]{.trans}  


If the conditional-device is
preceded by a preposition, 
or a annexed noun,
it they will be in the i-case.
Example:

(@ex001297) [بِمَنْ تَمْرُرْ أَمْرُرْ بِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/82](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/935)]{.citex}  
    [By whom you pass, I will pass.]{.trans}

(@ex001298) [غُلَامَ مَنْ تَضْرِبْ أَضْرِبْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 2/451](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1035)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever's slave-boy you beat, I will beat.]{.trans}  

The conditional-devices
[أَيْنَ]{.ar}/[أَيْنَمَا]{.ar},
[حَيْثُمَا]{.ar},
[مَتَى]{.ar},
[أَيَّانَ]{.ar},
and
[أَنَّى]{.ar}
are analyzed in the a-case as adverbs of time/place.
For example:

(@ex001299) [مَتَى تَخْرُجْ أَخْرُجْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [When you will exit, I will exit.]{.trans}  

(@ex001300) [مَتَى أَضَعِ الْعِمَامَة تَعْرِفُونِي]{.ar}
    [[[شرح قطر الندى وبل الصدى]{.ar} 86](https://shamela.ws/book/6970/86)]{.citex}  
    [When I take off the turban, you will recognize me.]{.trans}  

<!--
(@ex001301) [متى ما تَقُمْ أَقُمْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 3/135](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/1017)]{.citex}  
    [Whenever you stand, I will stand.]{.trans}  
-->

(@ex001302) [مَتَى مَا تَلْقَنِي فَرْدَيْنِ تَرْجُفْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/17](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1709)]{.citex}  
    [Whenever you meet me individually, you shall quake.]{.trans}  

(@ex001303) [أَيَّانَ تَذْهَبْ أَذْهَبْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [When you will go, I will go.]{.trans}  

(@ex001304) [فَأَيَّانَ مَا تَعْدِلْ بِهَا الرِّيحُ تَنْزِلِ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 88](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1710)]{.citex}  
    [So whenever the wind inclines it, it comes down.]{.trans}  

(@ex001305) [أَيْنَ تَجْلِسْ أَجْلِسْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [Where you will sit, I will sit.]{.trans}  

(@ex001306) [أَیۡنَمَا تَكُونُوا۟ یُدۡرِككُّمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة النساء]{.ar} 4:78](https://quran.com/4/78)]{.citex}  
    [Wherever you may be, death will overtake you]{.trans}  

(@ex001307) [أَنَّى تَذْهَبْ تُصِبْ خَيْرًا]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [Wherever you will go, you will strike goodness.]{.trans}  

(@ex001308) [حَيْثُمَا تَسْتَقِمْ تُفْلِحْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [Wherever you stand firm, you will succeed.]{.trans}  

The conditional-device
[كَيْفَمَا]{.ar}
is anaylzed as a [HAl]{.trn2}.
For example:

(@ex001309) [كَيْفَمَا تَكُنْ أَكُنْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ألفية ابن مالك للشاطبي]{.ar} 6/108](https://shamela.ws/book/20562/3495)]{.citex}  
    [However you will be, I will be.]{.trans}  

#### The conditional-device [أَيّ]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

The conditional-device
[أَيّ]{.ar}
behaves like the others above.
Except, it displays its case.
Examples:

As a subject:

(@ex001310) [أيٌّ يُكْرِمْنِي أُكْرِمْهُ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [Whichever [man] honors me, I will honor him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001311) [أيَّةٌ تُكْرِمْنِي أُكْرِمْهُا]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [Whichever [woman] honors me, I will honor her.]{.trans}  

As a direct doee:

(@ex001312) [أيَّهم تَضْرِبْ أَضْرِبْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [Whichever of them you beat, I will beat.]{.trans}  

(@ex001313) [أيًّا تَضْرِبْ أَضْرِبْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [Whichever you beat, I will beat.]{.trans}  

(@ex001314) [أَیࣰّا مَّا تَدۡعُوا۟ فَلَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَاۤءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الإسراء]{.ar} 17:110](https://quran.com/17/110) cited by [[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [Whichever [name] you call - to Him belong the best names.]{.trans}  
    ([فَ]{.ar} introducing the condition-response is discussed in @sec-j_sh_msc below.)


[مَا]{.ar} can be added between [أَيّ]{.ar} and its annexed-to noun.
For example:

(@ex001315) [أَیَّمَا ٱلۡأَجَلَیۡنِ قَضَیۡتُ فَلَا عُدۡوَ ٰ⁠نَ عَلَیَّۖ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الإسراء]{.ar} 17:110](https://quran.com/17/110) cited by [[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [Whichever of the two terms I complete - there is no injustice to me]{.trans}  

As a adverb of time/place:

(@ex001316) [أَيَّ وَقْتٍ تَقُمْ أَقُمْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [Whichever time you stand, I will stand.]{.trans}  

(@ex001317) [أَيَّ مَكَانٍ تَجْلِسْ أَجْلِسْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/16](https://shamela.ws/book/174/1708)]{.citex}  
    [Whichever time you stand, I will stand.]{.trans}  

#### The conditional-device [إِذْمَا]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

[إِذْمَا]{.ar},
according to the standard view,
is a particle like [إِنْ]{.ar}.
And like [إِنْ]{.ar} it will then mean [if]{.trans}, not [when]{.trans}.^[[[شرح التصريح على التوضيح]{.ar} 2/398](https://shamela.ws/book/9985/1152); [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/79](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1184#p1)]

(@ex001318) [إِذْمَا تَقُمْ أَقُمْ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح التصريح على التوضيح]{.ar} 2/398](https://shamela.ws/book/9985/1152)]{.citex}  
    [If you stand, I will stand.]{.trans}  


<!--
[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/459ff
-->


### Non-ø-case-izing conditional-devices

The main non-ø-case-izing conditional-devices
are [إِذَا]{.ar}
(which we treated in @sec-jsh_idha above),
and [لَوْ]{.ar}
(which we treat in @sec-jsh_law below.)

For some background regarding
non-ø-case-izing conditional-devices,
for the earlier grammarians,
conditionality was strongly associated with the syntax of a
ø-case condition-verb.
So much so that even [إِذَا]{.ar} and [لَوْ]{.ar} may not have been treated under the heading of conditional sentences.
As grammar developed, semantic considerations allowed
them to be discussed with [إِنْ]{.ar} as conditional-devices.^[Giolfo and Hodges, "Conditionality: Syntax and meaning in al-Sīrāfī and Ibn Sīnā"; Giolfo, "Real and irreal conditionals in Arabic grammar: From al-ʾAstarābāḏī to Sībawayhi"]

Even so,
unlike
ø-case-izing conditional-devices,
non-ø-case-izing conditional-devices,
are a loosely defined set,
with some
ø-case-izing conditional-devices
imparting only a whiff of,
or only partial
conditionality.

There are some indicators,
such that if one or more are present,
they can allow a sentence to have a conditional meaning, in varying degrees.
These are:

+ There are two clauses where the execution of the event in one (condition-response) clause is dependent on the fulfilment of the execution of an event in the other (condition) clause.
+ The condition clause occurs before the condition-response clause in sentence word order.
+ The condition clause has a verb which can be considered (loosely) the condition-verb. Same goes for the condition-response clause.
+ The tense of the condition-verb and/or condition-response-verb (if [mADI]{.trn2}) is shifted to the future.

We discuss some of these
non-ø-case-izing conditional-devices
below:

#### Question-devices and adverbs of time/place {.unnumbered}

The same
question-devices the adverbs of time/place 
which we discussed as 
ø-case-izing conditional-devices
can also impart a conditional meaning
when used with their original functions
as connected nouns and adverbs of time/place.

As discussed above,
when used as such,
they may technically not be considered "conditional sentences"
because of the lack of an (either overt or positional) ø-case condition-verb.

We list some examples below.
Note that the verbs in the condition and condition-response are not in the ø-case.
Technically, they won't be called the
"condition-verb"
and "condition-response-verb".
Furthermore, the structure of the "condition-core" and "condition-response-core"
could technically not have to be a verbal sentence.

(@ex001319) [مَا تَقُولُ أَقُولُ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/69](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/922)]{.citex}  
    [What you say, I will say.]{.trans}  

(@ex001320) [أَقُولُ مَا تَقُولُ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/70](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/923)]{.citex}  
    [I will say what you say.]{.trans}  
    This sentence has little conditional meaning, if any, but we have included it as the inverse of example (@ex001319) above.

(@ex001321) [الَّذِي تَقُولُ أَقُولُ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/69](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/922)]{.citex}  
    [The one that you say, I will say.]{.trans}  

(@ex001322) [مَنْ يَأْتِينِي آتِيهِ]{.ar}^[This is [يأتني]{.ar} in the source, but the context seems to indicate that it is a typographical error and that it should be [يأتيني]{.ar}. The commentary [[شرح كتاب سيبويه للسيرافي]{.ar} 3/266](https://shamela.ws/book/17726/1262) for this section has [يأتيني]{.ar}.]
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/69](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/922)]{.citex}  
    [Who comes to me, I will come to him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001323) [آتِي مَنْ يَأْتِينِي]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/70](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/923)]{.citex}  
    [I will come to the one who comes to me.]{.trans}  

(@ex001324) [آتِي مَنْ أَتَانِي]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/70](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/923)]{.citex}  
    [I will come to who came to me.]{.trans}  
    (Note that in this particular sentence, [مَنْ]{.ar} may also be considered to be a
    ø-case-izing conditional-device, like in example (@ex001293) above. In which case [أَتَانِي]{.ar} is a true condition-verb
    in place of [يَأْتِنِي]{.ar}, and there is a deleted condition-response after it.
    And the meaning will be [I will come to who **will come** to me]{.trans}.^[[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/70](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/923)])

(@) [ومَنْ يَمِيلُ أَمَالَ السَّيْفُ ذِرْوَتَهُ ~ حَيْثُ الْتَقَى من حفا فِي رَأْسِهِ الشَّعَرُ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/70](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/923)]{.citex}  

(@ex001325) [بِمَنْ تَمُرُّ بِهِ أَمُرُّ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/80](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/933)]{.citex}  
    [By whom you pass, I pass.]{.trans}

(@ex001326) [أَيُّهَا تَشَاءُ أُعْطِيكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/69](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/922)]{.citex}  
    [Whichever of them you wish, I will give you.]{.trans}  

(@ex001327) [أُعْطِيكَ أَيُّهَا تَشَاءُ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/70](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/923)]{.citex}  
    [I will give you whichever of them you wish.]{.trans}  

(@ex001328) [حَيْثُ تَكُونُ أَكُونُ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/58](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/911)]{.citex}  
    [Where you will be, I will be.]{.trans}  

(@ex001329) [إِنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ رَجُلٌ أَسِيفٌ وَإِنَّهُ مَتَى يَقُومُ فِي مَقَامِكَ لاَ يُسْمِعُ النَّاسَ]{.ar}
    [[[سنن النسائي]{.ar} :833](https://sunnah.com/nasai:833) cited by [[شواهد التوضيح لابن مالك]{.ar} 72](https://shamela.ws/book/98123/69)]{.citex}^[[[شواهد التوضيح لابن مالك]{.ar} 72](https://shamela.ws/book/98123/69) actually cites [صحيح البخاري]{.ar} but it has [متى يقم]{.ar}]  
    [[#abU]{.trn2} Bakr is a tender-hearted man, and when he stands in your place he will not be able to make the people hear.]{.trans}  

#### [كُلَّمَا]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

The adverb of time [كُلَّمَا]{.ar} [every time]{.trans}
is considered to be able to have a conditional meaning.
So much so, that it can cause tense-shifting.
So if a [mADI]{.trn2} verb is after then it can (but doesn't have to) have a future meaning.^[[[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 197](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=3&page=1171&index=150887/150906)]

Example:

(@ex001330) [كُلَّمَا أَصْبَحْتَ فَسَبِّحِ اللهَ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 198](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=3&page=1171&index=150887/150906)]{.citex}  
    [Every time you enter the morning, then glorify Allāh]{.trans}  


#### [أَمَّا]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

The particle
[أَمَّا]{.ar},
meaning [as for]{.trans},
is considered by some to sometimes have a conditional meaning.^[Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 136; [[شرح ابن عقيل على الألفية]{.ar} 4/52](https://shamela.ws/book/9904/1059)]
Usually, it is followed by a noun, and the condition-response is introduced with [فَ]{.ar}.
For example:

(@ex001331) [أَمَّا زَيدٌ فَذَاهِبٌ]{.ar}
    [[[مغني اللبيب لابن هشام]{.ar} 57](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/57084/read?part=1&page=55&index=3271127)]{.citex}  
    [As for Zayd, then [he is] going.]{.trans}  

In example (@ex001331) above, the conditional meaning is apparent
if we
paraphrase it as
[Whatever happens, Zayd is going.]{.trans}.^[[[مغني اللبيب لابن هشام]{.ar} 57](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/57084/read?part=1&page=55&index=3271127)]

Sometimes the [فَ]{.ar} may be omitted in the condition-response.
For example:

(@ex001332) [فأما القتال لا قتال لديكم]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن عقيل على الألفية]{.ar} 4/53](https://shamela.ws/book/9904/1060)]{.citex}  
    [As for fighting, [then] there is no fight with you.]{.trans}

#### [إِذْ]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

According to some reseachers,
the adverb of time [إِذْ]{.ar} [when]{.trans} can sometimes have a conditional meaning.
For example:

(@ex001333) [وَإِذۡ لَمۡ یَهۡتَدُوا۟ بِهِۦ فَسَیَقُولُونَ هَـٰذَاۤ إِفۡكࣱ قَدِیمࣱ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الأحقاف]{.ar} 46:11](https://quran.com/46/11) cited by Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 173]{.citex}  
    [And when they are not guided by it, they will say, "This is an ancient falsehood."]{.trans}  

#### [لَمَّا]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

[لَمَّا]{.ar} has a meaning similar to [إِذْ]{.ar},
and can also be considered to have a conditional meaning for the past tense.^[[[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 3/230](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=3&page=1204&index=150887/150910)]

(@ex001334) [لَمَّا نَزَلَ الْمَطَرُ رَبَا الزَّرْعُ]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/481]{.citex}  
    [When the rain came down, the crop grew.]{.trans}  


## Using [قَتَلَ]{.ar} vs [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}

Regarding
the distinction in meaning between using [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} vs. [قَتَلَ]{.ar} for a future meaning,
the [mADI]{.trn2} verb signifies certainty and the completion of an action.
Whereas,
the [muDArie]{.trn2} verb in general signifies an imperfect (i.e. progressive, continual, habitual, or future) action.
And a ø-case [muDArie]{.trn2} verb, in particular, signifies the potentiality of an action.^[see [التأويل الزمني للجملة الشرطية في اللغة العربية لعارف الدين]{.ar} 49]

Here are some possible circumstances where choosing a [mADI]{.trn2} vs [muDArie]{.trn2} verb in a conditional sentence
may affect nuances in the meaning:

#### The [muDArie]{.trn2} verb can be used to signify a continual action {.unnumbered}

In some contexts,
the [muDArie]{.trn2} verb can be used to signify a continual action.
Whereas [قَتَلَ]{.ar} can be used to signify a single action.^[[[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/58](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1163)]
For example:

(@jsh_ex_quran_31_12) [وَمَن **یَشۡكُرۡ** فَإِنَّمَا یَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن **كَفَرَ** فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِیٌّ حَمِیدࣱ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة لقمان]{.ar} 31:12](https://quran.com/31/12)]{.citex}  
    [And whoever is grateful is grateful for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever denies [His favor] - then indeed, Allāh is Free of need and Praiseworthy.]{.trans}  

In example (@jsh_ex_quran_31_12) above,
[يَشْكُرْ]{.ar} uses the [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} form,
whereas
[كَفَرَ]{.ar} uses the [قَتَلَ]{.ar} form.
One interpretation is that gratitute is a continual action whereas even only one action of disbelief requires that one stop doing it.^[[[تفسير الرازي]{.ar} for [سورة لقمان]{.ar} 31:12](https://tafsir.app/alrazi/31/12) cited by [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/58](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1163)]

By the way, [شَكَرَ]{.ar} in the [قَتَلَ]{.ar} form is also found as a condition-verb:

(@) [وَمَن **شَكَرَ** فَإِنَّمَا یَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن **كَفَرَ** فَإِنَّ رَبِّی غَنِیࣱّ كَرِیمࣱ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة النمل]{.ar} 27:40](https://quran.com/27/40)]{.citex}  
    [And whoever is grateful - his gratitude is only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous.]{.trans}  

#### [قَتَلَ]{.ar} can be used to signify a generic action {.unnumbered}

[قَتَلَ]{.ar} can be used to signify a generic action.^[Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 17--18]
The implication is that it is proven through past experience.^[[[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/63](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1168)]
For example:

(@) [مَنْ صَبَرَ ظَفَرَ]{.ar}
    [[[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/63](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1168)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever is patient, overcomes.]{.trans}  

Whereas, [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} may signify potentiality.
For example:

(@) [مَنْ يَعْمَلْ يَأْكُلْ]{.ar}
    [[[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/63](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1168)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever should work, he may eat.]{.trans}  

#### [قَتَلَ]{.ar} can be used to signify certainty in an event {.unnumbered}

In some contexts,
[قَتَلَ]{.ar} could be used
when an event is deemed or hoped to be more certain.^[[Jamil, "Arabic rhetoric made simple" Conditionals, part 2](https://www.learnarabiconline.com/arabic-rhetoric/ilm-ul-maani/conditionals-part-2/)]
For example:

(@) [إِنْ دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ\ ...]{.ar}
    [[Jamil, "Arabic rhetoric made simple" Conditionals, part 2](https://www.learnarabiconline.com/arabic-rhetoric/ilm-ul-maani/conditionals-part-2/)]{.citex}  
    [If he enters Paradise (and we hope it will be so)\ ...]{.trans}  

Consider also the following [Ayah]{.trn2}:

(@) [فَإِذَا جَاۤءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ قَالُوا۟ لَنَا هَـٰذِهِۦۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَیِّئَةࣱ یَطَّیَّرُوا۟ بِمُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥۤۗ]{.quran}  
    [[[سورة الأعراف]{.ar} 7:131](https://quran.com/7/131) cited by [[مختصر المعاني للتفتازاني]{.ar} 89](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/16360/read?part=1&page=85&index=72272/72275)]{.citex}  
    [But when good [i.e., provision] came to them, they said, "This is ours [by right]." And if a bad [condition] struck them, they saw an evil omen in Moses and those with him.]{.trans}

Note that the condition with [الْحَسَنَة]{.ar} [good]{.trans} is expressed with the [قَتَلَ]{.ar} form [جَاءَ]{.ar} and with [إِذَا]{.ar}.
Whereas the condition with [سَيِّئَة]{.ar} [evil]{.trans} is expressed with the [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} form [تُصِبْ]{.ar} and with [إِنْ]{.ar}.
This contrast has been explained by stating that [إِذَا]{.ar} and the [mADI]{.trn2} verb indicate a higher probability of occurrence,
and [إِنْ]{.ar} and the ø-case [muDArie]{.trn2} verb indicate a lower probability.^[[[مختصر المعاني للتفتازاني]{.ar} 89](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/16360/read?part=1&page=85&index=72272/72275); [[تفسير ابن عاشور]{.ar} for [سورة الأعراف]{.ar} 7:131](https://tafsir.app/ibn-aashoor/7/131)]

#### [قَتَلَ]{.ar} can be used to impart more force to the statement {.unnumbered}

In some contexts,
[قَتَلَ]{.ar} could be used to impart more force to the conditional sentence,
without necessarily implying the condition is likely to take place.
For example:

(@) [وَلَقَدۡ أُوحِیَ إِلَیۡكَ وَإِلَى ٱلَّذِینَ مِن قَبۡلِكَ **لَىِٕنۡ أَشۡرَكۡتَ** لَیَحۡبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ وَلَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡخَـٰسِرِینَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الزمر]{.ar} 39:65](https://quran.com/39/65) cited by [[مختصر المعاني للتفتازاني]{.ar} 93](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/16360/read?part=1&page=89&index=72272/72275)]{.citex}  
    [And it was already revealed to you and to those before you that if you should associate [anything] with Allāh, your work would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers.]{.trans}  

<!--
(@) [قُلۡ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَـٰنِ وَلَدࣱ فَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡعَـٰبِدِینَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الزخرف]{.ar} 43:81](https://quran.com/43/81)]{.citex}  
    [Say, [O Muḥammad], "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of [his] worshippers."]{.trans}  
-->

Regarding the condition
[لَئِنْ أَشْرَكْتَ]{.ar}
in this [Ayah]{.trn2}, the Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} would never associate anyone with Allāh.
And so it is actually his nation, to whom this threat is directed.^[[[تفسير ابن عثيمين]{.ar} for [سورة الزمر]{.ar} 39:65](https://tafsir.app/ibn-uthaymeen/39/65)]
The usage of the [قَتَلَ]{.ar} form [أَشْرَكَ]{.ar} has been analyzed to lend more force to this indirect use of the condition.^[[[مختصر المعاني للتفتازاني]{.ar} 93](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/16360/read?part=1&page=89&index=72272/72275)]


## The tense of the conditional sentence {#sec-jsh_tense}

### The tense of the simple conditional sentence

In a simple conditional sentence,
i.e.
one where the condition-core
and the condition-response-core
are simple verbal sentences,
the tense of both the condition and the condition-response
is typically shifted to the future
due to the influence of the conditional-device.
regardless of whether the [قَتَلَ]{.ar} or [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} form is used as the condition-verb or the condition-response-verb.
So, for example,
all of the following conditional sentences will typically have a future meaning:

(@ex001242) a. [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي أُكْرِمْكَ]{.ar}  
    b. [إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِي أَكْرَمْتُكَ]{.ar}  
    c. [إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِي أُكْرِمْكَ]{.ar}  
    d. [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي أَكْرَمْتُكَ]{.ar}  
    e. [إِذَا أَتَيْتَنِي أَكْرَمْتُكَ]{.ar}  
    [If you come to me, I will honor you.]{.trans}

Having said this,
a conditional sentence will not necessarily always signify a future event.
Instead,
the tense of a conditional sentence should really be determined from context.
In order to prove this, we show that
the simple conditional sentence can occasionally admit a past tense meaning.
Examples:

(@ex001243) [قَالُوۤا۟ إِن **یَسۡرِقۡ** فَقَدۡ سَرَقَ أَخࣱ لَّهُۥ مِن قَبۡلُۚ]{.quran}  
    [[[سورة يوسف]{.ar} 12:77](https://quran.com/12/77) cited by [[شواهد التوضيح لابن مالك]{.ar} 231](https://shamela.ws/book/98123/228)]{.citex}^[See also [[البحر المحيط لأبي حيان]{.ar} for [سورة يوسف]{.ar} 12:77](https://tafsir.app/albahr-almuheet/12/77) and Gätje, "Zur Struktur gestörter Konditionalgefüge im Arabischen" 175.]  
    [They said, "If he steals - a brother of his has stolen before."]{.trans}

(@ex001244) [وَإِذَا **رَأَوۡا۟** تِجَـٰرَةً أَوۡ لَهۡوًا **ٱنفَضُّوۤا۟** إِلَیۡهَا وَتَرَكُوكَ قَاۤىِٕمࣰاۚ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الجمعة]{.ar} 62:11](https://quran.com/62/11) cited by [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/66](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1171)]{.citex}  
    [But [on one occasion] when they **saw** a transaction or a diversion, [O Muḥammad], they **rushed** to it and left you standing.]{.trans}  

(@ex001245) [قُلۡ إِنِ **ٱفۡتَرَیۡتُهُۥ** فَعَلَیَّ إِجۡرَامِی وَأَنَا۠ بَرِیۤءࣱ مِّمَّا تُجۡرِمُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة هود]{.ar} 11:35](https://quran.com/11/35) cited by [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/66](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1171)]{.citex}  
    [Say, "If **I have invented it**, then upon me is [the consequence of] my crime; but I am innocent of what [crimes] you commit."]{.trans}

(@ex001246) [أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ إِذَا أُتِيَ بِطَعَامٍ سَأَلَ عَنْهُ **فَإِنْ قِيلَ** هَدِيَّةٌ **أَكَلَ** مِنْهَا **وَإِنْ قِيلَ** صَدَقَةٌ **لَمْ يَأْكُلْ** مِنْهَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :1077](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1077)]{.citex}  
    [that the Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} would, when he was brought some food, ask about it. If it **was said** [that it was] a gift, he **ate** from it, and if it **was said** [that it was] charity, he **did not eat** from it.]{.trans}  

(@ex001247) [مَا عَابَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم طَعَامًا قَطُّ إِنِ **اشْتَهَاهُ أَكَلَهُ** وَإِنْ **كَرِهَهُ تَرَكَهُ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :5409](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5409)]{.citex}  
    [The Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} never criticized any food whatsoever. If **he liked it, he ate** it. And if **he disliked it, he left** it.]{.trans}

### With [فَ]{.ar} as the condition-response-link {#sec-jsh_tense_fa}

In @sec-j_sh_msc below we will learn that
[فَ]{.ar} is sometimes used as a condition-response-link.
And we will learn the rules of when [فَ]{.ar} is required to introduce the condition-response.
In this section, we will only note that when
[فَ]{.ar} is used as
a condition-response-link
then
the tense of condition-response-core is free from the future-shifting influence of the conditional-device.
The tense of the condition-response-core is then determined from evaluating it independently.
Here are some examples:

(@ex001248) [وَإِن كَانَ قَمِیصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرࣲ **فَكَذَبَتۡ** وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِینَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة يوسف]{.ar} 12:27](https://quran.com/12/27)]{.citex}  
    [But if his shirt is torn from the back, **then she has lied**, and he is of the truthful.]{.trans}  

(@ex001249) [فَإِنْ كُنْتِ بَرِيئَةً **فَسَيُبَرِّئُكِ** اللَّهُ وَإِنْ كُنْتِ أَلْمَمْتِ بِذَنْبٍ **فَاسْتَغْفِرِي** اللَّهَ وَتُوبِي إِلَيْهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :2770](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2770)]{.citex}  
    [If you are innocent, then **Allāh will acquit you**, and if you have lapsed into a sin **then seek forgiveness** from Allāh and turn to Him in repentance.]{.trans}

(@ex001250) [إِنْ قَتَلْتَ حَمْزَةَ بِعَمِّي **فَأَنْتَ حُرٌّ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :4072](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4072)]{.citex}  
    [If you kill [#Hamzah]{.trn2} [in revenge] for my uncle, **then you are free**.]{.trans}  

### With [كَانَ]{.ar} as the condition-verb {#sec-jsh-kaana-shart}

We saw above that when [فَ]{.ar} is used to introduce the condition-response
then its tense is free
from the future-shifting influence of the conditional-device.
The verb [كَانَ]{.ar} can similarly be used to introduce the condition,
and it makes the tense of the condition free
from the future-shifting influence of the conditional-device.
In such sentences, the condition-core beginning with [كَانَ]{.ar} will still be considered a verbal sentence.

Let's say that we wish to expressly indicate a past tense for the condition,
as in the example:

(@ex001251) [If he studied, then he will succeed.]{.trans}

If we express the condition as
[إِنْ دَرَسَ]{.ar},
then it will typically take a future tense meaning.
In order to explicitly specify a past tense,
we begin the condition-core with [كَانَ]{.ar}, thus:

(@ex001252) [إِنْ **كَانَ** قَدْ دَرَسَ فَسَيَنْجَحُ]{.ar}  
    [If he studied, then he will succeed.]{.trans}

In example (@ex001252) above,
the [قَدْ]{.ar} is optional, and may be removed for the same meaning.

Similarly, let's say that we expressly indicate a present tense meaning for the condition
as in the example:

(@ex001253) [If he is eating, then let him.]{.trans}

[He is eating]{.trans}
can be translated as
[يَأْكُلُ]{.ar}
which is a u-case [muDArie]{.trn2} verb.
We cannot use this verb directly as the condition-verb with [إِنْ]{.ar}
and would have to modify it to the ø-case verb، thus:
[إِنْ يَأْكُلْ]{.ar}.
But then this would typically have the tense meaning
[if he will eat]{.trans}.

In order to specify a present tense,
we begin the condition-core with [كَانَ]{.ar}, thus:

(@ex001254) [إِنْ كَانَ يَأْكُلُ فَدَعْهُ]{.ar}  
    [If he is eating, then let him.]{.trans}

[كَانَ]{.ar} now can lose its past-tense meaning of "was".
But
[إِنْ كَانَ يَأْكُلُ]{.ar}
could also signify the past-continuous tense
[if he **was** eating]{.trans}.
Context will tell us which of two is intended.

[كَانَ]{.ar} can also be used to allow arbitrary sentences in the condition.
Let's say that we widh to express:

(@ex001255) [If you are sitting, then come to me.]{.trans}

[You are sitting]{.trans}
may be translated as
[أَنْتَ جَالِسٌ]{.ar}.
In order to use this as the condition,
we transform it using [كَانَ]{.ar} thus:

(@ex001256) [إِنْ كُنتَ جَالِسًا فَأْتِنِي]{.ar}  
    [If you are sitting, then come to me.]{.trans}

By the way
[إِنْ كُنْتَ جَالِسًا]{.ar}
could also signify the past-continuous tense
[if you were sitting]{.trans}.
It could even signify a future tense, for example:

(@ex001257) [إن كنت غدا جالسا فائتني]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 4/115](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=4&page=1552)]{.citex}  
    [If you are tomorrow sitting then come to me.]{.trans}

Here is another example of conditions with [كَانَ]{.ar} signifying a future meaning:

(@ex001258) [**إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ عَمَلٌ صَالِحٌ** أُخِذَ مِنْهُ بِقَدْرِ مَظْلَمَتِهِ، **وَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ حَسَنَاتٌ** أُخِذَ مِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ صَاحِبِهِ فَحُمِلَ عَلَيْهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :2449](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2449)]{.citex}  
    [**If he will have a good deed**, it will be taken from according to his oppression, **and if he will not have good deeds**, his companion's bad deeds will be taken from and put on him.]{.trans}

Context will help disambiguate which meaning is intended.

Here are some more examples of conditional sentences with [كَانَ]{.ar} as the condition-verb:

(@ex001259) [إِن كُنتُ قُلۡتُهُۥ فَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَهُۥۚ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة المائدة]{.ar} 5:116](https://quran.com/5/116), cited by [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/64](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1169)]{.citex}  
    [If I had said it, You would have known it.]{.trans}  

(@ex001260) [إِن كَانَ قَمِیصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلࣲ فَصَدَقَتۡ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَـٰذِبِینَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة يوسف]{.ar} 12:26](https://quran.com/12/26), cited by [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/64](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1169)]{.citex}  
    [If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars.]{.trans}  

(@ex001261) [قَالَ فَمَا لِي لَا أَعْتَدُّ بِهَا وَإِنْ كُنْتُ قَدْ عَجَزْتُ وَاسْتَحْمَقْتُ]{.ar}
    [[[مسند أحمد]{.ar} :304](https://hadithunlocked.com/ahmad:304)]{.citex}  
    [He said, "Why wouldn't I count it? Even if I wasn't able to and acted foolishly."]{.trans}  

(@ex001262) [قَالَ لَهَا وَإِنْ **كَانَ لَمْ يُؤْذَنْ** لِي فِي ثَقِيفٍ يَا خُوَيْلَةُ]{.ar}
    [[[تاريخ الطبري]{.ar} 3/85](https://shamela.ws/book/9783/1359) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 33]{.citex}  
    [He ([ﷺ]{.areng}) said to her, "And if [#vaqIf]{.trn2} **has not been permitted** for me, O [#xuwaylah]{.trn2}?"]{.trans}  

(@ex001263) [إِنْ **كَانَ لَا يَضُرُّكِ وَلَا يُضَيِّقُ عَلَيْكِ** فَإِنِّي أُحِبُّ أَنْ أُدْفَنَ مَعَ صَاحِبَيَّ]{.ar}
    [[[مستدرك الحاكم]{.ar} :4519](https://hadithunlocked.com/hakim:4519)]{.citex}  
    [If it **does not harm you or make it difficult for you** then I would like that I be buried with my two companions.]{.trans}  

(@ex001264) [مَنْ قَالَ أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ الَّذِي لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ الْحَىُّ الْقَيُّومُ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ غُفِرَ لَهُ وَإِنْ **كَانَ فَرَّ** مِنَ الزَّحْفِ]{.ar}
    [[[سنن أبي داود]{.ar} :1517](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1517)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever says, "I seek forgiveness from Allāh, the one whom there is no deity except He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and I turn to Him in repentance," he is forgiven even if he **had fled** from battle.]{.trans}

(@ex001265) [إِنْ **كُنْتَ تُرِيدُ** أَنْ تُصِيبَ السُّنَّةَ الْيَوْمَ فَاقْصُرِ الْخُطْبَةَ وَعَجِّلِ الْوُقُوفَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :1663](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1663)]{.citex}  
    [If **you want** to follow the Sunnah today then shorten the sermon and make earlier the stay [at [#earafah]{.trn2}].]{.trans}

(@ex001266) [فَإِنْ **كُنْتِ بَرِيئَةً** فَسَيُبَرِّئُكِ اللَّهُ وَإِنْ **كُنْتِ أَلْمَمْتِ** بِذَنْبٍ فَاسْتَغْفِرِي اللَّهَ وَتُوبِي إِلَيْهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :2770](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2770) cited by [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/65](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1170)]{.citex}  
    [If **you are innocent**, Allāh will acquit you, and if **you have lapsed** into a sin then seek forgiveness from Allāh and turn to Him in repentance.]{.trans}

(@ex001267) [وَإِن **كُنتُمۡ** فِی رَیۡبࣲ مِّمَّا نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا فَأۡتُوا۟ بِسُورَةࣲ مِّن مِّثۡلِهِۦ وَٱدۡعُوا۟ شُهَدَاۤءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَـٰدِقِینَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة البقرة]{.ar} 2:23](https://quran.com/2/23)]{.citex}  
    [And if you **are** in doubt about what We have sent down [i.e., the Qur’ān] upon Our Servant [i.e., Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ)], then produce a sūrah the like thereof and call upon your witnesses [i.e., supporters] other than Allāh, if you should be truthful.]{.trans}

(@ex001268) [إِذَا كَانَ الْمَاءُ قُلَّتَيْنِ لَمْ يَحْمِلِ الْخَبَثَ]{.ar}
    [[[سنن النسائي]{.ar} :52](https://sunnah.com/nasai:52)]{.citex}  
    [When the water is two qullahs then it will not carry filth.]{.trans}  

(@ex001269) [فَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ أَكْفَاءَ قَاتَلْنَاكُمْ]{.ar}
    [[[مغازي الواقدي]{.ar} 1/68](https://shamela.ws/book/23680/109)]{.citex}  
    [If you are a match for us we will fight you.]{.trans}

<!--
Consistent with what we stated in section\ () above,
-->
If the condition's sentence already has [كَانَ]{.ar}
to indicate the past tense, then another [كَانَ]{.ar} is not added.
For example:

<!--
(@ex001270) [كُنْتُ آتِي النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَأَسْتَأْذِنُ فَإِنَّ **كَانَ** فِي صَلَاةٍ سَبَّحَ وَإِنْ **كَانَ** فِي غَيْرِ صَلَاةٍ أَذِنَ لِي]{.ar}
    [[[مسند أحمد]{.ar} :809](https://sunnah.com/ahmad:809)]{.citex}  
    [I used to come to the Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} and ask permission to enter. If he **was** in prayer he would say [subHana -llAh]{.trn} and if he **was** not in prayer, he would permit me.]{.trans}  
-->

(@ex001271) [كَانَ يَنَامُ أَوَّلَ اللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَإِذَا **كَانَ** مِنَ السَّحَرِ أَوْتَرَ ثُمَّ أَتَى فِرَاشَهُ فَإِذَا **كَانَ** لَهُ حَاجَةٌ أَلَمَّ بِأَهْلِهِ فَإِذَا سَمِعَ الأَذَانَ وَثَبَ فَإِنْ **كَانَ** جُنُبًا أَفَاضَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَاءِ وَإِلاَّ تَوَضَّأَ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ إِلَى الصَّلاَةِ]{.ar}
    [[[سنن النسائي]{.ar} :1680](https://sunnah.com/nasai:1680)]{.citex}  
    [He would sleep in the first part of the night. Then he would stand (for prayer). Then when it was the last part of the night, he would pray the witr. Then he would come to his bed. Then if he had a need he would go to his wife. Then when he heard the [apAn]{.trn2}, he would get up. If we was in a state of sexual impurity he poured water over himself. And if not he would perform [wudUE]{.trn2}. Then he would go out to the prayer.]{.trans}  


The ø-case [muDArie]{.trn2} verb [يَكُنْ]{.ar} can also be used in this manner.
<!--
Consistent with what we learned in section\ () above,
-->
It may indicate potentiality or possibility.
For example:

(@ex001272) [فَإِن **يكن قد علا رَأْسِي** وَغَيره ~ صرف الزَّمَان وتغيير من الشّعْر]{.ar}
    [[[جمهرة الأمثال للعسكري]{.ar} 1/263](https://shamela.ws/book/6897/261)]{.citex}  
    [So if **it be that my head has become dignified** and the elapsing of time and a changing of hair has changed it\ ...]{.trans}

(@ex001273) [فَإِنْ تَكُنِ الدُّنْيَا بِلُبْنَى تَغَيَّرَتْ فَلِلدَّهْرِ وَالدُّنْيَا بُطُونٌ وَأَظْهُرُ]{.ar}
    [cited by Gätje, "Zur Struktur gestörter Konditionalgefüge im Arabischen" 175]{.citex}  
    [And if the world has changed by [#lubnA]{.trn2}, then the world has innards and outwards.]{.trans}  


(@ex001274) [إِنْ **يَكُ** هَذَا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ يُمْضِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3895](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3895) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 21]{.citex}  
    [If this **be** from Allāh, He will make it happen.]{.trans}

(@ex001275) [فَإِنْ **يَكُ** صَوَابًا فَمِنَ اللَّهِ وَإِنْ **يَكُنْ** خَطَأً فَمِنِّي وَمِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ وَاللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ بَرِيئَانِ]{.ar}
    [[[سنن أبي داود]{.ar} :2116](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:2116)]{.citex}  
    [If this **be** correct then [it is] from Allāh, and if it **be** erroneous then [it is] from me and from Satan. And Allāh and His Messenger are free [from it].]{.trans}  

Remember from @sec-maani_ism_fail_future
that the doer participle can be used to indicate an intention to do a future action.
This use of the doer participle can carry over to its use in a condition.
For example:

(@ex001276) [إِنْ كُنْتَ فَاعِلاً فَوَاحِدَةً]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :1207](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1207)]{.citex}  
    [If you are going to do it, then (only) once.]{.trans}
