-->

### With a static verb as the condition-verb

In the discussion above,
we have seen that, if the condition is to signify the present tense,
then we will usually have [كَانَ]{.ar} as the condition-verb.
In this section, we add that when the condition-verb is a _static_ verb,
then [كَانَ]{.ar} is not required
to signify the present tense.^[[كَانَ]{.ar} can still be used with a static verb. See for example [[سورة الأنعام]{.ar} 6:35](https://quran.com/6/35), [[سورة يونس]{.ar} 10:71](https://quran.com/10/71)]
We define a static verb,
in the context of conditional sentences to be one of the following^[from Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 13]:

1. An intransitive verb that has an adjectival meaning.
   For example:
   [كَثُرَ]{.ar} [to be many]{.trans},
   [صَحَّ]{.ar} [to be correct]{.trans},
   [كَبُرَ]{.ar} [to be big]{.trans},
   etc.
3. A _modal_ verb that takes a [أَنْ]{.ar} clause as a direct doee.
   For example:
   [شَاءَ]{.ar} [to wish]{.trans},
   [اسْتَطَاعَ]{.ar} [can]{.trans},
   etc.
4. A verb of perception.
   For example:
   [عَلِمَ]{.ar} [to know]{.trans},
   [ظَنَّ]{.ar} [to think]{.trans},
   [حَسِبَ]{.ar} [to consider]{.trans},
   etc.

Here are some examples of conditional sentences with a static verb as the condition-verb:

(@ex001277) [الرِّبَا **وَإِنْ كَثُرَ** فَإِنَّ عَاقِبَتَهُ تَصِيرُ إِلَى قُلٍّ]{.ar}
    [[[مسند أحمد]{.ar} :3754](https://hadithunlocked.com/ahmad:3754)]{.citex}  
    [Interest, even if it **is much**, its outcome becomes less.]{.trans}  

(@ex001278) [فَإِن طَلَّقَهَا فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَیۡهِمَاۤ أَن یَتَرَاجَعَاۤ **إِن ظَنَّاۤ** أَن یُقِیمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِۗ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة البقرة]{.ar} 2:230](https://quran.com/2/230)]{.citex}  
    [And if he [i.e., the latter husband] divorces her [or dies], there is no blame upon them [i.e., the woman and her former husband] for returning to each other if **they think** that they can keep [within] the limits of Allāh.]{.trans}  

For modal verbs like
[شَاءَ]{.ar} [to wish, want]{.trans},
[اسْتَطَاعَ]{.ar} [can]{.trans},
etc.,
if the [أَنْ]{.ar} clause that is the direct doee of the modal verb is in the condition
then it need not be repeated in the condition-response.
The condition-response
can then have an empty verb like [فَعَلَ]{.ar}.^[Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 22]
Example:

(@ex001279) [إِنْ **أَحَبَّ** أَهْلُكِ أَنْ أَصُبَّ لَهُمْ ثَمَنَكِ صَبَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَأُعْتِقَكِ فَعَلْتُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :2564](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2564) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 22]{.citex}  
    [If your people **like** that I pay them your price in a lump sum and so manumit you, I will do so.]{.trans}  

(@ex001280) [إِنَّكُمْ سَتَرَوْنَ رَبَّكُمْ كَمَا تَرَوْنَ هَذَا الْقَمَرَ لاَ تُضَامُّونَ فِي رُؤْيَتِهِ، فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ لاَ تُغْلَبُوا عَلَى صَلاَةٍ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا فَافْعَلُوا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :554](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:554)]{.citex}  
    [Certainly you will see your Lord as you see this moon and you will have no trouble in seeing Him. So if you can avoid missing a prayer before the sunrise and a prayer before sunset then do so.]{.trans}

Or the
[أَنْ]{.ar} clause direct doee of the modal verb can be omitted from the condition
when its meaning is given in the condition-response.
For example:

(@ex001281) [إِنْ **شِئْتَ** دَفَعْتُهَا إِلَيْكَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3828](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3828) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 22]{.citex}  
    [If you **wish**, I will give her to you]{.trans}  

## [فَ]{.ar} as a condition-response-link {#sec-j_sh_msc}

In the simple conditional sentence,
i.e.
one where the condition-core
and the condition-response-core
are simple verbal sentences,
the condition-verb and the condition-response-verb
can take,
what we will call,
the following _basic forms_:

* [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}, negated using [لَا يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}.
* [قَتَلَ]{.ar}, negated using [لَمْ يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}.

Also, as we know,
the conditional-device
generally has a future-shifting influence on these basic forms.

<!--
(We have also seen the [يَقْتُلُ]{.ar} form but we will treat it separately in section\ () below.)
-->

<!--
When the condition-response has either of the above two ([يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} or non-past tense [قَتَلَ]{.ar}) forms,
then it is not introduced by the condition-response-link [فَ]{.ar}.
So for example, 
we say:

(@ex001335) [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي آتِكَ]{.ar}  
    [If you come to me, I will come to you.]{.trans}

But we cannot say:

(@ex001336) ✗ [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي فَآتِكَ]{.ar}
-->

When the condition-response falls outside the above basic forms,
then it will typically be introduced by [فَ]{.ar}.
For example:

(@ex001337) [إِنْ يَأْتِكَ فَأَكْرِمْهُ]{.ar}  
    [If he comes to you, then honor him.]{.trans}

The condition-response in example (@ex001337) above is a verb of command verbal sentence.
Since it is not
one of the basic forms of the condition-response
we use a [فَ]{.ar} to introduce it.

The main reason that a [فَ]{.ar} is needed in such cases,
is to indicate that the condition-response is linked to the condition.^[[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/111](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2049), [[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 4/110](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=4&page=1547&index=150957/150973)]
That is, the condition-response is a consequence of the condition being fulfilled.
[فَ]{.ar} is not needed when the condition-response is one of the basic forms
because in those cases,
the condition-response is directly linked to the conditional-device,
either
by the conditional-device's future-shifting the tense of the condition-response-verb (in most cases),
or by the conditional-device's directly governing the condition-response-verb, if applicable.

Once the [فَ]{.ar} is added,
the condition-response is freed from the
future-shifting influence
of the conditional-device
and its direct government (if applicable).
So,
as we learned in @sec-jsh_tense_fa above,
the tense of the condition-response introduced by [فَ]{.ar}
is evaluated independently.

<!--
[فَ]{.ar} is typically mandatory when the condition-response is not
one of the basic forms.
So, for example,
we cannot (usually) say, without [فَ]{.ar}:

(@ex001338) ✗ [إِنْ يَأْتِكَ أَكْرِمْهُ]{.ar}  

But there are some exceptions
and we will see in the examples below that
[فَ]{.ar} is sometimes not added
even when the condition-response is not one of the basic forms above.

Similarly, [فَ]{.ar} is typically disallowed when
the condition-response is
one of the basic forms.

So, for example, we cannot say:

(@ex001339) ✗ [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي فَآتِكَ]{.ar}

Again,
there are some exceptions
and [فَ]{.ar} can sometimes be added to [قَتَلَ]{.ar}
and [لَا يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} forms in the condition-response, as we will see in the examples below.
-->

<!--
However,
as a special case, [فَ]{.ar} is allowed
when
[قَتَلَ]{.ar}, or [لَمْ يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}
form is used in the condition-response,
but what is intended by these forms is a true past-tense.
For example:

(@ex001340) [إِذَا أَتَيْتَنِي فَأَكْرَمْتُكَ]{.ar}
-->

<!--
[فَ]{.ar} is not needed when the condition-response is a [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} or (non-past tense) [قَتَلَ]{.ar} verbal sentence
because in those cases the link between the condition-response and the condition is readily apparent.
In the case of a [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} condition-response,
the link is indicated by the ø-case of the condition-response-verb,
as in example () above.
And in the case
of a [قَتَلَ]{.ar} condition-response,
it is indicated by the non-past tense meaning of the [قَتَلَ]{.ar} condition-response-verb,
as in the example below:

(@ex001341) [إِذَا أَتَيْتَنِي **أَتَيْتُكَ**]{.ar}
    [If you come to me, I will come to you.]{.trans}
-->
<!--
* [يَقْتُلُ]{.ar} (and [لَا يَقْتُلُ]{.ar}) for both [إِنْ]{.ar} and [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentences
1. For [إِنْ]{.ar} conditional sentences:
   * [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}
   * [قَتَلَ]{.ar} that loses its past tense meaning
   * Occasionally [يَقْتُلُ]{.ar}
2. For [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentences:
   * [قَتَلَ]{.ar} that loses its past tense meaning
   * [يَقْتُلُ]{.ar}

---

In this section we will study condition-responses that are introduced by [فَ]{.ar}.
-->
<!--
We will first treat conditional sentences that are introduced by [إِنْ]{.ar}.

### [فَ]{.ar} in the condition-response for [إِنْ]{.ar} conditional sentences
-->

<!--
Here is an example of an [إِنْ]{.ar} conditional sentence whose condition-response begins with [فَ]{.ar}:

(@ex001342) [إِنْ أَتَاكَ فَأَكْرِمْهُ]{.ar}  
    [If he comes to you then honor him.]{.trans}  
-->

<!--
[فَ]{.ar}, in the beginning of the condition-response,
explicitly makes it clear that the sentence in the condition-response is
a consequence of the condition.
-->

<!--
So far the conditional sentences that we have studied have not been introduced by [فَ]{.ar}.
For example:

(@ex001343) [إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِي أَكْرَمْتُكَ]{.ar}  
    [If you come to me, I will honor you.]{.trans}

This is because the condition-response in such conditional sentences is
a direct consequence
of the condition.
What we mean by
*direct consequence*
is that:

1. The condition-response occurs *because* of the condition being satisfied.
   For example, in example () above, my honoring you is *because of* your coming to me.
   By the way, in some conditional sentences this causality may not be strictly met. For example:

   (@) [فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡكَلۡبِ إِن تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَیۡهِ یَلۡهَثۡ أَوۡ تَتۡرُكۡهُ یَلۡهَثۚ]{.quran}
       [[[سورة الأعراف]{.ar} 7:176](https://quran.com/7/176) cited by [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/53](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1158)]{.citex}  
       [So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he [still] pants.]{.trans}  

2. The conditional sentence matches one of the patterns of conditional sentences. These are:
   
   a. For [إِنْ]{.ar} conditional sentences:

        i. [إِنْ يَقْتُلْ يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}
       ii. [إِنْ قَتَلَ قَتَلَ]{.ar}
      iii. [إِنْ قَتَلَ يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}
       iv. [إِنْ يَقْتُلْ قَتَلَ]{.ar}

   b. For [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentences: [إِذَا قَتَلَ قَتَلَ]{.ar}
        
   
   Substitutable in the above patterns are the negative constructions
   [لَا يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}
   (in place of [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar})
   and
   [لَمْ يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}
   (in place of [قَتَلَ]{.ar}).
   And also [يَقْتُلُ]{.ar} in place of [قَتَلَ]{.ar} for [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentences.


Sometimes,
the condition-response is not a direct consequence (as defined above) of the condition.
Instead,
the condition-response has the force of an independent sentence,
albeit one that is linked, in some respect, to the condition taking place.
-->
<!--
In order to show that the condition-response,
despite its force,
is linked to condition
-->
<!--
Because this link would otherwise not be apparent,
a [فَ]{.ar} is typically required to
explicitly indicate that the condition-response is
related to the occurrence of the condition.
-->

<!--
### Types of condition-responses requiring [فَ]{.ar}
-->

### Situations where [فَ]{.ar} is used as a condition-response-link {#sec-jsh_examples_of_iqtiran_fa}

Here is a (non-exhaustive) list of cases where
[فَ]{.ar} is used to introduce the condition-response:

<!--
#### The condition-response-core is a request sentence {.unnumbered}

What we mean by *request sentence* is a command, supplication, entreaty, or prohibition.
When the condition-response-core is a request sentence
then it is typically required to be introduced by [فَ]{.ar}.
For example:
-->

##### Direct commands {.unnumbered}

(@ex001344) [وَلاَ تُكَلِّفُوهُمْ مَا يَغْلِبُهُمْ، فَإِنْ كَلَّفْتُمُوهُمْ **فَأَعِينُوهُمْ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :30](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:30)]{.citex}  
    [Do not task them with what is too much for them but if you task them, then help them.]{.trans}  

<!--
(@ex001345) [إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي ـ أَوْ قَالَ عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ ـ فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :1166](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1166)]{.citex}  
    -->

(@ex001346) [فَإِنْ غُمَّ عَلَيْكُمْ **فَاقْدُرُوا** لَهُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :1906](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1906)]{.citex}  
    [If it is overcast then estimate for it.]{.trans}

(@ex001347) [إِذَا لَمْ تَسْتَحِي **فَافْعَلْ** مَا شِئْتَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3483](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3483)]{.citex}  
    [If you do not feel ashamed then do whatever you wish.]{.trans}

(@ex001348) [فَإِذَا لَقِيتُمُوهُمْ **فَاصْبِرُوا**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :2965](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2965)]{.citex}  
    [If you meet them then be patient.]{.trans}  

(@ex001349) [إِنْ لَمْ تَجِدِينِي **فَأْتِي** أَبَا بَكْرٍ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :7220](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7220)]{.citex}  
    [If you~1f~ don't find me then come to [#abU #bakr]{.trn2}.]{.trans}  

<!--
##### Supplications: {.unnumbered}
-->

(@ex001350) [اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ فِيَّ خَيْرًا **فَأَرِنِي** رُؤْيَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :7028](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7028)]{.citex}  
    [O Allāh, if you are knowing good in me then show me a dream.]{.trans}


##### Prohibitions {.unnumbered}

The form of the condition-response in prohibitions is
[لَا تَقْتُلْ]{.ar},
which appears to be a basic form.
But because the meaning that is intended by
[لَا تَقْتُلْ]{.ar}
is a prohibition, and not a simple future tense, a [فَ]{.ar} is added before it.

(@ex001351) [فَإِنْ وَجَدْتُمْ غَيْرَ آنِيَتِهِمْ **فَلاَ تَأْكُلُوا** فِيهَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :5488](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5488)]{.citex}  
    [If you find other than their utensils then don't eat in them]{.trans}  

(@ex001352) [وَإِنْ خَالَطَهَا كِلاَبٌ مِنْ غَيْرِهَا **فَلاَ تَأْكُلْ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :5483](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5483)]{.citex}  
    [And if other hounds join in it then don't eat [it]]{.trans}  

(@ex001353) [فَإِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ بِهِ بِأَرْضٍ **فَلاَ تَقْدَمُوا** عَلَيْهِ وَإِذَا وَقَعَ بِأَرْضٍ وَأَنْتُمْ بِهَا **فَلاَ تَخْرُجُوا** فِرَارًا مِنْهُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3473](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3473)]{.citex}  
    [So if you hear of it in a land then don't approach it, and if occurs in a land where you are present, then don't leave [that land] in order to flee from it.]{.trans}

(@ex001354) [إِنْ رَأَيْتُمُونَا ظَهَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ **فَلاَ تَبْرَحُوا** وَإِنْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُمْ ظَهَرُوا عَلَيْنَا **فَلاَ تُعِينُونَا**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :4043](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4043)]{.citex}  
    [If you see us having overcome them then don't leave [this place], and if you see them having overcome us then don't help us.]{.trans}  

##### Indirect commands {.unnumbered}

(@ex001355) [فَأَيُّكُمْ إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يُوَاصِلَ **فَلْيُوَاصِلْ** حَتَّى السَّحَرِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :1963](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1963)]{.citex}  
    [So whichever of you -- if he wants to continue on, then let him continue on until the last part of the night.]{.trans}  

(@ex001356) [إِذَا أَتَى أَحَدَكُمْ خَادِمُهُ بِطَعَامِهِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يُجْلِسْهُ مَعَهُ **فَلْيُنَاوِلْهُ** أُكْلَةً أَوْ أُكْلَتَيْنِ أَوْ لُقْمَةً أَوْ لُقْمَتَيْنِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :5460](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5460)]{.citex}  
    [If the servant of one of you brings him his food, then if he doesn't make him sit with him, then let him hand him a bite or two, or a morsel or two.]{.trans}

<!--
yaqtulu also can be hortative peled 79
-->

##### Indirect prohibitions {.unnumbered}

(@ex001357) [إِذَا شَرِبَ أَحَدُكُمْ **فَلاَ يَتَنَفَّسْ** فِي الإِنَاءِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :5630](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5630) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 79]{.citex}  
    [When one of you drinks then let him not breathe in the vessel.]{.trans}  

(@ex001358) [إِذَا كَانَ أَحَدُكُمْ يُصَلِّي، فَلاَ يَبْصُقْ قِبَلَ وَجْهِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :406](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:406) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 79]{.citex}  
    [When one of you is praying then let him not spit in front of him.]{.trans}  

##### Statements of hope {.unnumbered}

(@ex001359) [إِنْ كُنْتَ كَاذِبًا **فَصَيَّرَكَ** اللَّهُ إِلَى مَا كُنْتَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3464](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3464)]{.citex}  
    [If you are a liar then may Allah make you to what you used to be.]{.trans}  
    (The condition-response begins with a [قَتَلَ]{.ar} form but it is used as a wish and is not linked directly to the conditional-device.)

##### The condition-response-core begins with a fixed verb {.unnumbered}


(@ex001360) [إِنْ يَعِشْ هَذَا الْغُلاَمُ **فَعَسَى** أَنْ لاَ يُدْرِكَهُ الْهَرَمُ حَتَّى تَقُومَ السَّاعَةُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :2953a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2953a)]{.citex}  
    [If this boy should live then maybe old age will not hit him until the hour is estalished.]{.trans}  

(@ex001361) [فَإِنْ صَدَقَا وَبَيَّنَا بُورِكَ لَهُمَا فِي بَيْعِهِمَا وَإِنْ كَذَبَا وَكَتَمَا **فَعَسَى** أَنْ يَرْبَحَا رِبْحًا وَيُمْحَقَا بَرَكَةَ بَيْعِهِمَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :2114](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2114)]{.citex}  
    [If they speak the truth and mention the defects, then their bargain will be blessed, and if they tell lies and conceal the defects, they might gain some financial gain but they will be deprived of the blessing of their sale.]{.trans}

(@ex001362) [فَإِذَا كَانَتْ سَائِمَةُ الرَّجُلِ نَاقِصَةً مِنْ أَرْبَعِينَ شَاةً وَاحِدَةً **فَلَيْسَ** فِيهَا صَدَقَةٌ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :1454](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1454)]{.citex}  
    [If the man's livestock is less than forty sheep then there is no [zakAh]{.trn2} on it.]{.trans}  

(@ex001363) [وَمَن یَفۡعَلۡ ذَ ٰ⁠لِكَ فَلَیۡسَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ فِی شَیۡءٍ إِلَّاۤ أَن تَتَّقُوا۟ مِنۡهُمۡ تُقَىٰةࣰۗ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة آل عمران]{.ar} 3:28](https://quran.com/3/28) cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/466]{.citex}  
    [And whoever [of you] does that has nothing [i.e., no association] with Allāh, except when taking precaution against them in prudence.]{.trans}  

##### The condition-response-core is a nounal sentence {.unnumbered}

(@ex001364) [إِنْ قَتَلْتَ حَمْزَةَ بِعَمِّي **فَأَنْتَ** حُرٌّ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :4072](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4072)]{.citex}  
    [If you kill [#Hamzah]{.trn2} [in revenge] for my uncle, then you are free.]{.trans}  

(@ex001365) [فَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ **فَأُولَئِكَ** الَّذِينَ سَمَّى اللَّهُ، فَاحْذَرُوهُمْ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :4547](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4547)]{.citex}  
    [If you see the people who follow what is open to different interpretations, then they are ones whom Allāh named, so beware of them.]{.trans}  

The nounal sentence may begin with a particle, in which case as well [فَ]{.ar} is used.
For example:

(@ex001366) [مَن یُضۡلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَلَا هَادِیَ لَهُۥۚ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الأعراف]{.ar} 7:186](https://quran.com/7/186) cited by [[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 4/110](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=4&page=1547&index=150957/150973)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever Allāh sends astray - there is no guide for him.]{.trans}

(@ex001367) [إِن تُعَذِّبۡهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ عِبَادُكَۖ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة المائدة]{.ar} 5:118](https://quran.com/5/118) cited by [[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 4/110](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=4&page=1547&index=150957/150973)]{.citex}  
    [If You should punish them - indeed they are Your servants;]{.trans}

<!--
[فَ]{.ar} is sometimes dropped in this scenario by poetic license.
For example:

(@ex001368) [من يفعل الحسنات الله يشكرها]{.ar}
    [radiy 4/111]
-->

<!--
##### The condition-response-core is a question {.unnumbered}

radiy says fa need not be added. See 4/113.
-->

##### The condition-response-core is a [قَتَلَ]{.ar} verbal sentence but it signifies the past tense {.unnumbered}

When the condition-response is a [قَتَلَ]{.ar} verbal sentence but the verb signifies the past tense
then [فَ]{.ar} is added to it.^[See also Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 80]

(@ex001369) [وَإِن كَانَ قَمِیصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرࣲ **فَكَذَبَتۡ** وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِینَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة يوسف]{.ar} 12:27](https://quran.com/12/27) cited by [معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/105]{.citex}  
    [But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful.]{.trans}  

[قَدْ]{.ar} may also optionally be added.
For example:

(@ex001370) [إِنْ تَطْعَنُوا فِي إِمَارَتِهِ **فَقَدْ** طَعَنْتُمْ فِي إِمَارَةِ أَبِيهِ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :4250](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4250)]{.citex}  
    [If you speak ill of his leadership, you have already spoken ill of his father's leadership before.]{.trans}

<!--
[فَ]{.ar} is also used with [قَتَلَ]{.ar} in the condition-response when a future perfect event is signified.
For example:

-->

<!--
#### The condition uses [كَانَ [قَدْ] قَتَلَ]{.ar} to signify an event which already occurred {.unnumbered}

peled 72--73, wright 2/15

We discuss in section\ () below
that
[كَانَ (قَدْ) قَتَلَ]{.ar}
can be used in the condition to indicate an event which has already occurred.
In such cases,
the condition-response will typically be introduced by [فَ]{.ar}.
For example:
-->

<!--
#### The condition-response-core signifies a event which is expected to definitely occur {.unnumbered}

[فَ]{.ar} can be used to introduce a verbal sentence condition-response.
to make it more independent from the condition,
and to signify that the event indicated by the condition-response is expected to definitely occur
(if the condition is met).
-->

##### The condition-response-verb is preceded by a particle other than [لَمْ]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

When the condition-response-verb is preceded by [لَمْ]{.ar}
then it typically occurs directly in the condition-response without being introduced by [فَ]{.ar}.
But when the verb in the condition-response is preceded by another particle
like [سَ]{.ar}, [سَوْفَ]{.ar}, [مَا]{.ar} or [لَنْ]{.ar},
then a [فَ]{.ar} is required.
For example:

(@ex001371) [إِنْ كُنْتِ بَرِيئَةً **فَسَيُبَرِّئُكِ** اللَّهُ وَإِنْ كُنْتِ أَلْمَمْتِ بِذَنْبٍ فَاسْتَغْفِرِي اللَّهَ وَتُوبِي إِلَيْهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :4690](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4690)]{.citex}  

(@ex001372) [إِن تَسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ سَبۡعِینَ مَرَّةࣰ **فَلَن** یَغۡفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُمۡۚ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة التوبة]{.ar} 9:80](https://quran.com/9/80)]{.citex}  
    [If you should ask forgiveness for them seventy times - never will Allāh forgive them.]{.trans}  

By the way, once [فَ]{.ar} is used as a condition-response-link,
then [مَا]{.ar} may freely be used to negate a verb directly after it in the condition-response.
Remember from @sec-jsh_negating_fil_shart above, that [مَا]{.ar} may not be used to negate
the condition-response-verb (when there is no [فَ]{.ar}).
Here is an example of [مَا]{.ar} negating a verb in the condition-response that is introduced by [فَ]{.ar}:

(@ex001373) [وَمَن تَوَلَّىٰ **فَمَاۤ** أَرۡسَلۡنَـٰكَ عَلَیۡهِمۡ حَفِیظࣰا]{.quran}
    [[[سورة النساء]{.ar} 4:80](https://quran.com/4/80)]{.citex}  
    [but those who turn away - We have not sent you over them as a guardian.]{.trans}

In example (@ex001373) above, [فَ]{.ar} is analyzed as a condition-response-link
and [مَا]{.ar} after it negates the [mADI]{.trn2} verb [أَرْسَلَ]{.ar}.^[[[الجدول في إعراب القرآن لمحمود صافي]{.ar} for [سورة النساء]{.ar} 4:80](https://tafsir.app/aljadwal/4/80)]

[فَ]{.ar} is typically not used to introduce condition-responses that begin with [لَمْ]{.ar}.
However, some grammarians disagreed and allowed it.^[See [[الكشاف للزمخشري]{.ar} for [سورة الأنفال]{.ar} 8:17](https://tafsir.app/kashaf/8/17) [فَلَمۡ تَقۡتُلُوهُمۡ]{.quran}]

<!--
Emphasis is on the occurrence (or non-occurrence) of condition-response.
[فَ]{.ar} is then needed to indicate that even though emphasis is on the occurrence of condition-response,
it is still linked to condition.

#### Summary {.unnumbered}

Generally, [فَ]{.ar} is added to the condition-response,
when it may not be apparent that condition-response is linked to condition.
So [فَ]{.ar} makes it obvious.
-->

<!--
### [فَ]{.ar} in the condition-response for [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentences
-->

### Flexibility of allowing or dropping [فَ]{.ar}

In @sec-jsh_examples_of_iqtiran_fa above, we listed the main scenarios where [فَ]{.ar}
is used as a condition-response-link.
In this section,
we will give some examples
where [فَ]{.ar} would seem to be required but is dropped,
and conversely, where [فَ]{.ar} would seem to be disallowed but is added.
Grammarians have analyzed these and similar examples either
by [taqdIr]{.trn2}ing
or by relaxing the rules to allow flexibility in having [فَ]{.ar} as a condition-response-link.^[See [اقتران الفاء في جواب الشرط وعدمها في التعبير القراني]{.ar} for a survey of the different opinions held by the grammarians.]

#### The condition-response is a nounal sentence {.unnumbered}

(@ex001374) [مَن يَفعلِ الحَسَناتِ اللهُ يَشْكُرُها]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/65](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/918)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever does good deeds, Allāh will thank them.]{.trans}

In example (@ex001374) above,
the condition-response
[اللهُ يَشْكُرُها]{.ar}
is a nounal sentence but it does not begin with a [فَ]{.ar}.
Some allow this by poetic license only^[See [[النحو الوافي]{.ar} 4/465](https://shamela.ws/book/10641/2392#p1)]
while others allow it generally.^[See [[شواهد التوضيح لابن مالك]{.ar} 192](https://shamela.ws/book/98123/189#p1)]

(@ex001375) [وَإِنۡ أَطَعۡتُمُوهُمۡ إِنَّكُمۡ لَمُشۡرِكُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الأنعام]{.ar} 6:121](https://quran.com/6/121)]{.citex}  
    [And if you were to obey them, indeed, you would be associators [of others with Him].]{.trans}

In example (@ex001375) above,
there is no [فَ]{.ar} before
[إِنَّكُمۡ لَمُشۡرِكُونَ]{.quran}.
In order to reconcile this,
some have [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed a deleted oath
(see @sec-jsh_qasam below),
such that
[إِنَّكُمۡ لَمُشۡرِكُونَ]{.quran}
is not the condition-response but a oath-response.^[[[البحر المحيط لأبي حيان]{.ar} for [سورة الأنعام]{.ar} 6:121](https://tafsir.app/albahr-almuheet/6/121)]

(@ex001376) [إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَرَكْتَ وَلَدَكَ أَغْنِيَاءَ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَنْ تَتْرُكَهُمْ عَالَةً]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6733](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6733) cited by [[شواهد التوضيح لابن مالك]{.ar} 192](https://shamela.ws/book/98123/189#p1) see footnote 918]{.citex}  
    [Indeed if you leave your offspring wealthy, [then it] is better than that you leave them poor.]{.trans}

In example (@ex001376) above
a deleted
[فَهُوَ]{.ar}
is [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed in the condition-response,^[[[شواهد التوضيح لابن مالك]{.ar} 192](https://shamela.ws/book/98123/189#p1)]
thus:
[إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَرَكْتَ وَلَدَكَ أَغْنِيَاءَ **فَهُوَ** خَيْرٌ]{.ar}.

#### The condition-response is a command {.unnumbered}

(@ex001377) [فَإِنْ جَاءَ صَاحِبُهَا وَإِلاَّ اسْتَمْتِعْ بِهَا]{.ar}  
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :2437](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2437)  cited by [[شواهد التوضيح لابن مالك]{.ar} 192](https://shamela.ws/book/98123/189#p1); [[النحو الوافي]{.ar} 4/466 footnote](https://shamela.ws/book/10641/2393#p1)]{.citex}  
    [Then if its owner comes [then give it to him], and if not [then] utilize it]{.trans}

In example (@ex001377) above the condition-response is a verb of command but it is not preceded by a [فَ]{.ar}.
The above [HadIv]{.trn2} has also been narrated with a [فَ]{.ar} before the verb of command:

(@ex001378) [فَإِنْ جَاءَ صَاحِبُهَا، وَإِلاَّ فَاسْتَمْتِعْ بِهَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :2426](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2426)   cited by [[شواهد التوضيح لابن مالك]{.ar} 192 footnote 919](https://shamela.ws/book/98123/189#p1)]{.citex}  
    [Then if its owner comes [then give it to him], and if not then utilize it]{.trans}

#### The condition-response begins with a u-case [muDArie]{.trn2} verb {.unnumbered}

When the condition-response is a u-case [muDArie]{.trn2} verb,
then it is common for it to be preceded by [فَ]{.ar}.
For example:

(@ex001379) [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي فَأُكْرِمُكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/69](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/922)]{.citex}  
    [If you come to me then I will honor you.]{.trans}

(@ex001380) [وَمَنۡ عَادَ فَیَنتَقِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنۡهُۚ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة المائدة]{.ar} 5:95](https://quran.com/5/95) cited by [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/69](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/922)]{.citex}  
    [but whoever returns [to violation], then Allāh will take retribution from him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001381) [فَمَن یُؤۡمِنۢ بِرَبِّهِۦ فَلَا یَخَافُ بَخۡسࣰا وَلَا رَهَقࣰا]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الجن]{.ar} 72:13](https://quran.com/72/13) cited by [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/69](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/922)]{.citex}  
    [And whoever believes in his Lord will not fear deprivation or burden.]{.trans}  


In such cases, some grammarians have treated [فَ]{.ar} as being allowed because of a deleted subject
such that the [taqdIr]{.trn2} of
[إِنْ تَأْتِنِي فَأُكْرِمُكَ]{.ar}
in example (@ex001379) above
is
[فَأَنَا أُكْرِمُكَ]{.ar}.^[[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/69](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/922)]
Others did not see the need for such [taqdIr]{.trn2}.^[[[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 4/112](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=4&page=1549&index=150957/150973) citing [المبرد]{.ar}; See also [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/109](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1214)]

[فَ]{.ar} may also be omitted in such sentences.
We have already seen some examples where
the u-case [muDArie]{.trn2} verb in the condition-response does not begin with [فَ]{.ar}
in @sec-j_sh_jawab_ucase_wo_fa
above.
For convenience,
we repeat here the examples we had given there:

(@ex001382) [إن أتيتني آتيك]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/66](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/919#p1)]{.citex}  
    [If you come to me, I come to you.]{.trans}  

(@ex001383) [**وإن أتاه** خليلٌ يومَ مسألةٍ **يقولُ** لا غائبٌ مالي ولا حَرِمُ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/66](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/919#p1)]{.citex}  
    [And if a friend came to him on a day of asking, he says, "My wealth is neither absent nor denied."]{.trans}

(@ex001384) [يا أَقْرَعُ بنَ حابسٍ يا أَقْرَعُ ~ إنَّك **إن يُصْرَعْ أخوك تُصْرَعُ**]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/67](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/920#p1)]{.citex}  
    [O [#aqrae]{.trn2} son of [#HAbis]{.trn2}, O [#aqrae]{.trn2}! Indeed if your brother would be thrown down, you are being thrown down.]{.trans}  

(@ex001385) [قَالَتِ اللَّهُمَّ **إِنْ يَمُتْ يُقَالُ** هِيَ قَتَلَتْهُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :2217](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2217) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 17]{.citex}  
    [She said, "O Allāh if he should die, it will be said, 'She killed him.'"]{.trans}  

#### The condition-response is a question

When the condition-response is a question, then [فَ]{.ar} is often omitted.
This is usual when the question-device is [أَ]{.ar}
but other question-devices may also occur in this manner.^[[[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 4/113](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=4&page=1550&index=150957/150973)]
Here are some examples:

(@ex001386) [أَءِذَا مِتۡنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابࣰا وَعِظَـٰمًا **أَءِنَّا** لَمَبۡعُوثُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الصافات]{.ar} 37:16](https://quran.com/37/16)]{.citex}  
    [When we have died and become dust and bones, are we indeed to be resurrected?]{.trans}  

(@ex001387) [قُلۡ أَرَءَیۡتَكُمۡ إِنۡ أَتَىٰكُمۡ عَذَابُ ٱللَّهِ بَغۡتَةً أَوۡ جَهۡرَةً **هَلۡ** یُهۡلَكُ إِلَّا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلظَّـٰلِمُونَ]{.quran}  
    [[[سورة الأنعام]{.ar} 6:47](https://quran.com/6/47) cited by [[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 4/113](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=4&page=1550&index=150957/150973)]{.citex}  
    [Say, "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allāh should come to you unexpectedly or manifestly, will any be destroyed but the wrongdoing people?"]{.trans}  

(@ex001388) [قُلۡ أَرَءَیۡتُمۡ إِنۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ سَمۡعَكُمۡ وَأَبۡصَـٰرَكُمۡ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِكُم **مَّنۡ** إِلَـٰهٌ غَیۡرُ ٱللَّهِ یَأۡتِیكُم بِهِۗ ٱنظُرۡ كَیۡفَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلۡـَٔایَـٰتِ ثُمَّ هُمۡ یَصۡدِفُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الأنعام]{.ar} 6:46](https://quran.com/6/46) cited by [[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 4/113](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=4&page=1550&index=150957/150973)]{.citex}  
    [Say, "Have you considered: if Allāh should take away your hearing and your sight and set a seal upon your hearts, which deity other than Allāh could bring them [back] to you?"]{.trans}  
    
But
[فَ]{.ar} may also be admitted when the
the condition-response is a question.
For example:

(@ex001389) [قَالَ یَـٰقَوۡمِ أَرَءَیۡتُمۡ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَیِّنَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّی وَءَاتَىٰنِی مِنۡهُ رَحۡمَةࣰ **فَمَن** یَنصُرُنِی مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِنۡ عَصَیۡتُهُۥۖ]{.quran}  
    [[[سورة هود]{.ar} 11:63](https://quran.com/11/63) cited by [[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 4/113](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=4&page=1550&index=150957/150973)]{.citex}  
    [He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I should be upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself, who would protect me from Allāh if I disobeyed Him?]{.trans}  

## Alternate condition-response-links

### Sudden-[إِذَا]{.ar}


When the condition-response begins with [فَ]{.ar},
then it can be replaced with a sudden-[إِذَا]{.ar},
when the meaning of suddenness is appropriate,
and when the folloing conditions are satisfied^[[[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/115](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1220)]:

1. The condition-response must be a nounal sentence, not a verbal sentence.
1. The condition-response must be affirmative, not negative.
1. The condition-response must be truth-evaluable.
1. The condition-response must not begin with [إِنَّ]{.ar}.

Here is an example of a conditional sentence
that satisfies these conditions:

(@ex001390) [وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱلَّذِینَ مِن دُونِهِۦۤ إِذَا هُمۡ یَسۡتَبۡشِرُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الزمر]{.ar} 39:45](https://quran.com/39/45) cited by [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/115](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1220)]{.citex}  
    [but when those [worshipped] other than Him are mentioned, immediately they rejoice.]{.trans}

### [إِذَنْ]{.ar}


The particle
[إِذَنْ]{.ar}
[in that case]{.trans}
can be inserted between a condition
and a condition-response.
So it can be considered a condition-response-link.
But
it will have no affect on the condition-response-verb,
which can continue to be in the ø-case.^[See also [مغني اللبيب لابن هشام]{.ar} 1/20]

It does not take the place of [فَ]{.ar} like sudden-[إِذَا]{.ar},
so it can be used in conditional sentences which don't allow [فَ]{.ar} as a condition-response-link.

For example:

(@ex001391) [إِنْ تَزُرْنِي إِذَنْ أُكْرِمْكَ]{.ar}
    [[[ارتشاف الضرب من لسان العرب]{.ar} 4/1652](https://shamela.ws/book/16595/1649)]{.citex}  
    [If you visit me, in that case I will honor you.]{.trans}


## The [لَوْ]{.ar} conditional sentence {#sec-jsh_law}

The third main conditional-device used,
after [إِنْ]{.ar} and [إِذَا]{.ar},
is [لَوْ]{.ar}.
In terms of its classification as a word,
[لَوْ]{.ar} is a particle, like [إِنْ]{.ar},
and unlike [إِذَا]{.ar}, which is a noun.
In terms of its meaning,
[لَوْ]{.ar} typically forms a different sort of conditional sentence
than [إِنْ]{.ar} and [إِذَا]{.ar},
and therefore it is generally treated separately.

[لَوْ]{.ar}
is most commonly used to form
past and present
_counterfactual_
conditional sentences.
Less commonly, it is also used to form
future _hypothetical_ conditional sentences.^[Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 40]
Here are examples of such conditional sentences in English:

(@ex001392) [If you had been awake, you would have heard the coyote.]{.trans}
    [Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 40]{.citex}  
    This is a past counterfactual. The implication is that the addressed person was not awake. So his being awake is counter to fact.

(@ex001393) [If I were a boy, I would have curls.]{.trans}
    [Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 40]{.citex}  
    This is a present counterfactual. The implication is that the speaker is not a boy. So her being a boy is counter to fact.

(@ex001394) [If he ate all those doughnuts, he would be ill.]{.trans}
    [Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 40]{.citex}  
    This is a future hypothetical. This is similar to the kind of conditional sentence where [إِنْ]{.ar} is used but it is more _imaginative_.

We will cover the use of [لَوْ]{.ar} in such conditional sentences in the following subsections.

### The basic structure of a [لَوْ]{.ar} conditional sentence

The archetypal [لَوْ]{.ar} conditional sentence typically has the form

(@ex001395) [لَوْ قَتَلَ لَقَتَلَ]{.ar}

where [لَ]{.ar} is the (optional) condition-response-link.
Here is an example of a [لَوْ]{.ar} conditional sentence:

(@ex001396) [لَوْ جِئْتَنِي لَأَكْرَمْتُكَ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/105](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2043)]{.citex}  
    [If you had come to me, I would have honored you.]{.trans}  

As you can see, the meaning of the [لَوْ]{.ar} conditional sentence is,
by default,
a past counterfactual.
In example (@ex001396) above,
the implication is that you had not come to me.
So the condition never occurred.

Out of context, and sometimes even in context,
both a counterfactual and a hypothtical meaning can be understood.^[Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 44--45]
For example:

(@ex001397) [لَوْ كَانَ عِنْدَنَا مَالٌ لَأَعْطَيْتُكَ]{.ar}
    [cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 45]{.citex}  
    [If we had (or were to have) money, we would have (or would) give you.]{.trans}  


Here are some more examples of basic [لَوْ]{.ar} conditional sentences:

(@ex001398) [**لَوْ** جِئْتَ بِهَا بِالأَمْسِ **لَقَبِلْتُهَا** فَأَمَّا الْيَوْمَ فَلاَ حَاجَةَ لِي بِهَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :1411](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1411) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 43]{.citex}  
    [Had you brought it to me yesterday I would have accepted it. But as for today, then I have no need for it.]{.trans}  

(@ex001399) [**لَوْ** أُوتِيتُ مِثْلَ مَا أُوتِيَ هَذَا **لَفَعَلْتُ** كَمَا يَفْعَلُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :7232](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7232)]{.citex}  
    [If I had been given similar to what this [person] has been given, I would do similar to what he does.]{.trans}  

(@ex001400) [**لَوْ** دُعِيتُ إِلَى كُرَاعٍ **لأَجَبْتُ وَلَوْ** أُهْدِيَ إِلَىَّ ذِرَاعٌ **لَقَبِلْتُ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :5178](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5178)]{.citex}  
    [If I were invited to [a meal of] trotters, I would respond. And if forelegs were gifted to me I would accept.]{.trans}

(@ex001401) [**لَوْ** لَبِثْتُ فِي السِّجْنِ مَا لَبِثَ يُوسُفُ ثُمَّ أَتَانِي الدَّاعِي **لأَجَبْتُهُ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6992](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6992)]{.citex}  
    [If I stayed in prison as long as [#yUsuf]{.trn2} stayed, then the summoner came to me, I would have responded to him (to leave the prison).]{.trans}  

(@ex001402) [**لَوْ** أَدْرَكَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَا أَحْدَثَ النِّسَاءُ **لَمَنَعَهُنَّ** كَمَا مُنِعَتْ نِسَاءُ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :869](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:869)]{.citex}  
    [Had the Messenger of Allāh [ﷺ]{.areng} come across what the women have started doing, he would have forbidden them like the women of the Children of [#isrAEIl]{.trn2} were forbidden.]{.trans}  

### Optionality of [لَ]{.ar} in the condition-response

While [لَ]{.ar} is often used as a condition-response-link it is optional and may be dropped.
Here are some examples with and without [لَ]{.ar}:
<!--
Here are some more examples of the basic [لَوْ]{.ar} conditional sentence.
As you can see the condition-response-link [لَ]{.ar} is common but optional.
-->

(@ex001403) [إِنِّي لأَعْلَمُ كَلِمَةً لَوْ قَالَهَا **ذَهَبَ** عَنْهُ مَا يَجِدُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3282](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3282)]{.citex}  
    [Indeed I know a phrase, if he were to say it, what he feels will go away from  him.]{.trans}

(@ex001404) [إِنِّي لأَعْلَمُ كَلِمَةً لَوْ قَالَهَا **لَذَهَبَ** عَنْهُ مَا يَجِدُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6115](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6115)]{.citex}  
    [Indeed I know a phrase, if he were to say it, what he feels will go away from  him.]{.trans}


(@ex001405) [إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يَقُولُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ مَرِضْتُ فَلَمْ تَعُدْنِي قَالَ يَا رَبِّ كَيْفَ أَعُودُكَ وَأَنْتَ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ قَالَ أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ عَبْدِي فُلاَنًا مَرِضَ فَلَمْ تَعُدْهُ أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّكَ لَوْ عُدْتَهُ **لَوَجَدْتَنِي** عِنْدَهُ يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ اسْتَطْعَمْتُكَ فَلَمْ تُطْعِمْنِي  قَالَ يَا رَبِّ وَكَيْفَ أُطْعِمُكَ وَأَنْتَ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ  قَالَ أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّهُ اسْتَطْعَمَكَ عَبْدِي فُلاَنٌ فَلَمْ تُطْعِمْهُ أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّكَ لَوْ أَطْعَمْتَهُ **لَوَجَدْتَ** ذَلِكَ عِنْدِي يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ اسْتَسْقَيْتُكَ فَلَمْ تَسْقِنِي قَالَ يَا رَبِّ كَيْفَ أَسْقِيكَ وَأَنْتَ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ قَالَ اسْتَسْقَاكَ عَبْدِي فُلاَنٌ فَلَمْ تَسْقِهِ أَمَا إِنَّكَ لَوْ سَقَيْتَهُ **وَجَدْتَ** ذَلِكَ عِنْدِي]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :2569](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2569)]{.citex}  
    [Verily, Allāh, the Exalted and Glorious, would say on the Day of Resurrection: O son of Adam, I was sick but you did not visit Me. He would say: O my Lord; how could I visit You whereas You are the Lord of the worlds? Thereupon He would say: Didn't you know that such and such servant of Mine was sick but you did not visit him and were you not aware of this that if you had visited him, **you would have found Me** by him? O son of Adam, I asked food from you but you did not feed Me. He would say: My Lord, how could I feed You whereas You are the Lord of the worlds? He said: Didn't you know that such and such servant of Mine asked food from you but you did not feed him, and were you not aware that if you had fed him **you would have found** him by My side? (The Lord would again say: ) O son of Adam, I asked drink from you but you did not provide Me. He would say: My Lord, how could I provide You whereas You are the Lord of the worlds? Thereupon He would say: Such and such of servant of Mine asked you for a drink but you did not provide him, and had you provided him drink **you would have found** him near Me.]{.trans}

(@ex001406) [أُمِّي افْتُلِتَتْ نَفْسَهَا، وَأُرَاهَا لَوْ تَكَلَّمَتْ **تَصَدَّقَتْ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :2760](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2760)]{.citex}  
    [My mother died suddenly and I think that if she had spoken she would have given in charity.]{.trans}

(@ex001407) [لَوۡ نَشَاۤءُ لَجَعَلۡنَـٰهُ حُطَـٰمࣰا]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الواقعة]{.ar} 56:65](https://quran.com/56/65) cited by [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/92](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1197)]{.citex}  
    [If We willed, We could make it [dry] debris]{.trans}

(@ex001408) [لَوۡ نَشَاۤءُ جَعَلۡنَـٰهُ أُجَاجࣰا]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الواقعة]{.ar} 56:70](https://quran.com/56/70) cited by [[معاني النحو]{.ar} 4/92](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/1197)]{.citex}  
    [If We willed, We could make it bitter]{.trans}

### [قَدْ]{.ar} before the condition-verb or the condition-response-verb

As shown in example (@ex001396) above,
the basic form of the [لَوْ]{.ar} conditional sentence is
[لَوْ قَتَلَ لَقَتَلَ]{.ar}.
Rarely, a [قَدْ]{.ar} may be inserted before the condition-verb and/or the condition-response-verb.^[[[شرح الفارضي على ألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 4/64](https://ftp.shamela.ws/book/174/1756)]
For example:

(@ex001409) [لَوْ **قَدْ** جَاءَ مَالُ الْبَحْرَيْنِ **لَقَدْ** أَعْطَيْتُكَ هَكَذَا وَهَكَذَا ثَلاَثًا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :4383](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4383)]{.citex}  
    [If the money of [al-#baHrayn]{.trn2} should come, I will give you such-and-such ([repeating such-and-such] thrice).]{.trans}

[قَدْ]{.ar} may even be used in the condition-response without [لَ]{.ar}.
For example:

(@ex001410) [لَوْ قَدْ جَاءَ مَالُ الْبَحْرَيْنِ **قَدْ** أَعْطَيْتُكَ هَكَذَا وَهَكَذَا وَهَكَذَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :2296](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2296)]{.citex}  
    [If the money of [al-#baHrayn]{.trn2} should come, I will give you such-and-such.]{.trans}

Furthermore, the context of examples (@ex001409) and (@ex001410) above,
indicates a future hypothetical tense.
So [قَدْ]{.ar},
used in this way,
does not necessarily restrict the tense to the past.

### Negating the condition-verb

For negating the condition-verb, [لَمْ]{.ar} is used thus:

(@ex001411) [لَوْ لَمْ يَقْتُلْ\ ...]{.ar}

[لَوْلَا]{.ar} and [لَوْمَا]{.ar} are also used in negative conditional sentences but we will treat them separately in @sec-jsh_law_laa below.

Here are some examples of the condition-verb being negated with [لَمْ]{.ar}:

(@ex001412) [لَوْ **لَمْ تُذْنِبُوا** لَذَهَبَ اللَّهُ بِكُمْ وَلَجَاءَ بِقَوْمٍ يُذْنِبُونَ فَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ اللَّهَ فَيَغْفِرُ لَهُمْ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :2749](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2749)]{.citex}  
    [If you were not to sin Allāh would do away with you and He would bring a people who would sin and seek forgiveness from Allāh, and He would forgive them.]{.trans}  

(@ex001413) [أَمَا إِنَّكِ لَوْ **لَمْ تُعْطِيهِ** شَيْئًا كُتِبَتْ عَلَيْكِ كِذْبَةٌ]{.ar}
    [[[سنن أبي داود]{.ar} :4991](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4991)]{.citex}  
    [If you were not to give him anything, a lie would be recorded against you.]{.trans}  

(@ex001414) [أَمَا إِنَّكَ لَوْ **لَمْ تَفْعَلْ** لَلَفَعَتْكَ النَّارُ أَوْ لَمَسَّتْكَ النَّارُ]{.ar}
    [[[سنن أبي داود]{.ar} :5159](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5159)]{.citex}  
    [If you hadn't done [so], the fire would have enveloped you or the fire would have touched you.]{.trans}

(@ex001415) [لَوْ **لَمْ أَحْتَضِنْهُ** لَحَنَّ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ]{.ar}
    [[[سنن ابن ماجه]{.ar} :1415](https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:1415)]{.citex}  
    [Had I not embraced it, it would have cried yearning until the Day of Resurrection.]{.trans}  

<!--
(@ex001416) [لَوْ لَمْ أَسْمَعْ بِهَذَا لَقَضَيْنَا بِغَيْرِ هَذَا]{.ar}
    [[[سنن أبي داود]{.ar} :4573](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4573)]{.citex}  
    [Had I not heard of it we would have decreed something else.]{.trans}
-->
<!--
Remembers from sections () and () that only [لَا]{.ar} and [لَمْ]{.ar} are to negate the
condition-verb and the condition-response-verb for [إِنْ]{.ar} and [إِذَا]{.ar} conditional sentences.
However, for [لَوْ]{.ar} j_sh;s [مَا]{.ar}
-->

### Negating the condition-response-verb

When the condition-response-verb is to be negated, then either [لَمْ]{.ar} or [مَا]{.ar} can be used.
For the case of [لَمْ]{.ar}, the particle [لَ]{.ar} is not used as a condition-response-link.
For the case of [مَا]{.ar}, the particle [لَ]{.ar} is optional but it is almost always dropped.
Here are some examples:

(@ex001417) [لَوْ قَالَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ **لَمْ يَحْنَثْ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6720](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6720)]{.citex}  
    [If he had said, "If Allāh wills," he would not have been unsuccessful.]{.trans}  

(@ex001418) [لَوْ لَمْ أَرَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَسْجُدُ **لَمْ أَسْجُدْ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :1074](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1074)]{.citex}  
    [Had I not seen the Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} prostrating I would not have prostrated.]{.trans}

(@ex001419) [لَوِ اسْتَقْبَلْتُ مِنْ أَمْرِي مَا اسْتَدْبَرْتُ **مَا سُقْتُ** الْهَدْىَ، وَلَحَلَلْتُ مَعَ النَّاسِ حِينَ حَلُّوا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :7229](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7229)]{.citex}  
    [Had I known earlier of my affair what I knew later, I would not have driven my sacrificial animal and I would have exited [#iHrAm]{.trn2} with the people when they exited [#iHrAm]{.trn2}.]{.trans}  

(@ex001420) [إِنِّي لأَظُنُّ رَجُلاً لَوْ لَمْ يَطُفْ بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ **مَا ضَرَّهُ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :1277a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1277a)]{.citex}  
    [Indeed I think that if a man were not to go between [al-#SafA]{.trn2} and [al-#marwah]{.trn2} it would not harm him.]{.trans}  

<!--
Here are examples with both the condition-verb and the condition-response-verb being negated:
-->

Finally, here is a rare example of [لَمَا]{.ar} in the condition-response:

(@ex001421) [لَوْ وَجَدَنِي نَائِمًا **لَمَا أَيْقَظَنِي**]{.ar}
    [[[سيرة ابن هشام]{.ar} 2/56](https://shamela.ws/book/23833/793) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 51]{.citex}  
    [If he had found me sleeping, he would not have woken me.]{.trans}  

A different version of the same sentence without [لَ]{.ar} is also found:

(@ex001422) [وَاللهِ لَوْ وَجَدَنِي نَائِمًا **مَا أَيْقَظَنِي**]{.ar}
    [[[مغازي الواقدي]{.ar} 1/189](https://shamela.ws/book/23680/230) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 51]{.citex}  
    [By Allāh if he had found me sleeping, he would not have woken me.]{.trans}  

### [كَانَ]{.ar} in the condition or the condition-response

The verb [كَانَ]{.ar} can be used as the condition-verb.
This can be for a few purposes

[كَانَ]{.ar} can be used to transform nounal sentences so that they can be used in the condition.
Here are some examples:

(@ex001423) [لَوْ **كَانَ** الْمُطْعِمُ بْنُ عَدِيٍّ حَيًّا، ثُمَّ كَلَّمَنِي فِي هَؤُلاَءِ النَّتْنَى، لَتَرَكْتُهُمْ لَهُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3139](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3139)]{.citex}  
    [If [al-#muTeim ibn #eadiyy]{.trn2} were alive and he spoke to me regarding these mean people, I would have left them to him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001424) [لَوْ **كَانَ** لاِبْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيَانِ مِنْ مَالٍ لاَبْتَغَى ثَالِثًا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6436](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6436)]{.citex}  
    [If the son of [#adam]{.trn2} had two valleys of wealth, he would want a third.]{.trans}  

Here are some examples of [لَوْ كَانَ قَتَلَ]{.ar} to signify a past counterfactual:

(@ex001425) [لَوْ **كُنْتَ قُلْتَهَا** لَكَانَ أَحَبَّ إِلَىَّ مِنْ كَذَا وَكَذَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6122](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6122)]{.citex}  
    [If you had said it, it would have been more beloved to me than such-and-such.]{.trans}

(@ex001426) [لَوْ **كُنْتُ سَمِعْتُهُ** قَبْلَ أَنْ أَهْدِمَهُ لَتَرَكْتُهُ عَلَى مَا بَنَى ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :1333i](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1333i)]{.citex}  
    [If I had heard it before demolishing it, I would have left it [in the state] that Ibn [al-#zubayr]{.trn2} built [it].]{.trans}  

(@ex001427) [لَوْ **كُنْتِ أَعْطَيْتِهَا** أَخْوَالَكِ كَانَ أَعْظَمَ لأَجْرِكِ]{.ar}
    [[[سنن أبي داود]{.ar} :1690](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1690)]{.citex}  
    [If you had given her to your maternal uncles, it would have been greater for your reward.]{.trans}  

Here are some examples of [لَوْ كَانَ يَقْتُلُ]{.ar} to signify a progressive counterfactual:

(@ex001428) [وَقَالُوا۟ لَوۡ **كُنَّا نَسۡمَعُ** أَوۡ نَعۡقِلُ مَا كُنَّا فِیۤ أَصۡحَـٰبِ ٱلسَّعِیرِ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الملك]{.ar} 67:10](https://quran.com/67/10)]{.citex}  
    [And they will say, "If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze."]{.trans}  

(@ex001429) [لَوْ **كُنْتُ أُبْصِرُ** لأَرَيْتُكُمْ مَوْضِعَ الشَّجَرَةِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :1856e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1856e)]{.citex}  
    [If I were seeing (i.e. had sight) I would show you the place of the tree.]{.trans}  

The combination of [كَانَ]{.ar} and a doer participle is very commonly used to indicate a hypothetical situation.
Here are some examples:

(@ex001430) [لَوْ **كُنْتُ مُتَّخِذًا** خَلِيلاً لاَتَّخَذْتُهُ خَلِيلاً وَلَكِنْ أُخُوَّةُ الإِسْلاَمِ أَفْضَلُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3657](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3657)]{.citex}  
    [Were I to take a close friend, I would have taken [[#abU #bakr]{.trn2}] as a close friend. But the brotherhood of [#islAm]{.trn2} is better.]{.trans}

(@ex001431) [لَوْ **كُنْتُ رَاجِمًا** أَحَدًا بِغَيْرِ بَيِّنَةٍ لَرَجَمْتُهَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :1497c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1497c)]{.citex}  
    [If I were to stone anyone without evidence, I would have stoned her.]{.trans}  

Oftentimes, different expressions,
with and without [كَانَ]{.ar},
can be used for the same meaning.
For example:

(@ex001432) [لَوْ **كُنْتُ آمِرًا** أَحَدًا أَنْ يَسْجُدَ لأَحَدٍ لأَمَرْتُ الْمَرْأَةَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِزَوْجِهَا]{.ar}
    [[[جامع الترمذي]{.ar} :1159](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:1159)]{.citex}  
    [If I were to order anyone that they prostrate to another, I would have ordered the woman to prostrate to her spouse.]{.trans}

(@ex001433) [لَوْ **كُنْتُ آمُرُ** أَحَدًا أَنْ يَسْجُدَ لِأَحَدٍ لَأَمَرْتُ الْمَرْأَةَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِزَوْجِهَا]{.ar}
    [[[مسند أحمد]{.ar} :19403](https://hadithunlocked.com/ahmad:19403)]{.citex}  
    [If I were ordering anyone that they prostrate to another, I would have ordered the woman to prostrate to her spouse.]{.trans}

(@ex001434) [لَوْ **أَمَرْتُ** شَيْئًا أَنْ يَسْجُدَ لِشَيْءٍ لَأَمَرْتُ الْمَرْأَةَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِزَوْجِهَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح ابن حبان]{.ar} :4171](https://hadithunlocked.com/ibnhibban:4171)]{.citex}  
    [If I were to order anything that they prostrate to [another] thing, I would have ordered the woman to prostrate to her spouse.]{.trans}

[كَانَ]{.ar} can also be used with [لَوْ]{.ar} for an impersonal condition:

(@ex001435) [لَوْ **كُنْتُ أَنَا** لَمْ أُحَرِّقْهُمْ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3017](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3017)]{.citex}  
    [If it were I, I would not have burned them.]{.trans}  


<!--
Hypothetical.
Allows nounal sentence.

peled 44 (9), 45 (10) (12)
-->

[كَانَ]{.ar} is also used as the condition-response-verb.
Here are some examples
of [كَانَ]{.ar}
as the condition-response-verb.
allowing a nounal sentence in the condition-response:


(@ex001436) [لَوْ رَأَوْكَ **كَانُوا** أَشَدَّ لَكَ عِبَادَةً]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6408](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6408)]{.citex}  
    [If they were to see you they would be more devout to you in worship.]{.trans}  

(@ex001437) [قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَرْحَمُ اللَّهُ أُمَّ إِسْمَاعِيلَ لَوْ تَرَكَتْ زَمْزَمَ أَوْ قَالَ لَوْ لَمْ تَغْرِفْ مِنَ الْمَاءِ **لَكَانَتْ** عَيْنًا مَعِينًا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :2368](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2368)]{.citex}  
    [The Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} said, "May Allāh have mercy on the mother of [#ismAeIl]{.trn2}. Had she left Zamzam"---or he said, "Had she not scooped from the water"---"it would have been a flowing spring."]{.trans}

### [لَوْ أَنَّ]{.ar}

[لَوْ]{.ar} is frequently followed,
not by a verb,
but by an [أَنَّ]{.ar} clause.
For example:

(@ex001438) [لَوْ **أَنَّ زَيْدًا جَاءَ** لَأَكْرَمْتُهُ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 4/528](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/1892)]{.citex}  
    [If Zayd had come to me, I would have honored him.]{.trans}  

The grammarians analyze this kind of [لَوْ]{.ar} conditional sentence in two ways^[[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 4/528](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/1892); [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/478]:

a. That the [أَنَّ]{.ar} clause is the doer of a [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed condition-verb that signifies occurrence, like [ثَبَتَ]{.ar} [to be ascertained]{.trans} or [وَقَعَ]{.ar} [to occur]{.trans}. So the [taqdIr]{.trn2} of the above example is:

   (@) [لَوْ **وَقَعَ مَجِيءُ زَيْدٍ** لَأَكْرَمْتُهُ]{.ar}
       [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 4/528](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/1892)]{.citex}  
       [If Zayd's coming had occurred, I would have honored him.]{.trans}  

b. That [لَوْ]{.ar} in this case does not need a condition-verb, and that the [أَنَّ]{.ar} clause is a subject to a [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed info which is a noun like [ثَابِتْ]{.ar} [ascertained]{.trans}. So the [taqdIr]{.trn2} of the above example is:

   (@) [لَوْ **مَجِيءُ زَيْدٍ ثَابِتٌ** لَأَكْرَمْتُهُ]{.ar}  
       [If Zayd's coming [was] ascertained, I would have honored him.]{.trans}  

According to some grammarians,
the info of [أَنَّ]{.ar} should,
in such cases,
be a verb.^[[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/120](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2058)]
So the folloing would be disallowed:

(@) ✗ [لَوْ أَنَّ زَيْدًا حَاضِرِي\ ...]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/120](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2058)]{.citex}  
    [If Zayd were present with me\ ...]{.trans}  

Here are some more examples of [لَوْ أَنَّ]{.ar}:

(@ex001439) [وَلَوۡ **أَنَّهُمۡ** صَبَرُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ تَخۡرُجَ إِلَیۡهِمۡ لَكَانَ خَیۡرࣰا لَّهُمۡۚ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الحجرات]{.ar} 49:5](https://quran.com/49/5) cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/478]{.citex}  
    [And if they had been patient until you [could] come out to them, it would have been better for them.]{.trans}

(@ex001440) [وَلَوۡ **أَنَّهُمۡ** إِذ ظَّلَمُوۤا۟ أَنفُسَهُمۡ جَاۤءُوكَ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱسۡتَغۡفَرَ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ لَوَجَدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابࣰا رَّحِیمࣰا]{.quran}
    [[[سورة النساء]{.ar} 4:64](https://quran.com/4/64)]{.citex}  
    [And if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you, [O Muḥammad], and asked forgiveness of Allāh and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allāh Accepting of Repentance and Merciful.]{.trans}

(@ex001441) [لَوْ **أَنَّ** أَحَدَهُمْ رَفَعَ قَدَمَهُ رَآنَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :4663](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4663)]{.citex}  
    [If one of them should lift his foot, he would see us.]{.trans}

(@ex001442) [لَوْ **أَنَّ** لاِبْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَادِيَانِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6439](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6439)]{.citex}  
    [If the son of [#Adam]{.trn2} had a valley of gold, he would like that he have two valleys.]{.trans}

(@ex001443) [لَوْ **أَنَّ** الأَنْصَارَ سَلَكُوا وَادِيًا أَوْ شِعْبًا، لَسَلَكْتُ فِي وَادِي الأَنْصَارِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3779](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3779)]{.citex}  
    [If the [#anSAr]{.trn2} should take their way through a valley or a ravine, I would take my way in the valley of the [#anSAr]{.trn2}.]{.trans}

(@ex001444) [لَوْ **أَنَّ** أَحَدَكُمْ أَنْفَقَ مِثْلَ أُحُدٍ ذَهَبًا مَا أَدْرَكَ مُدَّ أَحَدِهِمْ وَلاَ نَصِيفَهُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :2540](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2540)]{.citex}  
    [If one of you should spend [the measure of] [#uHud]{.trn2} in gold, it would not reach [the measure of] one of them's [spending] one _mudd_, nor [would it reach] its half.]{.trans}  

### [لَوْلَا]{.ar} and [لَوْمَا]{.ar} {#sec-jsh_law_laa}

[لَوْلَا]{.ar} is a special conditional-device that almost always^[Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 61 cites exceptions in poetry]
precedes a noun in the condition-core.
The noun is treated as a subject and its info is usually deleted.
For example:

(@ex001445) [لَوْلَا زَيْدٌ لَغَرَقْتُ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ألفية ابن مالك للعثيمين]{.ar} 19/3](https://shamela.ws/book/36954/209)]{.citex}  
    [Were it not for Zayd, I would have drowned.]{.trans}  

In example (@ex001445) above, [زَيْدٌ]{.ar} is a subject.
Its info is a deleted noun, whose [taqdIr]{.trn2} is [مَوْجُودٌ]{.ar} or [حَاضِرٌ]{.ar} [present]{.trans} (meaning _there_).
So a possible [taqdIr]{.trn2} of the condition is:

(@ex001446) [لَوْلَا زَيْدٌ مَوْجُودٌ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ألفية ابن مالك للعثيمين]{.ar} 19/3](https://shamela.ws/book/36954/209)]{.citex}  
    [If Zayd were not present\ ...]{.trans}  

[لَوْلَا]{.ar} is frequently also followed by an [أَنَّ]{.ar} (or [أَنْ]{.ar}) clause.
In which case the [أَنَّ]{.ar} clause is treated as the subject.
For example:

(@ex001447) [لَوْلَا أَنَّ زَيْدًا عِنْدِي لَأَتَيْتُكَ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح كتاب سيبويه للسيرافي]{.ar} 3/336](https://shamela.ws/book/17726/1332)]{.citex}  
    [Were it not that Zayd is with me, I would have come to you.]{.trans}  

The info of the noun after is usually but not always deleted.^[[[شرح ألفية ابن مالك للعثيمين]{.ar} 19/3](https://shamela.ws/book/36954/209)]
Here is an example with a info:

(@ex001448) [فَلَوْلَا بَنُوهَا حَوْلَهَا لَخَبَطْتُهَا]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الكافية الشافية لابن مالك]{.ar}](https://shamela.ws/book/12024/359)]{.citex}  
    [Were it not for her sons around her I would have struck her]{.trans}  
    ([حَوْل]{.ar} is technically not the info but a adverb of place governed by a [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed info.)

<!--
(@ex001449) [لولا قومك حديثو عهد بكفر لهدمت الكعبة وبنيتها على قواعد إبراهيم]{.ar}
-->

There is a difference in meaning between [لَوْلَا]{.ar}, and [لَوْ]{.ar} with a negated verb.
Consider the following two examples:

(@ex001450) [لَوْ لَمْ تَضْرِبْنِي لَأَعْطَيْتُكَ الْمَالَ]{.ar}
    [Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 61]{.citex}
    [Had you not beaten me, I would have given you the money.]{.trans}  

(@ex001451) [لَوْلَا أَنَّكَ ضَرَبْتَنِي لَأَعْطَيْتُكَ الْمَالَ]{.ar}
    [Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 61]{.citex}  
    [Were it not that you had beaten me, I would have given you the money.]{.trans}  

Example (@ex001450) above only presupposes the condition, whereas example (@ex001451) asserts it.^[Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 61]

[لَوْمَا]{.ar} is less used than [لَوْلَا]{.ar} but is similar in usage and meaning.
Here are some more examples of [لَوْلَا]{.ar} and [لَوْمَا]{.ar}

(@ex001452) [لَوْلاَ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ لَمْ يَخْنَزِ اللَّحْمُ، وَلَوْلاَ حَوَّاءُ لَمْ تَخُنْ أُنْثَى زَوْجَهَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3330](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3330)]{.citex}  
    [Were it not for the Children of [#isrAEIl]{.trn2}, meat would not decay. And were it not for [#HawwAE]{.trn2}, a female would not betray her spouse.]{.trans}  

(@ex001453) [لَوْلاَ آخِرُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مَا فُتِحَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ قَرْيَةٌ إِلاَّ قَسَمْتُهَا، كَمَا قَسَمَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم خَيْبَرَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :4236](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4236)]{.citex}  
    [Were it not for the latter Muslims, never would a town be conquered except that I would have divided it like the Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} divided [#xaybar]{.trn2}]{.trans}  

(@ex001455) [لَوْلاَ أَنِّي رَأَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَبَّلَكَ مَا قَبَّلْتُكَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :1610](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1610)]{.citex}  
    [Were it not that I saw the Messenger of Allāh had kissed you, I would not have kissed you.]{.trans}  

(@ex001456) [وَلَوۡلَاۤ أَن كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَیۡهِمُ ٱلۡجَلَاۤءَ لَعَذَّبَهُمۡ فِی ٱلدُّنۡیَاۖ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الحشر]{.ar} 59:3](https://quran.com/59/3)]{.citex}  
    [And if not that Allāh had decreed for them evacuation, He would have punished them in [this] world]{.trans}  

(@ex001457) [لَوْلاَ أَنْ تَكُونَ صَدَقَةً لأَكَلْتُهَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :1071c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1071c)]{.citex}  
    [Were it not that it may be charity, I would have eaten it.]{.trans}

(@ex001458) [لَوْلاَ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَى أُمَّتِي لأَمَرْتُهُمْ بِالسِّوَاكِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :7240](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7240)]{.citex}  
    [Were it not that I may make it hard on my nation, I would have ordered them to use the [siwAk]{.trn2}.]{.trans}

(@ex001454) [لَوْلاَ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَهَانَا أَنْ نَدْعُوَ بِالْمَوْتِ لَدَعَوْتُ بِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6350](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6350)]{.citex}  
    [Were it not that the Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} had forbidden us to invoke [Allāh] for death, I would have invoked [Allāh] for it.]{.trans}

Here is an example with [لَوْمَا]{.ar}:

(@ex001459) [لَوْمَا أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَهَانَا أَنْ نَدْعُوَ بِالْمَوْتِ لَدَعَوْتُ بِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :2681a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2681a)]{.citex}  
    [Were it not that the Messenger of Allāh [ﷺ]{.areng} had forbidden us to invoke [Allāh] for death, I would have invoked [Allāh] for it.]{.trans}

#### [لَوْلَا]{.ar} as a question-device {.unnumbered}

[لَوْلَا]{.ar} is also used as a question-device to me [why not]{.trans}.
For example:

(@ex001460) [لَوْلاَ مَتَّعْتَنَا بِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6331](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6331)]{.citex}  
    [Why didn't you let us enjoy him?]{.trans}  

In this case we won't consider it a conditional-device.

<!--
### A condition-core beginning with a noun

FIXME: perhaps combine with the other section and move to top-level after [لَوْ]{.ar}

In a manner similar to what we discussed in section () above,
the condition-core of [لَوْ]{.ar} may occasionally begin with a noun.
For example:

(@ex001461) [قَالَ أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ بْنُ الْجَرَّاحِ أَفِرَارًا مِنْ قَدَرِ اللَّهِ فَقَالَ عُمَرُ **لَوْ غَيْرُكَ قَالَهَا** يَا أَبَا عُبَيْدَةَ، نَعَمْ نَفِرُّ مِنْ قَدَرِ اللَّهِ إِلَى قَدَرِ اللَّهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :5729](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5729)]{.citex}  
    [[#abU #eubaydah ibn al-#jarrAH]{.trn2} said, "Are you fleeing what Allāh has ordained?" [#eumar]{.trn2} said, "**Would that someone else had said [such a thing]**, O [#abU #eubaydah]{.trn2}! Yes, we are fleeing from what Allah has ordained to what Allah has ordained."]{.trans}
-->

<!--
### [لَوْ]{.ar} with the meaning of [إِنْ]{.ar}
-->

### A u-case [muDArie]{.trn2} condition-verb

The condition-verb in [لَوْ]{.ar} conditional sentences is typically of the form [قَتَلَ]{.ar}.
Sometimes, however, the [يَقْتُلُ]{.ar} form is also found, particularly
(but not exclusively)
when the condition-verb is [يَعْلَمُ]{.ar}.^[Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 57]
Here are some examples:

(@ex001462) [لَوۡ **یُطِیعُكُمۡ** فِی كَثِیرࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ لَعَنِتُّمۡ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الحجرات]{.ar} 49:7](https://quran.com/49/7)]{.citex}  
    [If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty]{.trans}

(@ex001463) [قَالُوا۟ لَوۡ **نَعۡلَمُ** قِتَالࣰا لَّٱتَّبَعۡنَـٰكُمۡۗ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة آل عمران]{.ar} 3:167](https://quran.com/3/167)]{.citex}  
    [They said, "If we had known [there would be] battle, we would have followed you."]{.trans}  

(@ex001464) [لَوْ **تَعْلَمُونَ** مَا أَعْلَمُ لَضَحِكْتُمْ قَلِيلاً وَلَبَكَيْتُمْ كَثِيرًا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :6486](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6486)]{.citex}  
    [If you knew what I know you would laugh little and you would cry much.]{.trans}  
(@ex001465) [فَقَالَ الْحَجَّاجُ لَوْ **نَعْلَمُ** مَنْ أَصَابَكَ فَقَالَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ أَنْتَ أَصَبْتَنِي]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :966](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:966) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 57]{.citex}  
    [[al-#HajjAj]{.trn2} said, "If we could only know who hit you." Ibn [#eumar]{.trn2} said, "You hit me."]{.trans}  

(@ex001466) [رَأَيْتُنِي يَوْمَ أَبِي جَنْدَلٍ وَلَوْ **أَسْتَطِيعُ** أَنْ أَرُدَّ أَمْرَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَرَدَدْتُهُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3181](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3181) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 57]{.citex}  
    [I found myself on the day of [#abU]{.trn2} Jandal [where] if I could have reversed the order of the Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng}, I would have reversed it.]{.trans}  

### A ø-case [muDArie]{.trn2} condition-verb

A ø-case [muDArie]{.trn2} condition-verb is exceedingly rare with [لَوْ]{.ar} but it is occasionally found.
For example:

(@ex001467) [لَوْ **تَعُذْ** حِينَ فَرَّ قَوْمُكَ بِي كُنْتَ مِنَ الأَمْنِ فِي أَعَزِّ مَكَانٍ]{.ar}
    [[[شواهد التوضيح لابن مالك]{.ar} 72](https://shamela.ws/book/98123/69#p1)]{.citex}  
    [Had you taken refuge, when your people fled, with me, you would have been, with regards to security, in the mightiest place.]{.trans}  

<!--
(@ex001468) [لو **يشأ** طار به ذو مَيعةٍ ْلاحقُ الآطالِ نهدٌ ذو خُصل]{.ar}
    [[[شواهد التوضيح لابن مالك]{.ar} 72](https://shamela.ws/book/98123/69#p1)]{.citex}
-->

### [لَوْ]{.ar} expressing a wish or hope {#sec-jsh_law_tamannii}

A special use of [لَوْ]{.ar} is for expressing a wish or hope.
These are of two types^[Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 53]:

The first is a [لَوْ]{.ar} clause by itself.
For example:

(@ex001469) [يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ رَجُلٌ أَسِيفٌ مَتَى يَقُمْ مَقَامَكَ لَا يُسْمِعِ النَّاسَ **لَوْ أَمَرْتَ عُمَرَ**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح ابن حبان]{.ar} :6873](https://hadithunlocked.com/ibnhibban:6873)]{.citex}  
    [O Messenger of Allāh Indeed [#abU]{.trn2} is a tender-hearted man. When he stands in your place, he will not be able to make the people hear. Would that you ordered [#eumar]{.trn2}.]{.trans}

The second is the [لَوْ]{.ar}-clause followed by a [فَ]{.ar} introducing a cause/purpose clause.
For example:

(@ex001470) [لَوْ تَأْتِينِي فَتُحَدِّثَنِي]{.ar}  
    [لَوْ تَأْتِينِي فَتُحَدِّثُنِي]{.ar}  
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/124](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2062)]{.citex}  
    [Would that you could come to me so that you could talk to me.]{.trans}  

One way of analyzing these types of sentences is
that the true condition-response of [لَوْ]{.ar} is deleted^[[[همع الهوامع للسيوطي]{.ar} 2/574](https://shamela.ws/book/6975/1146); [[مغني اللبيب لابن هشام]{.ar} 1/267](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/57084/read?part=1&page=265&index=3271127)]
(see @sec-jsh_hazf below).
And the clause beginning with [فَ]{.ar} takes the place of the true condition-response.

Occasionally the true condition-response is not deleted.
For example:

(@ex001471) [فَلَوْ نُبِشَ الْمَقَابِرُ عَنْ كُلَيْبٍ فَيُخْبِرُ بِالذَّنَائِبِ أي زير]{.ar}  
    [بيوم الشعشمين **لَقَرَّ عَيْنًا** وَكَيْفَ لِقَاءُ مَنْ تَحْتَ الْقُبُورِ]{.ar}
    [[[البحر المحيط لأبي حيان]{.ar} for [سورة السجدة]{.ar} 32:12](https://tafsir.app/albahr-almuheet/32/12)]{.citex}  
    [And if the graves were exhumed from Kulayb\ ... it would have been a coolness of the eyes\ ...]{.trans}  

<!--
(@ex001472) [لَوْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا لَصَلُحَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :2363](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2363)]{.citex}  
    [If you were to not do it, it would be good.]{.trans}  
-->

<!--
[[حذف جواب (لو)]{.ar}](https://jamharah.net/showthread.php?p=51540&__cf_chl_f_tk=olodL9o4qULPBi9qm4OZtgPe9o9jplpGgBKAcNjX6h0-1783293637-1.0.1.1-OL1LLUhK27d_zCqCdL3yEJVDwEpQsBIyUVPqNO7aG5c)]
-->

Here are some more examples of [لَوْ]{.ar} used to express a wish or hope:

(@ex001473) [وَدُّوا۟ لَوۡ تُدۡهِنُ فَیُدۡهِنُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة القلم]{.ar} 68:9](https://quran.com/68/9) cited by [[مغني اللبيب لابن هشام]{.ar} 1/265](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/57084/read?part=1&page=263&index=3271127)]{.citex}  
    [They wish that you would soften [in your position], so they would soften [toward you].]{.trans}

(@ex001474) [لَوْ صَلَّيْتَ بَعْدَهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :694e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:694e)]{.citex}  
    [Would that you prayed after it two [rakeah]{.trn2}s.]{.trans}  

(@ex001475) [يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ أَمْسَيْتَ إِنَّ عَلَيْكَ نَهَارًا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :5297](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5297)]{.citex}  
    [O Messenger of Allāh, would that you entered the evening. Indeed daytime is (still) upon you.]{.trans}  

(@ex001476) [فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ **لَوِ اتَّخَذْنَا مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى** فَنَزَلَتْ وَاتَّخِذُوا مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى وَآيَةُ الْحِجَابِ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ **لَوْ أَمَرْتَ نِسَاءَكَ أَنْ يَحْتَجِبْنَ فَإِنَّهُ يُكَلِّمُهُنَّ الْبَرُّ وَالْفَاجِرُ** فَنَزَلَتْ آيَةُ الْحِجَابِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :402](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:402)]{.citex}  
    [I said, "O Messenger of Allāh, would that we took the standing place of Abraham as a place of prayer." So [the [Ayah]{.trn2}] came down: And take, [O believers], from the standing place of Abraham a place of prayer. And [as regards] the [Ayah]{.trn2} of the veil, I said, "O Messenger of Allāh, would that you ordered your wives to cover themselves, for indeed the good and bad ones talk to them." So the [Ayah]{.trn2} of the veil came down.]{.trans}  


### A nounal sentence in the condition-response

Very rarely, a nounal sentence has been found to directly occur in the condition-response:

(@ex001477) [وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱتَّقَوۡا۟ **لَمَثُوبَةࣱ** مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ خَیۡرࣱۚ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة البقرة]{.ar} 2:103](https://quran.com/2/103)]{.citex}  
    [And if they had believed and feared Allāh, then the reward from Allāh would have been [far] better]{.trans}


Some grammarians have analyzed [لَمَثُوبَةٌ مِنَ اللهِ خَيرٌ]{.ar} to directly be the condition-response.
Whereas others have used [taqdIr]{.trn2}.^[[[هل يقع جواب (لو) جملة اسمية؟]{.ar}, jamharah.net](https://jamharah.net/showthread.php?p=51540&__cf_chl_f_tk=olodL9o4qULPBi9qm4OZtgPe9o9jplpGgBKAcNjX6h0-1783293637-1.0.1.1-OL1LLUhK27d_zCqCdL3yEJVDwEpQsBIyUVPqNO7aG5c)]


## Deletion in the conditional sentence {#sec-jsh_hazf}

For reasons of economy, emphasis, or style,
part of the conditional sentence may be omitted (i.e. deleted) in speech.
From context, the listener is able to restore the deleted part when understanding the conditional sentence.^[Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 198 quoting Crystal, _A dictionary of linguistics and phonetics_.]
In this section, we will give examples of deletion in the conditional sentence.^[The discussion follows Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ Chapter V, and re-uses many of the same examples.]

### Part of the condition or the condition-response is deleted {#sec-jsh_hazf_within_shart}

Consider the following examples:

(@ex001478) [الناسُ مَجزيُّونَ بأَعمالهم **إنْ خيراً فخيرٌ وإن شراً فشرٌ**]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 1/258](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/256)]{.citex}  
    [The people are rewarded according to their deeds: if good then good and if bad then bad.]{.trans}

(@ex001479) [المرء مقتولٌ بما قَتَلَ به **إنْ خِنْجَراً فخنجرٌ وإن سيفاً فسيفٌ**]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 1/258](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/256)]{.citex}  
    [[A] person is killed by what he killed with: if a dagger then a dagger, and if a sword then a sword.]{.trans}

Examples (@ex001478) and (@ex001479) above have parts of both the condition and the condition-response deleted.
Consider the single conditional sentence from example (@ex001478) above:

(@ex001480) [إِنْ خَيْرًا فَخَيْرٌ]{.ar}
    [cited by Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 208]{.citex}

The sentence, with the deleted parts restored is:

(@ex001481) [إِنْ كَانَ عَمَلُهُمْ خَيْرًا فَجَزَاؤُهُمْ خَيْرٌ]{.ar}
    [[[أوضح المسالك لابن هشام]{.ar} 1/254](https://shamela.ws/book/11825/256)]{.citex}  
    [If their deed was good, then their reward is good.]{.trans}

More combinations with deletion are  permissible.
Let's use example (@ex001478) again.
We can have the following combinations:

(@ex001482) a. [إِنْ خَيْرٌ فَخَيْرٌ]{.ar}  
    b. [إِنْ خَيْرًا فَخَيْرًا]{.ar}  
    c. [إِنْ خَيْرًا فَخَيْرٌ]{.ar}  
    d. [إِنْ خَيْرٌ فَخَيْرًا]{.ar}  
    [[[شرح كتاب سيبويه للسيرافي]{.ar} 2/156](https://shamela.ws/book/17726/654)]{.citex}  

In example (@ex001482) above,
when the condition has the 
a-case [خَيْرًا]{.ar},
then its restoration,
as we have seen, is
[إِنْ كَانَ عَمَلُهُمْ خَيْرًا]{.ar}.
And when the condition has the 
u-case [خَيْرٌ]{.ar},
then its restoration,
as we have seen, is
[إِنْ كَانَ فِي عَمَلِهِمْ خَيْرٌ]{.ar}.

Similarly
when the condition-response has the 
u-case [خَيْرٌ]{.ar},
then its restoration,
as we have seen, is
[فَجَزَاؤُهُمْ خَيْرٌ]{.ar}
And when the condition has the 
a-case [خَيْرًا]{.ar},
then its restoration,
as we have seen, is
[فَيُجْزَوْنَ خَيْرًا]{.ar}.^[[[أوضح المسالك لابن هشام]{.ar} 1/254](https://shamela.ws/book/11825/256)]



Here is another example:

(@ex001483) [صَلِّ قَائِمًا فَإِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ فَقَاعِدًا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :1116](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1116)]{.citex}  
    [Pray standing. But if you are not able then sitting.]{.trans}  

### The entire condition-core is deleted

The entire condition-core may be deleted when it is understood from context.
For example:


(@ex001484) [فَطَلِّقْهَا فَلَسْتَ لَهَا بِكُفْءٍ **وَإِلَا** يَعْلُ مَفْرَقَكَ الْحُسَامُ]{.ar}
    [cited by [[شرح ابن عقيل على الألفية]{.ar} 4/42](https://shamela.ws/book/9904/1049); Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 212]{.citex}  
    [So divorce her; for you are not adequate for her. And if not, the sword will hit your hair-parting (on your head)]{.trans}

The conditional sentence with the deleted condition-core restored is:

(@ex001485) [وَإِلَّا **تُطَلِّقْهَا** يَعْلُ مَفْرَقَكَ الْحُسَامُ]{.ar}
    [cited by [[شرح ابن عقيل على الألفية]{.ar} 4/43](https://shamela.ws/book/9904/1050)]{.citex}  
    [And if you don't divorce her, the sword will hit your hair-parting (on your head)]{.trans}

### The condition-response is deleted

We have already seen some cases of the condition-response being deleted.
For example:

In an inverted conditional sentence (see @sec-jsh_inverted_in above). Example:

(@ex001486) [هُوَ ظَالِمٌ إِنْ فَعَلَ]{.ar}
    [[[مغني اللبيب لابن هشام]{.ar} 2/647](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/57084/read?part=2&page=643&index=3271128) cited by Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 213]{.citex}  
    [He is a wrong-doer if he does it.]{.trans}  

In the case of [لَوْ]{.ar} expressing a wish or a hope (see @sec-jsh_law_tamannii above). Example:

(@ex001487) [لو أعطاني ووَهَبَني]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/124](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2062)]{.citex}  
    [Would that you gave me and granted me.]{.trans}  


The above can be considered cases of obligatory and regular deletion respectively.

(@ex001488) [بَلِّغُوا عَنِّي **وَلَوْ آيَةً**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3461](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3461)]{.citex}

The condition-response is also obligatorily deleted for parenthetical conditions.
For example:

(@ex001491) [هُوَ **إِنْ فَعَلَ** ظَالِمٌ]{.ar}
    [[[مغني اللبيب لابن هشام]{.ar} 2/647](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/57084/read?part=2&page=643&index=3271128)]{.citex}  
    [He, if he does it, is a wrong-doer.]{.trans}  

<!--
(@ex001492) [زَيْدٌ **وَإِنْ كَثُرَ مَالُهُ** زَعِيمٌ]{.ar}
    [Wright 2/40]{.citex}  
    [Zayd, even if his wealth be much, is stingy.]{.trans}
-->

(@ex001493) [وَإِنَّاۤ **إِن شَاۤءَ ٱللَّهُ** لَمُهۡتَدُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة البقرة]{.ar} 2:70](https://quran.com/2/70) cited by [[مغني اللبيب لابن هشام]{.ar} 2/647](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/57084/read?part=2&page=643&index=3271128); Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 213]{.citex}  
    [And indeed we, if Allāh wills, will be guided.]{.trans}

We will consider an additional case of obligatory deleted condition-response in @sec-jsh_qasam below.

In addition to obligatory or regular deletion,
the condition-response may also be optionally deleted for stylistic reasons.
For example:

(@ex001494) [وَلَوۡ أَنَّ قُرۡءَانࣰا سُیِّرَتۡ بِهِ ٱلۡجِبَالُ أَوۡ قُطِّعَتۡ بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ أَوۡ كُلِّمَ بِهِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۗ بَل لِّلَّهِ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ جَمِیعًاۗ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الرعد]{.ar} 13:31](https://quran.com/13/31) cited by [[مغني اللبيب لابن هشام]{.ar} 2/647](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/57084/read?part=2&page=643&index=3271128); Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 218]{.citex}  
    [And if there was any Qur’ān [i.e., recitation] by which the mountains would be removed or the earth would be broken apart or the dead would be made to speak, **[it would be this Qur’ān]**, but to Allāh belongs the affair entirely.]{.trans}
