### [Even if]{.trans}

A special case of a deleted condition-response is when the condition
imparts the meaning
[even if]{.trans}.
This occurs when conditional-device is preceded by [وَ]{.ar} and is not followed by a condition-response.
Examples:

(@ex001489) [أَنَا زَعِيمٌ بِبَيْتٍ فِي رَبَضِ الْجَنَّةِ لِمَنْ تَرَكَ الْمِرَاءَ **وَإِنْ كَانَ مُحِقًّا**]{.ar}
    [[[سنن أبي داود]{.ar} :4800](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4800)]{.citex}  
    [I guarantee a house in the surroundings of Paradise for a man who avoids arguing even if he were in the right.]{.trans}

(@ex001490) [قُلْتُ وَإِنْ زَنَى وَإِنْ سَرَقَ قَالَ وَإِنْ زَنَى وَإِنْ سَرَقَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :94b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:94b)]{.citex}  
    [I said, "Even if he fornicated and even if he stole?".  He said, "Even if he fornicated and even if he stole."]{.trans}  

Here is [even if]{.trans} as a parenthetical clause:

(@ex001492) [زَيْدٌ **وَإِنْ كَثُرَ مَالُهُ** زَعِيمٌ]{.ar}
    [Wright 2/40]{.citex}  
    [Zayd, even if his wealth be much, is stingy.]{.trans}

Frequently, the condition in an [even if]{.trans} may contain only a noun.
For example:

(@ex001488) [بَلِّغُوا عَنِّي **وَلَوْ آيَةً**]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3461](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3461)]{.citex}  
    [Convey from me (my teachings) even if one [Ayah]{.trn2}.]{.trans}  

In such cases, as in @sec-jsh_hazf_within_shart above,
there may be multiple ways to analyze the condition.
Consider the following sentence:

(@) [وَأْتِنِى بِدَابَّةٍ وَلَوْ حِمَارًا]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 1/269](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/267)]{.citex}  
    [And bring me a beast of burden, even if a donkey.]{.trans}

The a-case of
[حِمَار]{.ar}
is justified using the [taqdIr]{.trn2}:

(@) [وَلَوْ [كَانَ] حِمَارًا]{.ar}  
    [even if [it were] a donkey.]{.trans}

Instead of the a-case for
[حِمَار]{.ar},
the i-case may also be used:

(@) [وَأْتِنِى بِدَابَّةٍ وَلَوْ حِمَارٍ]{.ar}
    [composed from [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 1/269](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/267)]{.citex}  
    [And bring me a beast of burden, even if a donkey.]{.trans}

In this case the [taqdIr]{.trn2} is:

(@) [وَلَوْ [أَتَيْتَنِي بِ] حِمَارٍ]{.ar}  
    [even if [you brought me] a donkey.]{.trans}

The u-case is also possible, though not as preferred:

(@) [وَأْتِنِى بِدَابَّةٍ وَلَوْ حِمَارٌٍ]{.ar}
    [composed from [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 1/269](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/267)]{.citex}  
    [And bring me a beast of burden, even if a donkey.]{.trans}

In this case, the [taqdIr]{.trn2} would be:

(@) [وَلَوْ [يَكُونُ مِمَّا تَأْتِينِي بِهِ] حِمَارٌ]{.ar}  
    [composed from [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 1/269](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/267)]{.citex}  
    [even if a donkey [is what you bring me].]{.trans}

### Both the condition-core and the condition-response are deleted

Stylistically,
both the condition-core and the condition-response may be deleted.
For example:


(@ex001495) [قَالَتْ بَنَاتُ الْعَمِّ يَا سَلْمَى وَإِنْ كَانَ فَقِيرًا مُعْدَمًا قَالَتْ وَإِنْ]{.ar}
    [modified from [[أوضح المسالك لابن هشام]{.ar} 1/42](https://shamela.ws/book/11825/39), cited by Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 219]{.citex}  
    [The uncle's daughters (i.e. cousins) said, "O [#salmA]{.trn2}, even if he is a destitute poor [person]?" She said, "Even if."]{.trans}

In example (@ex001495) above, 
there are two conditional sentences.
The first conditional sentence is
[وَإِنْ كَانَ فَقِيرًا مُعْدَمًا]{.ar}
It's condition-response is deleted.

The second conditional sentence is only
[وَإِنْ]{.ar}.
Both its condition-core and condition-response are deleted.

Here is another example:

(@ex001496) [يقول القائل لا آتى الأمير لأنه جائر فيقال ائته وإن]{.ar}
    [[[شرح كتاب سيبويه للسيرافي]{.ar} 3/264](https://shamela.ws/book/17726/1260), cited by Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 219]{.citex}  
    [A speaker says, "I shall not come to the commander because he is unjust." So it is said (to him), "Come to him, even if."]{.trans}  
    That is: [Come to him, even if he is unjust]{.trans}

## A condition-core beginning with a noun

The basic principle for a condition-core is that it should be a verbal sentence.
(We include [كَانَ]{.ar} sentences in verbal sentences, loosely speaking.)
And the verb which begins the condition-core is classified as the condition-verb.

<!--
We had earlier stated that the condition requires a condition-verb in its condition-core.
Based on the preponderance of data in attested usage,
the grammarians extracted a basic principle that the condition-core
containing this condition-verb should be a verbal sentence.
-->
In all the examples we have seen so far,
this has been the case.
<!--
(We include [كَانَ]{.ar} sentences in verbal sentences, loosely speaking.)
-->
So, in the example:
[إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِي أَكْرَمْتُكَ]{.ar},
the condition-core is the verbal sentence
[أَتَيْتَنِي]{.ar},
and it is begun with the condition-verb [أَتَى]{.ar}.

Occassionally,
however,
the condition-core is found to begin with a noun.
For example:

(@ex001498) [**إِنِ ٱمۡرُؤٌا۟ هَلَكَ** لَیۡسَ لَهُۥ وَلَدࣱ وَلَهُۥۤ أُخۡتࣱ فَلَهَا نِصۡفُ مَا تَرَكَۚ]{.quran}  
    [[[سورة النساء]{.ar} 4:176](https://quran.com/4/176) cited by [[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/120](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2058)]{.citex}  
    [If a man dies, leaving no child but [only] a sister, she will have half of what he left.]{.trans}  

In example (@ex001498) above, the conditional-device [إِنْ]{.ar} is directly followed by the noun
[امْرُوٌ]{.ar}
and not the verb
[هَلَكَ]{.ar}.
The way that this,
and similar examples,
are made to align with the above stated principle of a
condition-core always being a verbal sentence,
is by [taqdIr]{.trn2}ing a deleted verb
[هَلَكَ]{.ar}
directly after the conditional-device [إِنْ]{.ar} as its condition-verb, thus^[The following is the standard analysis. Other analyses are described in Abdel-Ghani, _Conditional sentences within the Arab grammatical tradition_ 96--105 and [[شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} 4/93--94](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?part=4&page=1531&index=150957/150972)]:

(@ex001499) [إِنْ [هَلَكَ] امْرُوٌ]{.ar}

Once the original condition-verb
[هَلَكَ]{.ar}
is deleted,
its doer is left in place.
And an explanatory verb is added after it which gives the meaning of the deleted verb.
In this, and most cases, the explanatory verb matches the deleted verb.
So the resulting condition becomes
[إِنْ امْرُوٌ هَلَكَ]{.ar}.

In this way, the basic principle of
the condition-core always being a verbal sentence
remains intact.
And it restricts the the transformed condition
(after the deletion)
to have a verb.
Therefore, a condition like the following would be disallowed because it does not have a verb:

(@ex001500) ✗ [إِنْ عَمْرٌو خَارِجٌ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/120](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2058)]{.citex}  
    [If [#eamr]{.trn2} is outside\ ...]{.trans}  

In such conditions where the condition-core begins with a noun,
it is preferred that the conditional-device be [إِنْ]{.ar},
and that the condition-verb be [قَتَلَ]{.ar} not [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}.^[[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/121](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2059)]
Nevertheless,
counterexamples do occur.
For example:

(@ex001501) [**أَيْنَمَا** الرِّيحُ **تُمَيِّلْهَا** تَمِلْ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/112](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/966)]{.citex}  
    [Whichever way the wind makes it incline, it inclines.]{.trans}  

(@ex001502) [**إِذَا** أَنْتَ لَمْ تَنْفَعْ فَضُرَّ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح التسهيل لابن مالك]{.ar}](https://shamela.ws/book/13257/965)]{.citex}  
    [If you cannot benefit then harm.]{.trans}

In example (@ex001502) above,
the [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed original condition is
[إِذَا [لَمْ تَنْفَعْ]]{.ar}.
The verb
[تَنْفَعْ]{.ar}
(and [لَمْ]{.ar})
is deleted
and its doer is left in place.
But because its doer is a latent pronoun ([taqdIr]{.trn2}ed as [[أَنْتَ]]{.ar}),
it is transformed into its detached pronoun equivalent [أَنْتَ]{.ar} so that it can appear in surface speech.
Then an explanatory verbal expression
[لَمْ تَنْفَعْ]{.ar}
(which matches the deleted verbal expression)
is added,
and we end up with the resultant
[إِذَا أَنْتَ لَمْ تَنْفَعْ]{.ar}.

It is also possible for the explanatorily added verb to not exactly match the [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed deleted condition-verb.
For example:

<!--
Here are some examples:

(@ex001503) [إِنْ **أَنْتَ** أَكْرَمْتَ اللَّئِيمَ تَمَرَّدَا]{.ar}
    [abdelghani 96]{.citex}  
    [If you honor an ignoble [person], he rebels]{.trans}  
    (An extra alif is suffixed to [تَمَرَّدَ]{.ar} for rhyme.)

(@ex001504) [إذا أنت لم تنفع فضرّ]{.ar}
    [abdelghani 97]{.citex}  
In order to align outlier examples like () and () above with the basic principle
that the condition-core should be a verbal sentence,
the grammarians [taqdIr]{.trn2} the condition-core as a verbal sentence with a deleted verb.
So the [taqdIr]{.trn2} of the condition for example () above would be:

(@ex001505) [إِنْ [أَكْرَمْتَ اللَّئِيم]]{.ar}

The condition-core in the [taqdIr]{.trn2} is
[[أَكْرَمْتَ اللَّئِيم]]{.ar}
which is a verbal sentence.
In order to transform this [taqdIr]{.trn2} into the surface speech
[إِنْ أَنْتَ أَكْرَمْتَ اللَّئِيم]{.ar},
the following theoretical steps are taken:

  i. The 
     [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed verbal sentence
     [[أَكْرَمْتَ اللَّئِيم]]{.ar}
     is deleted, except for the doer of the condition-verb.
 ii. The condition-verb's doer is left in place.
     In this case, it is the
     the attached pronoun [تَ]{.ar}.
     But because the 
     an attached pronoun cannot occur by itself,
     it is converted to the detached pronoun
     [أَنْتَ]{.ar}.
iii. An explanatory verbal sentence
     [أَكْرَمْتَ اللَّئِيم]{.ar}
     is added after the doer [أَنْتَ]{.ar} in order to give the meaning of
     [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed verbal sentence.
     In this (and most) cases, the explanatory verbal sentence matches the [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed original condition-core.
     The verb in the explanatory verbal sentence is now the new condition-verb.


The benefit of this [taqdIr]{.trn2},
and of mandating a verbal sentence as the condition-core,
is that it prevents arbitrary nounal sentences,
that do not have a verb as the condition-verb,
from being the condition-core.
So for example, we cannot say:

(@ex001506) ✗ [إِنْ أَنْتَ كَرِيمٌ ...]{.ar}  
    [If you are honorable ...]{.trans}

Let's take a look at another example:
-->

(@ex001507) [ فإن أنت لم ينفعك علمك فانتسب ~ لعلّك تهديك القرون الأوائل]{.ar}  
    [cited by Abdel-Ghani, _Conditional sentences within the Arab grammatical tradition_ 101; [[شرح التسهيل لابن مالك]{.ar} 2/140](https://shamela.ws/book/13257/536)]{.citex}  
    [If your knowledge does not benefit you then affiliate yourself [to your predecessors]. Perhaps the earlier generations can guide you.]{.trans}

In example (@ex001507) above,
the additional complication is that the doer [أَنْتَ]{.ar}
that begins the condition-core, does not match the doer
[عِلْمُكَ]{.ar}
of the explanatory verbal sentence
[لم ينفعك علمك]{.ar}.^[Abdel-Ghani, _Conditional sentences within the Arab grammatical tradition_ 101--102]
But we can still mold this to fit in with out basic principle and the transformational steps that we gave above. Here's how:

The [taqdIr]{.trn2} for the condition can be [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed as:

(@ex001508) [فإن [لم تنتفع بعلمك]]{.ar}

The [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed verbal sentence
[[لم تنتفع بعلمك]]{.ar}
is deleted except for the condition-verb [تنتفع]{.ar}'s doer, the latent pronoun [[أَنْتَ]]{.ar}.
This latent doer pronoun
is transformed for surface speech into the detached pronoun [أَنْتَ]{.ar}.
An explanatory verbal sentence
[لم ينفعك علمك]{.ar}
is added after the doer
[أَنْتَ]{.ar}
to give the meaning of
a
[taqdIr]{.trn2}ed verbal sentence.
In this case, the explanatory verbal sentence does not exactly match the [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed original condition-core in wording,
but has a similar meaning.^[[[شرح التسهيل لابن مالك]{.ar} 2/140](https://shamela.ws/book/13257/536); see also [[التذييل والتكميل لأبي حيان]{.ar} 6/313](https://shamela.ws/book/17116/2004)]

The noun which follows the conditional-device may also be in the a-case as the direct doee of the deleted verb.
For example:

(@ex001509) [إِنْ زَيْدًا لَقِيتَهُ فَأَكْرِمْهُ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الأشمونى لألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 1/428](https://shamela.ws/book/11742/419)]{.citex}  
    [If it is Zayd you meet then honor him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001510) [حَيْثُمَا عَمْرًا لَقِيتَهُ فَأَهِنْهُ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الأشمونى لألفية ابن مالك]{.ar} 1/428](https://shamela.ws/book/11742/419)]{.citex}  
    [If it is [#eamr]{.trn2} you meet then insult him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001511) [لا تجزعي إن مُنفِسًا أهلكتُه وإذا هلكتُ فعند ذلك فاجزعي]{.ar}
    [[[شرح التسهيل لابن مالك]{.ar} 2/141](https://shamela.ws/book/13257/537); see also [[التذييل والتكميل لأبي حيان]{.ar} 6/313](https://shamela.ws/book/17116/2004)]{.citex}  
    [Do not grieve if I have destroyed a rival; but if I should perish, then at that time grieve.]{.trans}

Here are some more examples of conditional sentences whose condition-core begins with a noun:

(@ex001512) [**وَإِنۡ أَحَدࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِینَ ٱسۡتَجَارَكَ** فَأَجِرۡهُ حَتَّىٰ یَسۡمَعَ كَلَـٰمَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ أَبۡلِغۡهُ مَأۡمَنَهُۥۚ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة التوبة]{.ar} 9:6](https://quran.com/9/6)]{.citex}  
    [And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allāh [i.e., the Qur’ān].]{.trans}  

(@ex001513) [**فَإِنْ أَحَدٌ تَرَخَّصَ** لِقِتَالِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِيهَا فَقُولُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَذِنَ لِرَسُولِهِ وَلَمْ يَأْذَنْ لَكُمْ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :104](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:104) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 20]{.citex}  
    [So if anyone allows himself license because of the fighting of the Messenger of Allāh [ﷺ]{.areng} then say to him, "Allāh permitted His Messenger and did not permit you."]{.trans}

(@ex001514) [**وَإِنْ هُمْ أَبَوْا** فَوَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، لأُقَاتِلَنَّهُمْ عَلَى أَمْرِي هَذَا حَتَّى تَنْفَرِدَ سَالِفَتِي، وَلَيُنْفِذَنَّ اللَّهُ أَمْرَهُ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :2731](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2731) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 19]{.citex}  
    [But if they refuse, then by Him in whose Hand my soul is, I will definitely fight them on this cause of mine until [I die], but Allāh will [make His cause victorious].]{.trans}  

Here is an example with [إِذَا]{.ar} as the conditional-device:

(@ex001515) [إِذَا هُوَ لَمْ يُعْطِ فِيهَا حَقَّهَا تَطَؤُهُ بِأَخْفَافِهَا]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :1402](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1402) cited by Peled, _Conditional structures in Classical Arabic_ 27]{.citex}  
    [If he had not given their due [[zakAt]{.trn2}] for them, then they would tread him with their hooves]{.trans}

Here is an example with [لَوْ]{.ar} as the conditional-device:

(@ex001516) [قَالَ أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ بْنُ الْجَرَّاحِ أَفِرَارًا مِنْ قَدَرِ اللَّهِ فَقَالَ عُمَرُ **لَوْ غَيْرُكَ قَالَهَا** يَا أَبَا عُبَيْدَةَ، نَعَمْ نَفِرُّ مِنْ قَدَرِ اللَّهِ إِلَى قَدَرِ اللَّهِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :5729](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5729)]{.citex}  
    [[#abU #eubaydah ibn al-#jarrAH]{.trn2} said, "Are you fleeing what Allāh has ordained?" [#eumar]{.trn2} said, "**Would that someone else had said [such a thing]**, O [#abU #eubaydah]{.trn2}! Yes, we are fleeing from what Allah has ordained to what Allah has ordained."]{.trans}

<!--
(@ex001517) [فإنْ يَكُ عامِرٌ قد قالَ جَهلاً فإنَّ مَظِنَّةَ الجَهْلِ الشّبابُ]{.ar}
    [cited by Gätje, "Zur Struktur gestörter Konditionalgefüge im Arabischen" 174]{.citex} 
-->



<!--
From the above examples, we can note the following points:

* The condition-verb is always [قَتَلَ]{.ar} (or [لَمْ يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} which is equivalent).
* The original doer before the condition-verb is usually either a pronoun, or a generic or indefinite noun.
  There very few cases, where it is a definite specific noun.
-->


## The request-response

There is a special kind of sentence where a statement that can be classified as a _request_,
is followed by _request-response_.
For example:

(@ex001518) [ائْتِنِي آتِكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/93](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/946)]{.citex}  
    [Come to me, I will come to you.]{.trans}

In example (@ex001518) above,
the sentence
[ائْتِنِي]{.ar}
is the request.
And the sentence
[آتِكَ]{.ar}
is the request-response.

Note that the verb [آتِ]{.ar} in the request-response is in the ø-case,
as the direct consequence of fulfilling the request
[ائْتِنِي]{.ar}.
In order to justify the ø-case of the verb in the request-response,
the grammarians [taqdIr]{.trn2} 
a deleted condition
before it
that matches the the request.
It is this deleted condition
that causes the verb in the request-response to be in the ø-case.^[[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/94](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/947) citing [الخليل]{.ar}]
Here are a couple of possible [taqdIr]{.trn2}s of example (@ex001518) above:

(@ex001519) [ائْتِنِي [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي] آتِكَ]{.ar}  
    [Come to me. [If you come to me], I will come to you.]{.trans}

(@ex001520) [ائْتِنِي [إن يكن منك إتيانٌ] آتِكَ]{.ar}  
    [from [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/94](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/947)]{.citex}  
    [Come to me. [If there is a coming from you], I will come to you.]{.trans}

### Different types of requests

Requests that take a request-response may be of different types:

#### A command {.unnumbered}

Example (@ex001518) above is an example of a command request.
Here is another example:

(@ex001521) [أَسْلِمْ تَسْلَمْ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :1773a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1773a)]{.citex}  
    [Submit, you will be in peace.]{.trans}  

A possible [taqdIr]{.trn2} is:

(@ex001522) [أَسْلِمْ [إِنْ أَسْلَمْتَ] تَسْلَمْ]{.ar}  
    [Submit. [If you submit] you will be in peace.]{.trans}  

#### A prohibition {.unnumbered}

(@ex001523) [لا تفعل يكن خيراً لك]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/93](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/946) cited by Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 205]{.citex}  
    [Don't do it, it will be better for you.]{.trans}  

The [taqdIr]{.trn2} for the example above is:

(@ex001524) [لا تفعل [إِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ] يكن خيراً لك]{.ar}  
    [Don't do it. [If you don't do it] it will be better for you.]{.trans}  

#### A question {.unnumbered}

Example:

(@ex001525) [أَيْنَ بَيْتُكَ أَزُرْكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/94](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/947) cited by Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 206]{.citex}  
    [Where is your house? I will visit you.]{.trans}  

The [taqdIr]{.trn2} for the example above is:

(@ex001526) [أَيْنَ بَيْتُكَ [إِنْ أَعْلَمْ مَكَانَ بَيْتِكَ] أَزُرْكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/94](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/947)]{.citex}  
    [Where is your house? [If I know the location of your house] I will visit you.]{.trans} 

Here is another example:

(@ex001527) [یَـٰۤأَیُّهَا ٱلَّذِینَ ءَامَنُوا۟ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ تِجَـٰرَةࣲ تُنجِیكُم مِّنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِیمࣲ ۝ تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَتُجَـٰهِدُونَ فِی سَبِیلِ ٱللَّهِ بِأَمۡوَ ٰ⁠لِكُمۡ وَأَنفُسِكُمۡۚ ذَ ٰ⁠لِكُمۡ خَیۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ ۝ **یَغۡفِرۡ** لَكُمۡ ذُنُوبَكُمۡ **وَیُدۡخِلۡكُمۡ** جَنَّـٰتࣲ تَجۡرِی مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَـٰرُ وَمَسَـٰكِنَ طَیِّبَةࣰ فِی جَنَّـٰتِ عَدۡنࣲۚ ذَ ٰ⁠لِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِیمُ ۝ ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الصف]{.ar} 61:10–12](https://quran.com/61/10-12) cited by [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/94](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/947)]{.citex}  
    [O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?  [It is that] you believe in Allāh and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allāh with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you only knew.  He will forgive for you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great attainment.]{.trans}

In example (@ex001527) above, the request-response
[يَغْفِرْ]{.ar} is analyzed to be in the ø-case
following the question request [هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ]{.ar}.^[[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/94](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/947)]

#### A wish {.unnumbered}

Example:

(@ex001528) [أَلَا مَاءَ أَشْرَبْهُ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/93](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/946) cited by Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 206]{.citex}  
    [Is there no water I would drink?]{.trans} 

[#taqdIr]{.trn2}:

(@ex001529) [أَلَا مَاءَ [إِنْ يَكُنْ مَاءٌ] أَشْرَبْهُ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/94](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/947)]{.citex}  
    [Is there no water? [If there were water] I would drink it.]{.trans} 

Example:

(@ex001530) [لَيْتَهُ عِنْدَنَا يُحَدِّثْنَا]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/93](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/946)]{.citex}  
    [Would that he were with us, he would talk to us.]{.trans}

[#taqdIr]{.trn2}:

(@ex001531) [لَيْتَهُ عِنْدَنَا [إِنْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَنَا] يُحَدِّثْنَا]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/94](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/947)]{.citex}  
    [Would that he were with us. [If he were with us] he would talk to us.]{.trans}

#### An offer {.unnumbered}

Example:

(@ex001532) [أَلَا تَنْزِلُ تُصِبْ خَيْرًا]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/93](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/946)]{.citex}  
    [Won't you come settle? You will obtain benefit.]{.trans}

[#taqdIr]{.trn2}:

(@ex001533) [أَلَا تَنْزِلُ [إِنْ تَنْزِلْ] تُصِبْ خَيْرًا]{.ar}  
    [Won't you come settle? [If you will come settle] you will obtain benefit.]{.trans}

### The verb following the request may optionally be in the u-case

In the examples above, the 
verb following the request may optionally be in the u-case.^[[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/95](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/948)]
So for example, we can say:

(@ex001534) [ائْتِنِي **آتِيكَ**]{.ar}  
    [Come to me. I will come to you.]{.trans}  

<!--
When constructed in this way, the second sentence
(@ex001535) [آتيك]{.ar}  
is independent from the first sentence,
and not necessarily its direct consequence.
-->
In such cases, any [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed condition would not govern the u-case verb.
Here are some more examples:

(@ex001536) [خُذۡ مِنۡ أَمۡوَ ٰ⁠لِهِمۡ صَدَقَةࣰ **تُطَهِّرُهُمۡ** وَتُزَكِّیهِم بِهَا]{.quran}
    [[[سورة التوبة]{.ar} 9:103](https://quran.com/9/103) cited by Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 207]{.citex}  
    [Take, [O Muḥammad], from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them increase, and invoke [Allāh's blessings] upon them.]{.trans}

(@ex001537) [فَهَبۡ لِی مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِیࣰّا **یَرِثُنِی** وَیَرِثُ مِنۡ ءَالِ یَعۡقُوبَۖ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة مريم]{.ar} 19:5–6](https://quran.com/19/5-6) cited by Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 207]{.citex}  
    [so give me from Yourself an heir Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob.]{.trans}

### The [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed condition should match the request

The grammarians specify that the request-response should be the direct consequence
of satisfying a [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed condition that matches the request.
Let's explain what we mean by taking a look at the following (non-complying) example:

(@ex001538) ✗ [لَا تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ **يَأْكُلْكَ**]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/97](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/950)]{.citex}  
    [Don't go near the lion, it will eat you.]{.trans}

In example (@ex001538) above,
a [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed condition that matches the request is
[إِنْ لَمْ تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ]{.ar}.
If we insert this condition into the original sentence we get:

(@ex001539) ✗ [لا تدن من الأسد [إِنْ لَمْ تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ] ياكلك]{.ar}  
    [Don't go near the lion. [If you don't go near the lion] it will eat you.]{.trans}

As you can see, the sentence does not now make logical sense.
In such cases, it is better that the verb following the request be in the u-case.^[[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/97](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/950)]
So we should say

(@ex001540) ✓ [لَا تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ **يَأْكُلُكَ**]{.ar}  
    [Don't go near the lion. It will eat you.]{.trans}

A [فَ]{.ar} may also be prefixed to the u-case verb with no problem:

(@ex001541) ✓ [لَا تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ **فَيَأْكُلُكَ**]{.ar}  
    [Don't go near the lion. For it will eat you.]{.trans}

By the way, example (@ex001532) [أَلَا تَنْزِلُ تُصِبْ خَيْرًا]{.ar}
is not a problem because
the offer
[أَلَا تَنْزِلُ]{.ar}
is equivalent to the command
[انْزِلْ]{.ar}.^[[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/94](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/947)]

Similarly, example (@ex001528) [أَلَا مَاءَ أَشْرَبْهُ]{.ar}
is not a problem because
the wish
[أَلَا مَاءَ]{.ar}
is equivalent to hoping for water
[أَتَمَنَّى مَاءً]{.ar}.
So the [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed condition
[إِنْ يَكُنْ مَاءٌ]{.ar}
is valid.

## The conditional sentence within a larger sentence


The conditional sentence can occur as an element within a larger compound sentence.^[Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ chapter 6; [الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} [430--440](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n431/mode/2up), [455ff](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n455/mode/2up)]
It may occur in different capacities.
We will discuss some of them below.

### The conditional sentence as a info

The conditional sentence may occur as a info of a larger sentence.
For example:

(@ex001542) [زَيْدٌ إِنْ تُكْرِمْهُ يُكْرِمْكَ]{.ar}
    [[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 430](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n431/mode/2up) citing [الإيضاح للفارسي]{.ar}]{.citex}  
    [Zayd: if you honor him, he will honor you.]{.trans}  

In example above,
the conditional sentence
[إِنْ تُكْرِمْهُ يُكْرِمْكَ]{.ar}
is analyzed as the info of the subject
[زَيْدٌ]{.ar}.

Here is another example:

(@ex001543) [وَٱلَّـٰۤـِٔی یَىِٕسۡنَ مِنَ ٱلۡمَحِیضِ مِن نِّسَاۤىِٕكُمۡ إِنِ ٱرۡتَبۡتُمۡ فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلَـٰثَةُ أَشۡهُرࣲ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الطلاق]{.ar} 65:4](https://quran.com/65/4) cited by [[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 430](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n431/mode/2up)]{.citex}  
    [And those who no longer expect menstruation among your women - if you doubt, then their period is three months]{.trans}  

In example (@ex001543) above, the conditional sentence
[إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ\ ...]{.ar} has been analyzed as a info of [اللَّائِي]{.ar}.^[[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 430](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n431/mode/2up) citing [القيسي]{.ar}]

### The conditional sentence as a attribute

The conditional sentence may occur as a attribute of a attributee.
For example:

(@ex001544) [لَا تَسۡـَٔلُوا۟ عَنۡ أَشۡیَاۤءَ إِن تُبۡدَ لَكُمۡ تَسُؤۡكُمۡ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة المائدة]{.ar} 5:101](https://quran.com/5/101) cited by [[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 430](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n431/mode/2up)]{.citex}  
    [do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you]{.trans}  

In example (@ex001544) above, the conditional sentence
[إِنْ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ]{.ar}
is analyzed to be a attribute of
[أَشْيَاءَ]{.ar}.^[[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 430](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n431/mode/2up) citing [الأنباري]{.ar}]

### The conditional sentence as a [HAl]{.trn2}

Some grammarians have said that a conditional sentence can occur as a [HAl]{.trn2}.
One example given is:

(@ex001545) [أفعلُ هذا إن جاء زيدٌ]{.ar}
    [[[المساعد على تسهيل الفوائد لابن عقيل]{.ar} 2/43](https://shamela.ws/book/133358/639)]{.citex}  
    [I will do this if Zayd comes.]{.trans}

In example (@ex001545) above,
the inverted conditional sentence (with a deleted condition-response)
[إن جاء زيدٌ]{.ar}
is analyzed as a [HAl]{.trn2}.^[[[المساعد على تسهيل الفوائد لابن عقيل]{.ar} 2/43](https://shamela.ws/book/133358/639)]


In @sec-jsh_inverted_in above for example (@ex001190),
we saw that some grammarians may treat such a conditional sentence as something akin to a adverb of time/place.^[[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/118](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2056)]
For example:

(@ex001546) [آتِيكَ إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِى]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/118](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2056)]{.citex}  
    [I will come to you if you come to me.]{.trans}  

### The conditional sentence as a connecting sentence

The conditional sentence may occur as a connecting sentence of a connected noun.
For example:


(@ex001547) [ٱلَّذِینَ إِن مَّكَّنَّـٰهُمۡ فِی ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَقَامُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الحج]{.ar} 22:41](https://quran.com/22/41) cited by [[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 430](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n431/mode/2up)]{.citex}  
    [[And they are] those who, if We give them authority in the land, establish prayer]{.trans}  

In example (@ex001547) above, the conditional sentence
[إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ]{.ar}
is analyzed to be a connecting sentence of
[الَّذِينَ]{.ar}.^[[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 430](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n431/mode/2up) citing [الأنباري]{.ar}]

### The conditional sentence within a question

The main category here is a [أَ]{.ar} preceding a conditional sentence.
The [أَ]{.ar}
simply asks a question and
has no effect on the syntax on the following conditional sentence.^[See also [[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 432--440](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n433/mode/2up)]
Examples:

(@ex001548) [أإن تأتني آتك]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/82](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/935)]{.citex}  
    [Is it that if you come to me, I come to you?]{.trans}

(@ex001549) [أمتى تشتمني أشتمك]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/82](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/935)]{.citex}  
    [Is it that when you revile me, I revile you?]{.trans}

(@ex001550) [أمن يفعل ذاك أزره]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/82](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/935)]{.citex}  
    [Is it that whoever does that, I should visit him?]{.trans}  

### The conditional sentence within foundational government sentences

[إِنَّ]{.ar}, [كَانَ]{.ar}, and [لَيْسَ]{.ar}
are foundational government-devices
and they
have subjects and infos.
It is possible for their subjects to be
[مَنْ]{.ar}, [مَا]{.ar}, and [أَيّ]{.ar},
which, as we know from @sec-jsh_other_adats above,
can also be conditional-devices.

But when these nouns
are the subjects
of one of these
foundational government-devices,
then
they cannot also be conditional-devices at the same time.
These nouns then revert back to connected nouns.
For example:

(@ex001551) [إِنَْ مَنْ يَأْتِينِي آتِيهِ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/71](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/924)]{.citex}  
    [Indeed who comes to us is whom we come to.]{.trans}  

(@ex001552) [كَانَ مَنْ يَأْتِينِي آتِيهِ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/71](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/924)]{.citex}  
    [Who comes to us was whom we come to.]{.trans}  

(@ex001553) [لَيْسَ مَنْ يَأْتِينِي آتِيهِ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/71](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/924)]{.citex}  
    [Who comes to us is not whom we come to.]{.trans}  

In examples (@ex001551) through (@ex001553) above,
[مَنْ]{.ar} is the subject and a connected noun,
[يَأْتِينِي]{.ar}
(in the u-case)
is its connecting sentence,
and
[آتِيهِ]{.ar}
(in the u-case)
is the info.

Conditional-devices that are not connected nouns
may not occur as the subjects of these
foundational government devices.
So we cannot say:

(@ex001554) ✗ [إِنَّ إِنْ\ ...]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/72](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/925)]{.citex}  

(@ex001555) ✗ [إِنَّ مَتَى\ ...]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/72](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/925)]{.citex}  

If these
foundational government devices
have other subjects,
then a conditional sentence
may freely be info.
Examples:

(@ex001556) [إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَأْتِنَا نَأْتِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/72](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/925)]{.citex}  
    [Indeed [the state-of affairs] is: who will come to us, we will come to him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001557) [كُنْتُ مَنْ يَأْتِنَي آتِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/72](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/925)]{.citex}  
    [I was: who will come to me, I will come to him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001558) [كَانَ مَنْ يَأْتِهِ يُعْطِهِ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/72](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/925)]{.citex}  
    [He was: who will come to him, he will give to him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001559) [لَيْسَ مَنْ يَأْتِهِ يُحْبِبْهُ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/72](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/925)]{.citex}  
    [He is not: who will come to him, he will love him.]{.trans}  

(@ex001560) [إِنَّهُۥ مَن یَأۡتِ رَبَّهُۥ مُجۡرِمࣰا فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ جَهَنَّمَ لَا یَمُوتُ فِیهَا وَلَا یَحۡیَىٰ]{.quran}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/72](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/925)]{.citex}  
    [Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.]{.trans}

In such sentences,
the state-of-affairs pronoun can be deleted.
For example:

(@ex001561) [إنَّ مَن لامَ في بني بنت حسّان ألُمهْ وأَعْصِه في الخُطوبِ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/73](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/926)]{.citex}  
    [Indeed [the state-of-affairs] is: whoever blames [me] regarding the sons of the daughter of [#HassAn]{.trn2}, I will blame him and I will disobey him in the affairs.]{.trans}  
    ([إِنَّ]{.ar} has a deleted state-of-affairs pronoun thus: [إِنَّهُ]{.ar}.)

(@ex001562) [قد علمت أن من يأتني آته]{.ar}
    [[[سورة طه]{.ar} 20:74](https://quran.com/20/74) cited by [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/73](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/926)]{.citex}  
    [You have known that [the state-of-affairs] is: whoever comes to me, I come to him.]{.trans}  
    ([أَنَّ]{.ar} has a deleted state-of-affairs pronoun thus: [أَنَّهُ]{.ar}.)

### The conditional sentence after non-foundational government introductory devices

There are words that introduce sentences,
but don't govern an subject and info directly.
For example:
[إِذْ]{.ar} [when]{.trans},
[أَمَّا]{.ar} [as for]{.trans},
[إِذَا]{.ar} [when]{.trans},
[لَـٰكِنْ]{.ar} [but]{.trans},
[لَا]{.ar} [not]{.trans},
[مَا]{.ar} [not]{.trans}.

#### [إِذْ]{.ar}, [أَمَّا]{.ar}, and [مَا]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

For most such introductory devices
will again be followed by connected nouns,
and not, typically, conditional-devices.
Examples:

(@ex001563) [أتذكر إذ من يأتينا نأتيه]{.ar}  
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/75](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/928)]{.citex}  
    [Do you remember when who [was] coming to us, we [were] coming to him?]{.trans}

(@ex001564) [ما من يأتينا نأتيه]{.ar}  
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/75](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/928)]{.citex}  
    [It is not that who comes to us, we come to him.]{.trans}

(@ex001565) [أما من يأتينا فنحن نأتيه]{.ar}  
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/75](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/928)]{.citex}  
    [As for who comes to us, then we come to him.]{.trans}

Note that again
[يَأْتِينِي]{.ar}
and
[آتِيهِ]{.ar}
are in the u-case.
And again,
the conditional-device
[إِنْ]{.ar} would typically not follow these introductory devices.

Having said that,
by poetic license,
we can find a conditional sentence after these introductory devices.
In that case, sentences like the following examples would be pemissible:

(@ex001566) [أتذكر إذ من يأتنا نأته]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/75](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/928)]{.citex}  
    [Do you remember when: whoever would come to us, we would come to him?]{.trans}

(@ex001567) [أتذكر إذ إن تأتنا نأتك]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/76](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/929)]{.citex}  
    [Do you remember when: if you would come to us, we would come to you?]{.trans}

When [إِذْ]{.ar} is separated from the conditional sentence by a noun,
then there is no problem in having the conditional sentence.
For example:

(@ex001568) [أتذكر إذ **نحن** من يأتنا نأته]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/76](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/929)]{.citex}  
    [Do you remember when **we**: whoever would come to us, we would come to him?]{.trans}

#### sudden-[إِذَا]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

The same goes for the sudden-[إِذَا]{.ar}.
For example:

(@ex001569) [مررت به فإذا من يأتيه يعطيه]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/76](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/929)]{.citex}  
    [I passed by him, then, suddenly, whoever [was] coming to him, he [was] giving him.]{.trans}  

A conditional sentence can also be used, if we there is a noun after [إِذَا]{.ar}:

(@ex001570) [مررت به فإذا هو من يأتيه يعطيه]{.ar}
    [modified from [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/76](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/929)]{.citex}  
    [I passed by him, then, suddenly, he: whoever would come to him, he would give to him.]{.trans}  
    (The [هو]{.ar} may be optionally deleted, so we can also say: [فإذا من يأتيه يعطيه]{.ar}.)

#### [لَـٰكِنْ]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

[لَـٰكِنْ]{.ar} is similar to [إِذَا]{.ar},
so we can say
(with a deleted pronoun after [لَـٰكِنْ]{.ar}):

(@ex001571) [ما أنا ببخيلٍ ولكن إن تأتني أعطك]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/77](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/930)]{.citex}  
    [I am not a miser. Rather if you come to me, I will give to you.]{.trans}  
    (There is a deleted pronoun after [لَـٰكِنْ]{.ar}.)

#### [لَا]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

[لَا]{.ar} is different from the other introductory devices above.
A conditional sentence may freely occur after it.
For example:

(@ex001572) [لا من يأتك تعطه]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/76](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/929)]{.citex}  
    [It is not that whoever will come to you, you will give to him.]{.trans}
    

## The condition combined with an oath {#sec-jsh_qasam}

We know from chapter ()
that the oath-sentence,
like the conditional sentence,
has two parts:

 i. The oath
ii. The oath-response

For example,

(@ex001573) [وَاللهِ لَأَفْعَلَنَّ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/104](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/957)]{.citex}  
    [By Allāh, I will do it.]{.trans}  

In example (@ex001573) above,
[وَاللهِ]{.ar}
is the oath, and
[لَأَفْعَلَنَّ]{.ar}
is the oath-response.
The oath-response is
prefixed by the oath-response-[لَ]{.ar}.

The oath-sentence is often combined with the conditional sentence.
This can occur in a few different ways:

a. The oath occurs in the beginning of a sentence, before the condition.
b. The condition occurs in the beginning of a sentence, before the oath.
c. The oath and condition are in the info of a compound sentence.

Let's discuss each of these in turn.

<!--
a. The oath/condition does not occur in the info of a compound sentence.
    i. The oath occurs before the condition in sentence word order.
   ii. The condition occurs before the oath in sentence word order.
b. The oath/condition occurs in the info of a compound sentence.
-->

### The oath occurs in the beginning of a sentence, before the condition

The general principle, when analyzing such sentences,
is that there will be only one response,
either a oath-response, or a condition-response.
And,
typically,
the response will be for whichever of the oath or the condition occurred first in sentence word order.

Consider the following example:

(@ex001574) [وَاللهِ لَئِنْ أَكْرَمْتَنِي لَأُكْرِمَنَّكَ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/141](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2079)]{.citex}  
    [By Allāh, if you honor me, I will honor you.]{.trans}  

In example (@ex001574) above,
the oath
[وَاللهِ]{.ar}
occurs before the condition
[إنْ أَكْرَمْتَنِي]{.ar}
in sentence word order.
Therefore,
the response
[لَأُكْرِمَنَّكَ]{.ar}
is here the oath-response.
This is evinced by the
the usage of emphatic verb
and the [لَ]{.ar} before it,
which are hallmarks of the oath-response.
The condition-response is obligatorily deleted.

Note also, the usage of another [لَ]{.ar} that prefixes the conditional-device:
[لَئِنْ]{.ar}.
This is a special [لَ]{.ar} that is only used when a
oath precedes the conditional-device [إِنْ]{.ar}.
It indicates that any response which follows is a oath-response.^[[[معجم المسائل النحوية والصرفية الواردة في القرآن الكريم]{.ar} 28](https://shamela.ws/book/11928/29)]

Here is another example of
a oath preceding a condition:

(@ex001575) [واللهِ لَئِنْ أتيتَني لأتيتُك]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/141](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2079)]{.citex}  
    [By Allāh, if you came to me, I will come to you.]{.trans}  

In example (@ex001575) above,
[لأتيتُك]{.ar}
is again the oath-response.
In this case, it uses a [mADI]{.trn2} verb,
even though it has a future meaning.

Often times,
the actual oath may optionally be deleted.
For example:

(@ex001576) [لَىِٕنۡ أُخۡرِجُوا۟ لَا یَخۡرُجُونَ مَعَهُمۡ وَلَىِٕن قُوتِلُوا۟ لَا یَنصُرُونَهُمۡ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الحشر]{.ar} 59:12](https://quran.com/59/12) cited by [[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/142](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2080)]{.citex}  
    [If they are expelled, they will not leave with them, and if they are fought, they will not aid them.]{.trans}

In example (@ex001576) above,
a oath is assumed to be deleted.
The response
[لَا یَخْرُجُونَ]{.ar}
is still analyzed to be an oath-response.^[[[شرح ابن يعيش على المفصل]{.ar} 5/142](https://shamela.ws/book/13301/2080)]
This is again indicated by the [لَ]{.ar} preceding the conditional-device ([لَئِنْ]{.ar}),
and also by the use of the u-case of the [muDArie]{.trn2} verb in the response
([يَخْرُجُونَ]{.ar})
instead of the ø-case.

Occasionally,
both the oath and the [لَ]{.ar} before the conditional-device [إِنْ]{.ar} may optionally be deleted.
But the oath is implied,
and so the response matches the syntax of the condition-response,
not the condition-response.
For example:

(@ex001577) [إن أتيتني لأكرمنك]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/66](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/919)]{.citex}  
    [If you came to me, I will honor you]{.trans}  

In example (@ex001577) above,
the [taqdIr]{.trn2},
with the optionally deleted elements restored, is:

(@ex001578) [والله لئن أتيتني لأكرمنك]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/66](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/919)]{.citex}  
    [By Allāh, if you came to me, I will honor you]{.trans}  

When the oath precedes the condition,
and thus the response is an oath-response and not a condition-response,
it is preferred that the condition-verb
be of the form [قَتَلَ]{.ar} 
(or its equivalent [لَمْ يَقْتُلْ]{.ar})
and not [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar}.
This is because
(as we also mentioned in @sec-jsh_qatala above)
when the condition-verb is [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar},
then it strongly prefers
that a condition-response,
with a symmetrical [يَقْتُلْ]{.ar} as the condition-response-verb,
be actually uttered in surface speech.
So it is preferred not to say:

(@ex001579) ✗ [لَئِنْ **تَفْعَلْ** لَأَفْعَلَنَّ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/66](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/919)]{.citex}  
    [[By Allāh,] if you do, I will do.]{.trans}  

This preference can be seen in the following [Ayah]{.trn2}s:

(@ex001580) [وَإِن لَّمۡ تَغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَتَرۡحَمۡنَا **لَنَكُونَنَّ** مِنَ ٱلۡخَـٰسِرِینَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الأعراف]{.ar} 7:23](https://quran.com/7/23) cited by [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/66](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/919)]{.citex}  
    [and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers]{.trans}  
    [لَنَكُونَنَّ]{.ar} is analyzed as an oath-response to a deleted oath.^[[[البحر المحيط لأبي حيان]{.ar} for [سورة الأعراف]{.ar} 7:23](https://tafsir.app/albahr-almuheet/7/23)]

(@ex001581) [وَإِلَّا تَغۡفِرۡ لِی وَتَرۡحَمۡنِیۤ **أَكُن** مِّنَ ٱلۡخَـٰسِرِینَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة هود]{.ar} 11:47](https://quran.com/11/47) cited by [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/66](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/919)]{.citex}  
    [And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers]{.trans}  
    [أَكُنْ]{.ar} is analyzed as a condition-response.^[[[الجدول في إعراب القرآن لمحمود صافي]{.ar} for [سورة هود]{.ar} 11:47](https://tafsir.app/aljadwal/11/47)]

Here are some more examples of a oath in the beginning of a sentence, preceding a condition:

(@ex001582) [لَئِنْ بَقِيتُ إِلَى قَابِلٍ لأَصُومَنَّ التَّاسِعَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :1134b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1134b)]{.citex}  
    [If I live to the coming year, I will definitely fast the ninth.]{.trans}  

(@ex001583) [قَالَ أَبُو جَهْلٍ **لَئِنْ رَأَيْتُ مُحَمَّدًا يُصَلِّي لأَطَأَنَّ عَلَى عُنُقِهِ** فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَوْ فَعَلَ لأَخَذَتْهُ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ عِيَانًا]{.ar}
    [[[جامع الترمذي]{.ar} :3348](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3348)]{.citex}  
    [[#abU]{.trn2} Jahl said, "If I see [#muHammad]{.trn2} praying, I shall certainly stomp on his neck." So the Prophet [ﷺ]{.areng} said, "If he did that, the angels would seize him visibly."]{.trans}  

(@ex001584) [وَاللَّهِ لَئِنْ حَلَفْتُ لاَ تُصَدِّقُونِي وَلَئِنِ اعْتَذَرْتُ لاَ تَعْذِرُونِي]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح البخاري]{.ar} :3388](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3388)]{.citex}  
    [By Allāh, if I were to take an oath, you would not believe me. And if I were to offer an excuse, you would not excuse me.]{.trans}  

What we have said regarding
the response being a oath-response when the oath precedes the condition
is true generally.
However, rarely,
the response in such cases can be the condition-response,
not the oath-response.
For example:

(@ex001585) [لَئِنْ كَانَ حُدِّثْتُهُ الْيَوْمَ صَادِقًا **أَصُمْ** فِي نَهَارِ الْقَيْظِ لِلشَّمْسِ بَادِيًا]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/476]{.citex}  
    [If what I have been told today is true, I will fast in the heat of the day out in the sun.]{.trans}  
    [أَصُمْ]{.ar} in the ø-case indicates that it is the condition-response not the oath-response.

The above discussion has dealt with only the conditional-device [إِنْ]{.ar}.
Other conditional-devices that govern two ø-case verbs,
like [مَنْ]{.ar}, [مَا]{.ar}, etc.,
will behave the same way.
For example:

(@ex001586) [لَّمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنۡهُمۡ لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِینَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الأعراف]{.ar} 7:18](https://quran.com/7/18)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever follows you among them - I will surely fill Hell with you, all together]{.trans}  

In example (@ex001586) above, the [لَ]{.ar} in [لَمَنْ]{.ar} has been analyzed as following a deleted oath.
[لَأَمْلَأَنَّ]{.ar} is then the oath-response.
Other analyses are also possible.^[[[البحر المحيط لأبي حيان]{.ar} for [سورة الأعراف]{.ar} 7:18](https://tafsir.app/albahr-almuheet/7/18)]

### The condition occurs in the beginning of a sentence, before the oath

When the
condition
(or any portion thereof)
occurs before the oath,
then
the response
is considered to be the condition-response,
and the oath-response is obligatorily deleted.

(@ex001587) [إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِي وَاللهِ آتِكَ]{.ar}
    [[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 451](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n451/mode/2up) citing [شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar}]{.citex}  
    [If you came to me, by Allāh, I will come to you.]{.trans}  

(@ex001588) [إِنْ قَامَ زَيْدٌ وَاللهِ يَقُمْ عَمْرٌو]{.ar}
    [[[شرح ابن عقيل على الألفية]{.ar} 4/44](https://shamela.ws/book/9904/1051)]{.citex}  
    [If Zayd stands, by Allāh, [#eamr]{.trn2} will stand.]{.trans}  

(@ex001589) [إنْ وَاللهِ جِئْتَنِي أُكْرِمْكَ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح التسهيل لابن مالك]{.ar} 3/216](https://shamela.ws/book/13257/1032)]{.citex}  
    [If, by Allāh, you come to me, I will honor you.]{.trans}  

There is also another possibility,
which is that
the sentence can have both a oath-response and a condition-response.
And
the entire oath-sentence is the condition-response.
A [فَ]{.ar} will be needed as the condition-response-link.
Examples:

(@ex001590) [إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِي فَوَاللهِ لَآتِيَنَّكَ]{.ar}
    [[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 451](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n451/mode/2up) citing [شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar}]{.citex}  
    [If you came to me, then by Allāh, I will come to you.]{.trans}  

### The oath and condition are in the info of a compound sentence

When the
oath and condition sentence occur in the info of a compound sentence,
then
the standard position of the grammarians is that
the response shall be the condition-response,
and that the oath-response be obligatorily deleted,
regardless of whether the condition preceded the oath,
or vice-versa.^[[[المساعد على تسهيل الفوائد لابن عقيل]{.ar} 3/177](https://shamela.ws/book/133358/1452)]

(@ex001591) [زيد والله إن يقم عمرو **يأت**]{.ar}
    [[[المساعد على تسهيل الفوائد لابن عقيل]{.ar} 3/177](https://shamela.ws/book/133358/1452)]{.citex}  
    [Zayd, by Allāh, if [#eamr]{.trn2} stands, will come.]{.trans}  

(@ex001592) [زيد إن يقم عمرو والله **يأت**]{.ar}
    [[[المساعد على تسهيل الفوائد لابن عقيل]{.ar} 3/177](https://shamela.ws/book/133358/1452)]{.citex}  
    [Zayd, if [#eamr]{.trn2} stands, by Allāh, will come.]{.trans}  

<!--
In examples () and () above,
[يَأْتِ]{.ar} is the condition-response and the entire conditional sentence is the info of the subject [زَيْدٌ]{.ar}.
More examples:
-->

(@ex001593) [أَنَا وَاللهِ إِنْ تَأْتِنِي لَا آتِكَ]{.ar}
    [[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 448](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n449/mode/2up) citing [كتاب سيبويه]{.ar}]{.citex}  
    [I, by Allāh, if you come to me, I will not come to you.]{.trans}  

(@ex001594) [أَنَا إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِي وَاللهِ آتِكَ]{.ar}
    [[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 450](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n451/mode/2up) citing [شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar}]{.citex}  
    [I, if you came to me, by Allāh, I will come to you.]{.trans}  

The above is the most common opinion of the grammarians.
However, some grammarians have allowed
that when the oath precedes the condition,
then the response can be the oath-response
and the condition-response is deleted.^[[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 449](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n449/mode/2up) citing [شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar} and [ارتشاف الضرب من لسان العرب]{.ar}]
For example:

(@ex001595) [أَنَا وَاللهِ إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِي **لَآتِيَنَّكَ**]{.ar}
    [[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 449](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n449/mode/2up) citing [شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar}]{.citex}  
    [I, by Allāh, if you came to me, I will come to you.]{.trans}  

Another opinion found amongst the grammarians is that
both the condition-response and the oath-response can be deleted.
And so the following verbal sentence is directly the info.^[[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 449](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n449/mode/2up) citing [ارتشاف الضرب من لسان العرب]{.ar}]
For example:

(@ex001596) [زَيْدٌ واللهِ إِن أَكْرَمْتَهُ **يُكْرِمُكَ**]{.ar}
    [[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 449](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n449/mode/2up) citing [ارتشاف الضرب من لسان العرب]{.ar}]{.citex}  
    [Zayd: by Allāh, if you honor him, he will honor you.]{.trans}  
    [يُكْرِمُكَ]{.ar}, in the u-case is the info of [زَيْدٌ]{.ar}.

Lastly, there is also the possibility that
the sentence can have both a oath-response and a condition-response.
And
the entire oath-sentence is the condition-response.^[[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 449](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n449/mode/2up) citing [ارتشاف الضرب من لسان العرب]{.ar}]
A [فَ]{.ar} will be needed as the condition-response-link.
For example:

(@ex001597) [أَنَا إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِي فَوَاللهِ لَآتِيَنَّكَ]{.ar}
    [[[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 450](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n451/mode/2up) citing [شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar}]{.citex}  
    [I, if you came to me, then by Allāh, I will come to you.]{.trans}

However, some grammarians have allowed additional possibilities:

  i. That both the oath-response and the condition-response are deleted.
     For example:

     (@) [أنا والله إن تأتني آتيك]{.ar}
         [[[المساعد على تسهيل الفوائد لابن عقيل]{.ar} 3/178](https://shamela.ws/book/133358/1452)]{.citex}  
         [I, by Allāh, if you come to me, I will come to you.]{.trans}  
         [آتِيكَ]{.ar}, in the u-case is the info of [أَنَا]{.ar}.


 ii. That condition-response is deleted.
     For example:

     (@) [أنا والله إن تأتني لَآتِيَنَّكَ]{.ar}
         [[[المساعد على تسهيل الفوائد لابن عقيل]{.ar} 3/178](https://shamela.ws/book/133358/1452)]{.citex}  
         [I, by Allāh, if you come to me, I will come to you.]{.trans}  
         [لَآتِيَنَّكَ]{.ar} is the oath-response. The sentence [والله إن تأتني لَآتِيَنَّكَ]{.ar} is the info of [أَنَا]{.ar}.

     For example:

     (@) [أنا والله إن تأتني آتك]{.ar}
         [[[المساعد على تسهيل الفوائد لابن عقيل]{.ar} 3/178](https://shamela.ws/book/133358/1452)]{.citex}  
         [I, by Allāh, if you come to me, I will come to you.]{.trans}  
         [آتِكَ]{.ar}, in the ø-case is the condition-response. The conditional sentence [إن تأتني آتك]{.ar} is the info of [أَنَا]{.ar}.

### [لَوْ]{.ar} combined with a oath

When the conditional-devices [لَوْ]{.ar} or [لَوْلَا]{.ar} are combined with a oath,
then
firstly, no additional [لَ]{.ar} is prefixed to them,
like it was in the case of [لَئِنْ]{.ar}.
Secondly,
the standard position of the grammarians is that
the response shall be the condition-response,
and that the oath-response be obligatorily deleted,
regardless of whether the condition preceded the oath,
or vice-versa.^[[[المساعد على تسهيل الفوائد لابن عقيل]{.ar} 3/179](https://shamela.ws/book/133358/1454)]
Examples:

(@ex001598) [وَاللهِ لَوْلَا اللهُ مَا اهْتَدَيْنَا وَلَا تَصَدَّقْنَا وَلَا صَلَّيْنَا]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الكافية الشافية لابن مالك]{.ar} 2/894](https://shamela.ws/book/12024/898)]{.citex}  
    [By Allāh, were it not for Allāh we would not have been guided, nor would we have given charity, nor would we have prayed.]{.trans}  

(@ex001599) [فَأُقْسِمُ لَوْ أَبْدَى النَّدِيُّ سَوَادَهُ لَمَا مَسَحَتْ تِلْكَ الْمُسَالَاتِ عَامِرُ]{.ar}
    [[[شرح الكافية الشافية لابن مالك]{.ar} 2/893](https://shamela.ws/book/12024/897)]{.citex}  
    [So I swear, if the gathering [was attended by] his personage, [the tribe of] [#eAmir]{.trn2} would not be able to wipe those sideburns [of his] (out of respect and fear of him).]{.trans}

However, some grammarians have allowed additional possibilities.^[see [[تمهيد القواعد بشرح تسهيل الفوائد لناظر الجيش]{.ar} 6/3121ff](https://shamela.ws/book/16826/3079)]

## Multiple verbs in the condition or condition-response

### A condition-verb or condition-response-verb with a verbal sentence as a [HAl]{.trn2}

The condition-verb or condition-response-verb may be followed by a verbal sentence which is a [HAl]{.trn2} to it.
For example:

(@ex001600) [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي تَسْأَلُنِي أُعْطِكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/85](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/938#p1) cited by [[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 390](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n391/mode/2up)]{.citex}  
    [If you come to me---asking me--, I will give to you.]{.trans}  


The verbal sentence
[تَسْأَلُنِي]{.ar}
is a [HAl]{.trn2}.
And that is why its verb is in the u-case.

Here is another example:

(@ex001601) [وَإِنْ أَتَانِي **يَمْشِي** أَتَيْتُهُ هَرْوَلَةً]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :2675a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2675a)]{.citex}  
    [And if he comes to Me walking, I come to him rushing.]{.trans}  

### A condition-verb or condition-response-verb with a re-specifier

The condition-verb or condition-response-verb may be followed by a verbal sentence
which is an re-specifier to it.
Examples:

(@ex001602) [إِنْ تَأْتِنَا تَسْأَلْنَا نُعْطِكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/87](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/940) cited by [[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 396](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n397/mode/2up)]{.citex}  
    [If you come to us, you ask us, we will give to you.]{.trans}  
    [تَسْأَلْنَا]{.ar} is a re-specifier of [تَأْتِنَا]{.ar}.

(@ex001603) [إِنْ تَأْتِنَا نُحْسِنْ إِلَيْكَ نُعْطِكَ وَنَحْمِيكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/87](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/940)]{.citex}  
    [If you come to use, we will be good to you, we will give to you and we will protect you.]{.trans}  
    [نُعْطِكَ]{.ar} is a re-specifier of [نُحْسِنْ إِلَيْكَ]{.ar}.

(@ex001604) [وَمَن یَفۡعَلۡ ذَ ٰ⁠لِكَ **یَلۡقَ** أَثَامࣰا۝ **یُضَـٰعَفۡ** لَهُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ یَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِیَـٰمَةِ وَیَخۡلُدۡ فِیهِۦ مُهَانًا]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الفرقان]{.ar} 25:68–69](https://quran.com/25/68-69) cited by [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/87](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/940)]{.citex}  
    [And whoever should do that will meet a penalty. Multiplied for him is the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated]{.trans}  
    [يُضَاعَفْ]{.ar},
    in the ø-case,
    is analyzed as a re-specifier of [يَلْقَ]{.ar}.^[[[الجدول في إعراب القرآن لمحمود صافي]{.ar} for [سورة الفرقان]{.ar} 25:69](https://tafsir.app/aljadwal/25/69)]

### A condition-verb followed by a conjunction

If the condition-verb is followed by a conjunction
and then the second verb,
then the second is, by default, in the ø-case to match the condition-verb.
Examples:

(@ex001605) [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي **ثُمََّ تَسْأَلْنِي** أُعْطِكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/87](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/940)]{.citex}  
    [If you come to me, then you ask me, I will give to you.]{.trans}  

(@ex001606) [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي **فَتَسْأَلْنِي** أُعْطِكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/87](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/940)]{.citex}  
    [If you come to me, then you ask me, I will give to you.]{.trans}  

(@ex001607) [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي **وَتَسْأَلْنِي** أُعْطِكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/87](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/940)]{.citex}  
    [If you come to me, and you ask me, I will give to you.]{.trans}  

According to one view,^[[[المقتضب للمبرد]{.ar} 2/66](https://shamela.ws/book/6965/335) cited by [[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar}](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n405/mode/2up)]
the u-case is also permissible for the second verb
when the conjunction is with [وَ]{.ar}.
And this is because
its verbal sentence is considered a [HAl]{.trn2} with a preceding [و]{.ar} of [HAl]{.trn2}
and a following detached pronoun is deleted.
For example:

(@ex001608) [إِنْ تَأْتِنَا **وَتَسْأَلُنَا** نُعْطِكَ]{.ar}
    [[[المقتضب للمبرد]{.ar} 2/66](https://shamela.ws/book/6965/335) cited by [[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar}](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n405/mode/2up)]{.citex}  
    [If you come to us, while you are asking us, I will give to you.]{.trans}  
    The [taqdIr]{.trn2} is [إِنْ تَأْتِنَا **وَ[أَنْتَ]** تَسْأَلُنَا نُعْطِكَ]{.ar}.

When the conjunction is with [وَ]{.ar} or [فَ]{.ar},
then the 
a-case is also permissible for the second verb.
A [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed [أَنْ]{.ar} is implied before the second verb.^[[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/468]
Examples:

(@ex001609) [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي **فَتُحَدِّثَنِي** أُحَدِّثْكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/88](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/941)]{.citex}  
    [If you come to me, so [that] you talk to me, I will talk to you.]{.trans}  

(@ex001610) [إِنْ تَأْتِنِي **وَتُحَدِّثَنِي** أُحَدِّثْكَ]{.ar}
    [[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/88](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/941)]{.citex}  
    [If you come to me, and [that] you talk to me, I will talk to you.]{.trans}  

### A condition-response-verb followed by a conjunction

If the condition-response-verb is followed by a conjunction
and then the second verb,
then the second is, by default, in the ø-case to match the condition-response-verb.
For example:

(@ex001611) [مَنْ يَأْكُلْ كَثِيرًا يَتْخَمْ **وَيَمْرَضْ**]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/469]{.citex}  
    [Whoever eats a lot, he will suffer from indigestion and be sick.]{.trans}  

When the conjunction is with [وَ]{.ar} or [فَ]{.ar},
then the 
u-case is also permissible for the second verb,
with the analysis that a new sentence is beginning.
For example:

(@ex001612) [مَنْ يَأْكُلْ كَثِيرًا يَتْخَمْ **فَيَمْرَضُ**]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/470]{.citex}  
    [Whoever eats a lot, he will suffer from indigestion. Then he will be sick.]{.trans}  


When the conjunction is with [وَ]{.ar} or [فَ]{.ar},
then the 
a-case is also permissible for the second verb,
with the analysis that
a [taqdIr]{.trn2}ed [أَنْ]{.ar} is implied before the second verb.^[[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/469]

(@ex001613) [مَنْ يَأْكُلْ كَثِيرًا يَتْخَمْ **فَيَمْرَضَ**]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/469]{.citex}  
    [Whoever eats a lot, he will suffer from indigestion causing him to be sick.]{.trans}  

(@ex001614) [إِنْ تُكْرِمْ سَالِمًا أُكْرِمْكَ **وَأُسَاعِدَكَ**]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 2/469]{.citex}  
    [If you honor [#sAlim]{.trn2}, I will honor you and [at the same time] I will help you.]{.trans}  

When the condition-response itself begins with a [فَ]{.ar},
and the verb in the condition-response is followed by a conjunction and a second verb,
then we have two possibilities^[[[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/90](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/943) cited by [[الجملة الشرطية عند النحاة العرب للشمسان]{.ar} 410](https://archive.org/details/aljomla-ashrtia.g/page/n411/mode/2up)]:

1. The second verb is in the u-case. This is the default.
2. The second verb is in the ø-case, as a condition-response-verb to the original condition.

For example:

(@ex001615) [مَن یُضۡلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَلَا هَادِیَ لَهُۥۚ **وَیَذَرُهُمۡ** فِی طُغۡیَـٰنِهِمۡ یَعۡمَهُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الأعراف]{.ar} 7:186](https://quran.com/7/186) cited by [[كتاب سيبويه]{.ar} 3/90](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/943)]{.citex}  
    [Whoever Allāh sends astray - there is no guide for him. And He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly.]{.trans}  
    Some readings have [وَيَذَرْهُمْ]{.ar} in the ø-case.^[[[القراءات العشر من الشاطبية والدرة — دار الصحابة]{.ar} for [سورة الأعراف]{.ar} 7:186](https://tafsir.app/m-sahabah/7/186)]

## A conditional sentence interrupted by another conditional sentence

<!--
[النحو الوافي]{.ar} 4/489

Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 221ff

It is possible for a new conditional sentence to begin before an existing conditional sentence has completed.
Sometimes, this is straighforward, where the entire second conditional sentence
is the condition-response of the first conditional sentence.
For example:

(@ex001616) [إِنْ دَخَلْتَ فَإِنْ سَلَّمْتَ فَلَكَ كَذَا]{.ar}
    [Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 224 quoting [شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar}]{.citex}  
-->

It is possible for a new conditional sentence to begin before an existing conditional sentence has completed.

(@ex001617) [إِنْ رَكِبْتِ إِنْ لَبِسْتِ فَأنْتِ طَالِقٌ]{.ar}
    [Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 227 quoting [ابن هشام]{.ar}]{.citex}  
    [If you ride, if you wear your clothes, you are divorced.]{.trans}  

If only one of the conditions is fufilled then the divorce does not occur.
But the question is, would the divorce occur if she wore and then rode, or if she rode and then wore?
The grammarians have discussed such conditional sentences at length
and the view of the majority is that if the wife wore her clothes and then rode,
then
in this case she will be divorced.^[Al-Saad, _Conditional structure in Classical Arabic_ 230]
